courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.title: Zennovation in Sedation: Rethinking What is Possible
courses.description: In this educational presentation, we will discuss sedation in dogs. The foundation will be set by reviewing the basic physiology behind commonly used sedatives in dogs. We will discuss the most commonly used sedatives and reversal agents, and introduce the novel sedative Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan hydrochlorides).

courses.title: NC State Small Animal Abdominal Ultrasound Course
courses.description: The NC State Small Animal Abdominal Ultrasound Course provides lectures and hands-on laboratories for practitioners who wish to become more competent at abdominal ultrasonography in the small animal patient. It will provide a solid foundation in ultrasound physics, anatomy, and many case examples. In addition, this course allows hands-on experience for the practitioner.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Dentistry, Level 2
courses.description:
This class is available to DVMs who have completed one of the Introduction to Canine and Feline Dentistry and Oral Surgery classes. This 8-hour class will consist of 4 hours of lecture followed by 4 hours of hands-on wet lab. The topics discussed in lecture will include periodontal disease, dental fractures, an introduction to endodontic pathology, and common extraction complications.
The lab will include the basics of open and closed root planning, application of perioceutic products, odontoplasty with bonded sealants of uncomplicated crown fractures, difficult extractions, and surgical removal of root tips.
This class will be presented by Steven Honzelka, DVM, DAVDC.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Degenerative Lumbosacral Stenosis
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will examine the pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings of degenerative lumbosacral stenosis (DLSS) in canine patients. This course will also review and compare treatments including surgical decompression, epidural steroid injections, and medical management to optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: Mountain to Sea Veterinary Leadership Retreat - Greece
courses.description:
This eight session, hands-on leadership course empowers veterinary
professionals to delegate with intention, build trust, and develop leadership capacity within their teams. Many leaders struggle to let go of tasks and decisions due to fear, identity, or a lack of clear frameworks. The result is bottlenecks, burnout, and missed growth opportunities for the team. Across four days, participants will explore the emotional and strategic barriers to delegation, learn proven delegation and coaching models, and apply tools to foster a culture of accountability and ownership. Through real-time practice, feedback, and collaboration, attendees will leave with a customized action plan to confidently empower their teams.

courses.title: Surgical Management of Chylothorax
courses.description: The presentation will discuss the latest concepts in surgical management of canine and feline chylothorax with a focus on the important practical aspects of intraoperative decision-making and the latest data on outcomes.

courses.title: The future of proactive veterinary care
courses.description:
What would you do for every patient if you had unlimited time? Most vets have an instinctive answer and almost no way to act on it. This session is about the technology that's finally closing that gap. Digitail CEO Sebastian Gabor and Dr. Laila Proenca lay out a vision for AI in veterinary medicine. Not scribes and summaries, but a complete proactive intelligence layer that pulls together PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications to tell you in real time what every patient needs before they walk through the door. Anchored in fresh findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study and grounded in Dr. Proenca's own experience running this kind of system in her clinic, you'll see what proactive care actually looks like day-to-day: the conversations it enables, the cases it surfaces, and the membership and wellness models it makes possible for the first time.
Key Takeaways
- Understand how AI is evolving beyond documentation tools into proactive patient intelligence, and what that shift means for day-to-day clinic operations.
- Learn how integrating PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications can surface patient needs before the appointment begins.
- See real-world evidence from a practitioner already running a proactive care model, anchored in findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study.
- Discover how proactive AI infrastructure enables membership and wellness plan models that were previously too operationally complex to sustain.

courses.title: Women IN Surgery - Vet (WINS-Vet)
courses.description:
This two-day Women in Surgery (WINS) forum is designed to bring veterinary surgeons together to advance clinical expertise, strengthen professional resilience, and foster a supportive community within orthopedic surgery. Through a combination of expert-led lectures, case-based panel discussions, and hands-on laboratory training, participants will explore the principles and practical application of joint arthrodesis across the forelimb and hindlimb.
The program features focused sessions on carpal and tarsal arthrodesis, including tips, techniques, and decision-making strategies for procedures such as partial versus pancarpal arthrodesis. Attendees will engage in interactive panel discussions and case reviews that emphasize clinical reasoning, fixation selection, and postoperative management. Dedicated ArthroLab experiences provide the opportunity to apply these concepts in a hands-on setting using current plating systems and instrumentation.
In addition to technical training, the forum highlights professional development and peer collaboration through resident abstract presentations and facilitated group discussions. Topics include protecting surgical repairs, managing complex trauma cases, and cultivating strength and perspective in challenging clinical environments. The program culminates in collaborative case-sharing sessions, encouraging participants to exchange insights and build lasting professional connections.

courses.title: Self-Compassion for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description:
This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will focus on self-compassion. We are often our own worst critics, especially when we are passionate about our work. This can negatively impact our mood, mental health, and work performance. This program will provide tools and techniques to practice to protect our wellbeing, plus the reasoning behind why these methods work.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242038.)

courses.title: CANINE MASSAGE FUNDAMENTALS (1419-37823)
courses.description: Canine Massage is a valuable modality that veterinary professionals should add to their existing skill set to accompany the care provided by the veterinarian. Massage benefits dogs physically and emotionally, including reducing stress and anxiety as well as decreasing pain and discomfort as a result of age, illness, surgery, or injury. Massage can help improve outcomes by supporting the healing process, reducing healing time, and generally improving quality of life. Effective canine massage involves much more than applying massage techniques to the body. In addition to learning the techniques in this 3-day workshop, participants will learn the essential skills of palpation, which include understanding the basics of skeletal anatomy, proper body mechanics, and how to engage your "thinking fingers" in order to assess the dog's body. Participants will also learn how to use passive range of motion (PROM) as part of the assessment process. By the end of the workshop, participants will have gained the tools necessary to provide a dog with an effective and safe massage to promote relaxation and wellness. Prerequisites: Trust and Relationship-Building with Dogs (Parts 1 and 2), Canine Massage Fundamentals Part 1 (online), or instructor permission.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: 2026 AAVLD Annual Meeting Davis Thompson Foundation Pre-Meeting Workshop: Molecular Diagnostics for Pathologists
courses.description: Join us for the 2026 AAVLD-Davis Thompson Foundation Pre-Meeting Workshop where we will help you navigate the development, interpretation, strengths, and limitations of modern molecular tests. Our esteemed speakers are ready to guide you through a colorful array of fluorescent and stained slides, illuminate the dark shadows of next generation sequencing, and even help you reach peak amplification of your PCR expertise.

courses.title: Anesthetic Plans: A Practical Approach
courses.description: The lecture is 1 hour and focuses on how to design anesthesia protocols for everyday patients. The lecture covers everything from patient preparation to drug selection and maintenance.

courses.title: Emergency Ophthalmology
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review ophthalmic emergencies, including triage and presentation, patient history, exam, and ocular diagnostics. In addition, specific disease processes including ulcers, glaucoma, uveitis, and others will be presented.

courses.title: 28947 - ONE-DAY BAT REHABILITATION BASICS WORKSHOP (1131-35646)
courses.description: In this class, rehabilitatorparticipantss learn the basic skills that are essential to successfully rehabilitating orphaned and injured bats and returning them to their natural habitat. The class format is a combination of lecture, discussion, and hands-on activities designed to provide students with key information and experience.

courses.title: THRIVE: mental health, relationship management and career development
courses.description: This 7-day continuing education focused on mental health and professional development. Delegates will be resident for 7 days at a 5* safari lodge in the Victoria Falls National Park, Zimbabwe, Africa. Here you can be immersed in nature with the goal of stepping out of your normal environment and developing new mental health, self-awareness, and relationship skills that will benefit career satisfaction, growth, and longevity. This course mixes retreat-style relaxation and safari experiences, with immersive and interactive teaching. The course runs with a maximum of 16 people at a time, for an exclusive and tailored experience. What you will learn: - The Enneagram: typing your personality, understanding opposite personalities, and how to use this to develop team relationships - Conflict management and embracing differences - Intruder syndrome and how to combat it - Self-awareness. how to combat stress - Burnout: why it happens and how to prevent it - Self-forgiveness: Techniques to prevent self-blame and utilise perceived failure to develop your career - Emotional IQ ACCOMMODATION Delegates will enjoy their own luxury lodge room with king-size bed (shared rooms can be accommodated) with cool luxurious white linen, large sweeping mosquito nets, warm evening lighting and safari chic design. Rooms are ensuite with showers as well as outdoor showers to enjoy the African night sky. Each room has its own private deck overlooking the river. LOCATION The lodge is set in the Victoria Falls National Park, a big 5 wildlife area. You can expect to be serenaded with calls of the wild at breakfast and supper, elephants trumpeting and lions roaring into the night. In the evening, you can enjoy sunsets igniting the horizon and then kicking back around the fire, under a sky of stars.

courses.title: Radiology
courses.description: This interactive session will focus on the identification and interpretation of common thoracic and abdominal radiographic abnormalities through a case-based approach. Attendees will engage in the systematic review of representative cases, gaining practical insights into key disease processes and radiographic patterns.

courses.title: Integrative Neuromodulation: Basic Skills in Dry Needling and Photomedicine
courses.description: This immersive 3-day program covers the scientific foundations and clinical applications of dry needling and photomedicine for small animal patients. Through lectures, demonstrations, hands-on laboratories, clay modeling, palpation practice, movement assessment, neurologic localization exercises, and case-based discussions, participants will build practical skills for evaluating and supporting musculoskeletal, neurologic, chronic pain, and geriatric patients.

courses.description: PSIvet's two-day, in-person veterinary business symposium designed to educate veterinarians and veterinary staff to more effectively manage several aspects of the business of veterinary medicine, led by leading national experts and educators, for improved financial, business, and clinical outcomes of independent veterinary practices.
courses.location: Hyatt Regency St. Louis at The Arch

courses.title: Advanced Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Wet Lab
courses.description: This two-day course will discuss advanced oral and maxillofacial surgeries, with an emphasis on use of maxillofacial miniplates for repair of mandibular and maxillary fractures. Utilizing a mixture of lecture and wet lab, the event will provide 12 hours of education provided by a fellow of the AVDC Oral and Maxillofacial Fellowship. Participants will leave with an understanding of techniques and equipment needed for application of miniplates in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Lymphatic Massage - The Common Denominator
courses.description: In addition to mastering the fundamental massage techniques, every canine massage therapist and veterinary rehabilitation specialist should understand how to effectively use lymphatic massage protocols as they are an essential skill that can benefit dogs in any situation. In this advanced workshop, participants learn specific lymphatic massage techniques that can be used after deep tissue work to help clear metabolic wastes from the body; after surgery or injury to reduce swelling; and during palliative and hospice care to help sick and convalescing dogs by boosting the immune system and clearing out toxins, which when accumulated can cause nausea, fatigue, and pain. These techniques are gentle, nuanced, and effective, and the relaxation effects are profound. Lymphatic massage can truly be used in just about every situation and in every session with a dog, making it the common denominator in canine massage.

courses.title: Reptile Nutrition
courses.description: This presentation is a thorough review of reptile nutrition, including information on carnivores, omnivores, and herbivores. It will include limitations of commercially available invertebrate prey and how to improve their nutritional status through gut-loading and powder supplementation for commonly kept insectivores. Herbivore feeding strategies will be reviewed, including the nutritional content of common store-bought greens and correlating this to the natural feeding strategies of commonly kept herbivores. Different methods of water provision will be reviewed. This presentation will include a thorough literature review of the last 5 years.

courses.title: Situations That Challenge Us: Abuse, Neglect, and Limited Resources
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will review our legal and ethical obligations in instances of suspected cruelty, abuse, and neglect. This course will include related client communication strategies and reporting mandates, distinguish between neglect and lack of access to resources, and what to do with each type of challenging situation.

courses.title: Symposium on Therapeutic Advances in Animal Rehabilitation (STAAR)
courses.description: STAAR Conference for veterinarians and animal rehabilitation professionals aims to bring to you the most advanced courses in rehabilitation, sports medicine, and fitness taught by industry leaders and pioneers. Wet labs are intensive and designed for the serious veterinary practitioner. Our unique method of education focuses on hands-on, practical experience using live equines. Wet labs include approximately 1 horse per every 3-4 participants so that learned skills and techniques can be directly and immediately implemented into practice. Classes are intimate, informal, and small to maximize learning (maximum 15 participants/class). STAAR brings its signature hands-on practical model to equine education and integrates many professions involved in comprehensive equine care.

courses.title: Mastering Pelvic and Femur Traumatology
courses.description:
Participants will take a deep dive into complex trauma cases, including sacroiliac (SI) luxation, hip luxation, and complex fractures of the femur and pelvis. Refine techniques in fluoroscopy-guided procedures in the state-of-the-art ArthroLab, equipped with multiple C-arms to support and maximize hands-on learning in a realistic surgical environment.
Master percutaneous repairs using fluoroscopy: Optimize positioning and improve accuracy with guided pin placement to simplify approaches to SI injuries, capital physeal and femoral neck fractures. Reduce surgical time with real-time imaging strategies.
The wet labs will also cover:
- Surgical Hip arthroscopy and arthroscopic hip luxation stabilizations
- Minimally invasive hip joint exploration using Nanoneedle technology
- Open surgical approaches to master repairs using the newest canine-specific anatomical plates designed for pelvic and femur fractures, enhancing surgical precision and confidence.
As part of the immersive format, participants will engage in:
-Live surgical demonstrations
-Case-based discussions
-Collaborative problem-solving with peers and faculty
During interactive case presentation sessions, attendees are encouraged to bring their own cases to explore different scenarios and discover innovative solutions.

courses.title: Canine Respiratory Emergencies
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review recognition and stabilization of patients presenting in respiratory distress. This course will also include point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) diagnostics with a focus on lung ultrasound, plus diagnostic interpretation and interventional strategies for critically ill patients.

courses.title: Updates on Plasma Cell Pododermatitis and ICGN
courses.description: This session will share recent research regarding the clinical presentation of plasma cell pododermatitis (PCP) and associated immune complex mediated glomerular nephritis (ICGN) in cats, an uncommon but serious condition traditionally associated with a poor prognosis. Familiarity with these disease processes and their potential association may facilitate earlier diagnosis and improve outcomes for young cats affected by these conditions.

courses.provider: TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY OFFICE OF VETERINARY CONTINUING EDUCATION
courses.title: 2026 Vet-KU - Texas A&M Internal Medicine Conference: Endocrinology
courses.description: This 25-hour program will provide attendees with current practically relevant information on small animal endocrinology. To this end, several sessions will outline a logical diagnostic approach to challenging but common problems, such as polyuria/polydipsia, while others will help attendees formulate better treatment plans for common but challenging conditions, such as diabetes mellitus. The program will cover a wide range of important disease entities including diabetes mellitus in cats and dogs, canine hypercortisolism, canine hypoadrenocorticism, hypothyroidism in dogs and cats, hyperthyroidism in cats, and endocrine neoplasia. Special emphasis will be paid to major new developments in the treatment of diabetes mellitus. The final hour of each day will be an interactive session, covering complex and controversial topics. The 4 speakers are all recognized experts in this field: Andrew Bugbee (Texas A&M University), Sean Hulsebosch (University of California Davis), Daniel Langlois (Michigan State University), Jocelyn Mott (University of Florida).

courses.title: Gonadectomy in Dogs- Pros and Cons
courses.description: This program will discuss the pros and cons of gonadectomy in dogs.The surgeon will review sterilization options for female and male dogs and the literature on gonadectomy(primarily focusing on decreased risk of oncologic and orthopedic conditions when remaining hormonally intact) and will review how to pick a surgical option for your specific patient.

courses.title: Tough Pain Problems Symposium
courses.description: A symposium geared to strengthen pain assessments, diversify treatment options, and improve clinical outcomes with evidence-based integrative medicine and rehabilitation. We have leading researchers and clinicians present research and discuss scientific, integrative medicine and rehabilitation approaches for short- and long-term pain problems in veterinary patients large and small. We promote evidence-based, safe, and restorative treatment options for animals in pain.

courses.title: Osteopathic Medical Massage for Small Animals Certification (CVMM)
courses.description: The 2026 Medical Massage program includes instructional videos, hands-on coursework at home and onsite, expanded sections on anatomy, myofascial dysfunction, osteopathic and Swedish massage techniques, and the neurophysiology of soft tissue manual therapy. Certification for veterinarians is based on the successful completion of online modules, hands-on practice at home, the in-person Clinical Intensive, and a case report documenting the clinical implementation of medical massage.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. courses.title: Surgical Extractions in Canines and Felines
courses.description: This 9 hour course will be 2.5 hours of interactive lecture and 6.5 hours of hands-on laboratory. The lecture will cover the indications for surgical extractions in both cats and dogs and the appropriate surgical techniques for exodontia. Each participant will be working at their own stations with their specimens, equipment and instrumentations at specially designed dental training tables. Specific teeth in both Canines and Felines will be assigned to practice surgical exodontia. This will involve making the appropriate muco-gingival flaps, bone reduction and teeth elevation techniques. Utilizing videography, the procedures for each tooth will be illustrated throughout the laboratory portion.

courses.title: External Coaptation Principles: Casting and Splinting 101
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will be presented as a hands-on lab focusing on splinting and casting techniques for fracture stabilization. This course will include indications for external coaptation, proper application methods, and complication prevention strategies to optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: Connecting with Empathy to Clients Under Stress
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will review how to have difficult conversations with pet families in crisis to communicate information. This course provides guidance regarding the neurological implications of stress and strategies for the best way to communicate.

courses.title: Chronic Canine Respiratory Diseases
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review signalment, clinical signs, diagnostics, and treatment of the most common canine chronic respiratory diseases that can lead to respiratory emergencies and pulmonary hypertension.

courses.title: CORA Based Leveling Osteotomy (CBLO)
courses.description:
CORA based leveling osteotomy (CBLO) is a unique procedure that modifies the tibial
plateau angle in order to prevent cranial translation (cranial drawer) and tibial thrust in the cranial cruciate deficient
stifle. Advantages of the technique include ease of the osteotomy, non-articular osteotomy, and rapid healing of the
osteotomy. Rapid healing and early return to function are the result of complete bone contact along the surface of
the osteotomy and ability to apply compression at the osteotomy. Numerous advantages of the technique have been
identified and will be presented in lecture format. In vitro and in vivo outcome studies will be presented as well as
complications and their management.

courses.title: ADVANCED SKILLS BAT REHABILITATION WORKSHOP (1131-35648)
courses.description: In this one-day class, participants learn how to manage more complex cases, including long-term care, closed fracture stabilization, open fracture reduction and repair, wound care, anesthesia, and pain management.

courses.title: Internal Medicine in Real Life: Practical Strategies for Your Toughest Chronic Cases
courses.description:
Internal Medicine in Real Life: Practical Strategies for Your Toughest Chronic Cases
This three-part CE series is designed for general practitioners who want practical, confidence-building approaches to liver disease, hyperadrenocorticism, and chronic kidney disease. Across three interactive 2-hour sessions, you'll learn how to diagnose these conditions efficiently, avoid common mistakes, and implement treatment strategies that actually move the needle for your patients
Session 1- Demystifying Liver Disease in Dogs and Cats
Confused about feline cholangiohepatitis? Unsure how aggressively to pursue diagnostics in the icteric cat? Curious how to apply ACVIM guidelines to canine chronic hepatitis? This session breaks down the most common hepatopathies you see in practice - clearly, simply, and practically. Learn streamlined diagnostic pathways, treatment strategies that make a difference, and case-based pearls that demystify these often frustrating conditions.
Session 2 - Is This Cushing's and Do I Care?
Cushing's is one of the most confusing and sometimes frustrating diseases in veterinary medicine. This session gives you a practical, evidence-based roadmap for when to test, how to test, and - most importantly - when to treat. We'll tackle the gray areas, the unexpected complications, the borderline test results, and the realistic conversations you need to have with clients to keep expectations aligned with outcomes.
Session 3-Chronic Kidney Disease: Moving the Needle
CKD is one of the most common - and manageable - conditions in older cats and dogs. This session focuses on early recognition, IRIS-guided treatment, and practical strategies that improve longevity and quality of life. Learn how to identify progression earlier, manage complications proactively, and use nutritional therapy as a powerful tool in slowing disease progression.

courses.title: Medical and Surgical Management of Otitis Media in Rabbits
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review the diagnosis and treatment of otitis media in rabbits. This course will cover how to identify clinical signs, apply advanced imaging techniques, and surgical management approaches to optimize patient outcomes in exotic practice.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: V.I.P. Veterinary Introductory Pathology- A System-Based Review
courses.description: This monthly webinar series will present a systems-based introduction to veterinary histopathology. Each month, a different body system (Integument, Urinary, Reproductive, Cardiovascular, Endocrine, Pulmonary, Musculoskeletal, Digestive, Hemolymphatic, Nervous, and Special Senses [Eye and Ear]) will be introduced in a way that participants of any level of experience (veterinary students, interns, residents and/or anatomic pathologists) will be able to comprehend and further expand their knowledge of veterinary pathology. Each webinar will introduce the normal tissue architecture, histological features of each anatomic structure and highlight the response to injury of different tissues and cell types found within each system. Cumulatively, by the end of the series, participants will have learned about the embryologic development, structure, function, and response to injury of twelve body systems - As well as received an introduction to some species specific variations of different systemic components. Additionally, these webinars will introduce unique patterns and types of injury that are seen in certain organ systems (such as patterns of pneumonia and zonal patterns of hepatocyte injury). courses.title: Does Another One Really Have to Bite the Dust
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will be presented as a hands on lab highlighting how outdated habits, team communication gaps, and drug protocol missteps can turn a survivable code into a tragedy. Participants wont just review the latest reassessment campaign on veterinary resuscitation initiative updates, they will perform them on canine and feline manikins to build the muscle memory and confidence needed to deliver high quality chest compressions, master the single dose atropine rule, and run a coordinated code. This course will provide the skills to give patients the best possible shot at the return of spontaneous circulation.

courses.title: Cant Walk or Wont Walk
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review common presentations of mixed orthopedic and neurologic conditions, in addition to awkward metabolic systemic disorders. This course will also highlight front limb and rear limb examination findings plus treatments options for non-ambulatory patients.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: 2026 ACVP/Davis-Thompson Foundation Pre-Meeting Workshop - Pathology of the Respiratory System
courses.description:
Course Description: Pathology of the respiratory system, especially of the interstitial lung diseases, creates considerable difficulty for diagnostic pathologists due to the complexity of lesions, overlapping histologic features of the many conditions that affect the respiratory tract, and development of new knowledge of these diseases. Our speakers will present a workshop based on their extensive experience in respiratory pathology which include authorship of book chapters and scholarly articles on respiratory diseases.
This meeting is suitable for veterinary students, interns, residents, graduate students and anatomic pathologists. The workshop will be organized into presentations and case-based interactive discussion with digital microscopy files available to registrants prior to the meeting. The presentations will focus on the diagnostic approach to diseases of the respiratory tract of domestic mammals.
Course Objectives: At the end of this workshop, participants will have the ability to outline the approach to and identify normal anatomy of the lung in domestic species, identify patterns of lung disease, and define the terminology associated with pulmonary pathology. Participants will also be introduced to mechanisms of disease in specific interstitial lung diseases and recognize/diagnose interstitial lung diseases specific to small and large animal species.
Attendees will review the anatomy of the respiratory system and to the patterns of diseases affecting the respiratory system. Focusing on interstitial lung diseases, they will develop insights into the diverse morphologic patterns of interstitial lung diseases, and differences in their pathogenesis and cause, followed by a review of specific interstitial lung diseases affecting companion and food-producing domestic mammals. Finally, there will be an interactive case-based discussion with digital microscopy files available to registrants prior to the workshop. These case-based discussions will be used to ill

courses.title: Ophthalmic Surgery
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will be presented as a lecture plus hands-on lab focusing on ophthalmic surgery for eyelid mass removal, laceration repair, entropion correction, and pocket imbrication for cherry eye. This course will include a review of surgical indications for these conditions, pre-operative testing, client communication strategies in preparation for the procedures, plus post-operative recommended care. The hands-on lab portion will feature step-by-step demonstrations on porcine cadaver eyes with eyelids for participants to practice surgical techniques. In addition, live patient surgical videos will be featured.

courses.title: THRIVE: mental health, relationship management and career development
courses.description: This 7-day continuing education focused on mental health and professional development. Delegates will be resident for 7 days at a 5* safari lodge in the Victoria Falls National Park, Zimbabwe, Africa. Here you can be immersed in nature with the goal of stepping out of your normal environment and developing new mental health, self-awareness, and relationship skills that will benefit career satisfaction, growth, and longevity. This course mixes retreat-style relaxation and safari experiences, with immersive and interactive teaching. The course runs with a maximum of 16 people at a time, for an exclusive and tailored experience. What you will learn: - The Enneagram: typing your personality, understanding opposite personalities, and how to use this to develop team relationships - Conflict management and embracing differences - Intruder syndrome and how to combat it - Self-awareness. how to combat stress - Burnout: why it happens and how to prevent it - Self-forgiveness: Techniques to prevent self-blame and utilise perceived failure to develop your career - Emotional IQ ACCOMMODATION Delegates will enjoy their own luxury lodge room with king-size bed (shared rooms can be accommodated) with cool luxurious white linen, large sweeping mosquito nets, warm evening lighting and safari chic design. Rooms are ensuite with showers as well as outdoor showers to enjoy the African night sky. Each room has its own private deck overlooking the river. LOCATION The lodge is set in the Victoria Falls National Park, a big 5 wildlife area. You can expect to be serenaded with calls of the wild at breakfast and supper, elephants trumpeting and lions roaring into the night. In the evening, you can enjoy sunsets igniting the horizon and then kicking back around the fire, under a sky of stars.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Pulmonary Hypertension: What Is It and Where Does It Come From
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review the pathophysiology, clinical signs, diagnosis, and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. This course will also include case-based examples to distinguish between pulmonary disease with hypertension and cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

courses.title: Cracking the Cruciate Code: From Diagnosis to Treatment
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will provide an overview of the anatomy and pathophysiology of the cranial cruciate ligament plus feature physical exam findings associated with complete and partial tears. In addition to highlighting key points for client education, this course will review diagnostic approaches, radiographic interpretations, technique tips for extracapsular repairs, plus treatment options for cruciate ligament disease.

courses.title: The future of proactive veterinary care
courses.description:
What would you do for every patient if you had unlimited time? Most vets have an instinctive answer and almost no way to act on it. This session is about the technology that's finally closing that gap. Digitail CEO Sebastian Gabor and Dr. Laila Proenca lay out a vision for AI in veterinary medicine. Not scribes and summaries, but a complete proactive intelligence layer that pulls together PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications to tell you in real time what every patient needs before they walk through the door. Anchored in fresh findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study and grounded in Dr. Proenca's own experience running this kind of system in her clinic, you'll see what proactive care actually looks like day-to-day: the conversations it enables, the cases it surfaces, and the membership and wellness models it makes possible for the first time.
Key Takeaways
- Understand how AI is evolving beyond documentation tools into proactive patient intelligence, and what that shift means for day-to-day clinic operations.
- Learn how integrating PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications can surface patient needs before the appointment begins.
- See real-world evidence from a practitioner already running a proactive care model, anchored in findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study.
- Discover how proactive AI infrastructure enables membership and wellness plan models that were previously too operationally complex to sustain.

courses.title: Gonadectomy in Dogs- Pros and Cons
courses.description: This program will discuss the pros and cons of gonadectomy in dogs.The surgeon will review sterilization options for female and male dogs and the literature on gonadectomy(primarily focusing on decreased risk of oncologic and orthopedic conditions when remaining hormonally intact) and will review how to pick a surgical option for your specific patient.

courses.title: Good Grief
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will provide an overview on grief theories and how they can be applied at various stages of the veterinary care process. In addition, this program will review specific strategies to use when working with clients through their grief process. (This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1184250.)

courses.title: Lower Back Pain and Conservative Management of Lumbosacral Disease
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review the diagnosis and conservative management of lower back pain and lumbosacral disease in canine patients. This course will include common etiologies, physical examination techniques for differentiating spinal from orthopedic pain, and the role of biomechanics in spinal compression.

courses.title: Equine Massage Certification
courses.description: Therasage Equine Massage provides a highly educational opportunity for students to broaden their knowledge of equine massage, develop business skills that lead to a promising career path, and earn certification in Equine Massage to be able to gain employment.

courses.title: Flexible Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
courses.description: This two-day introductory GI endoscopy course will include 7 hours of lectures covering indications, basic technique, and disorders diagnosed via endoscopy and a total of 9 hours of laboratory time for key hands-on experience. Day one laboratory will use GI models and fresh cadavers to learn basic endoscopic manipulation, biopsy techniques, foreign body removal, and PEG tube placement. Day two laboratory will involve live dogs performing basic upper GI endoscopy to perfect manipulation skills. Bring your technician; they can attend lectures and individual training on endoscopic instrumentation and set up, biopsy management and assist during the laboratory.

courses.title: Nutrition and Stem Cell Therapy in Dogs and Cats: Optimizing for Better Outcomes
courses.description: Stem cell therapy is an exciting part of regenerative veterinary medicine, but the patient's nutritional and metabolic state may influence how well these therapies perform. This webinar reviews the biologic links between nutrition, inflammation, microbiome function, and stem cell behavior, with a practical focus on dogs and cats. Participants will learn how veterinary teams can help support the patient's biological environment before, during, and after regenerative treatment, while exploring where the scientific evidence is well established and where it continues to emerge.

courses.title: The Cat Friendly Experience: From Meet to Treat
courses.description:
Despite overall declines in U.S. veterinary visits, feline care continues to grow, with rising cat adoptions and increasing clinical visits. Yet cats remain one of the most underserved patient populations, often due to the stress and anxiety associated with veterinary visits. This webinar presents a practical, evidence-based approach to improving both the feline exam experience and caregiver satisfaction through the principles of Cat Friendly Practice. Attendees will gain insight into the physiologic and emotional effects of stress in cats, the influence of the clinical environment on behavior, and how caregiver perception impacts compliance.
With a focus on creating a feline friendly clinic environment, adopting feline-specific handling techniques, and navigating the expanding options of products licensed for cats, this session equips veterinary professionals to reduce fear, improve diagnostic accuracy, and foster stronger client relationships. The result is a calmer, more compassionate approach to feline care that supports increased visits, better preventive medicine, and earlier disease detection

courses.title: Grain of Truth: Sorting Facts from Fables in Pet Nutrition
courses.description:
This course addresses prevalent nutrition myths affecting veterinary practice and clinical
dietary recommendations. Veterinarians will learn evidence-based clarifications to common misconceptions about
pet food ingredients, formulation principles, and nutritional adequacy. Topics include digestibility myths, protein
requirements, ingredient quality (by-products, grains, legumes, oils), human-grade standards, supplement necessity,
raw feeding claims, weight management strategies, and a clearer understanding of the different nutrition
credentials.

courses.title: A Fresh Perspective: a discussion on feeding fresh
courses.description: This course provides veterinary professionals with a balanced, evidence based look at fresh pet food diets compared to fresh homemade and traditional dry food. Topics include a review of pet food safety; effective strategies for navigating popular nutrition trends; the practical benefits of fresh feeding; and key considerations for tailoring to a patient's needs. Attendees will leave equipped to objectively counsel clients on fresh versus dry feeding options.

courses.title: Is Osteoarthritis a Disease of Young Dogs? Rethinking Risk Across All Life Stages
courses.description:
Osteoarthritis is often framed as a condition of older dogs - but the evidence challenges that assumption. Nearly 40% of dogs across all ages, breeds, and body weights show signs of OA pain, yet fewer than half are ever diagnosed and only a third are treated.
Emerging data from dogs as young as 8 months, combined with what we know about the unique genetic history of domestic breeds, reveals that OA risk begins far earlier than most practitioners expect.
This session examines the biological and epidemiological evidence supporting OA as a disease of all life stages, reviews the pain physiology driving clinical signs, and applies key concepts through a real-world case study. Attendees will leave with a practical screening framework to identify, assess, and address OA pain across every canine patient in their practice.

courses.title: When less is more: Is once-daily insulin possible in diabetic dogs?
courses.description: This webinar unites the patient, the pet owner, and the healthcare team to achieve the best possible outcomes in managing the many changes associated with diabetes mellitus. At the center are once-daily treatment options that simplifies care for most pets. In this talk, attendees will learn how a once-daily insulin protocol can be a practical reality for most diabetic dogs using case examples to show how to successfully start, regulate, and maintain patients to optimize patient and owner quality of life.

courses.title: Equine Upper Airway Symposium
courses.description: This three-and-a-half-day symposium offers lectures and wet labs designed to present in-depth, current scientific information regarding pathophysiology, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis for upper airway (UA) conditions in the horse. The target participants for the meeting are veterinarians in resident training programs and clinicians who have not had the desired exposure to UA conditions in the horse.

courses.title: Dental Radiograph Positioning Training
courses.description: Dental Radiography Positioning Training will provide hands on training for veterinarians and technicians on proper radiograph acquisition technique, and the operation of and care for their equipment.

courses.provider: UNIVERSITY OF DENVER, DANIELS COLLEGE OF BUSINESS
courses.title: VMG 1.0 Leadership Academy
courses.description: VMG 1.0 Leadership Academy is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: VET Expo 2026, Sydney
courses.description: The VET Expo is Australia largest veterinary event with close over 1000 registered attendees, 120 speakers, and 100 exhibitors. Vet Expo compared to traditional style conferences, is faster paced with 20 or 60 minute presentations with innovative sessions including technical demos and a pitch fest and is free to attend. The event is specifically designed for the whole veterinarian profession including vet specialists, general practices, vet nurses, practice managers, clinic owners, technicians, researchers, government, and other animal health professionals. Speakers are from a wide range of backgrounds include vets, vet nurses, academics and researchers, animal behaviorist's, animal welfare professionals, and practice managers.

courses.title: CVM Conference November 2026
courses.description: The CVM Conference will offer attendees the chance to earn 20 CE hours from over 130 sessions, over many topics such as radiology, toxicology, ophthalmology, field medicine, equine and bovine sessions, and other professional topics as well.

courses.title: UNIVERSAL HIP WORKSHOP (407-36907)
courses.description: Developed in cooperation with experienced industry-leading surgeons, this two-day workshop consists of a comprehensive online educational component, supplemental classroom instruction, and extensive hands-on laboratory experience. This multi-faceted approach to education is designed to offer participants the necessary resources and support to sufficiently familiarize themselves with the procedure, and reliably offer an advanced orthopedic service to their clientele. Participants will learn proper technique for use of the Universal Hip system, focusing on preoperative planning, surgical technique, and clinical follow-up, with opportunity to use the instruments to gain an understanding of the surgical objectives.

courses.title: Veterinary Abdominal Ultrasound Training Camp
courses.description: This hands-on, small-group veterinary abdominal ultrasound training program is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians of all skill levels, from beginners to advanced practitioners. Participants will gain practical experience performing diagnostic-quality abdominal ultrasounds using a structured, protocol-based approach. Over three immersive days, attendees will master core organ imaging, systematic scanning workflows, and advanced techniques for the liver, pancreas, adrenal glands, and gastrointestinal tract. The program includes interactive lectures, live-patient scanning labs, and 30 days of personalized feedback through mentored teleradiology, ensuring participants leave with confidence, improved efficiency, and skills that translate directly to clinical practice. This course emphasizes hands-on learning, real-world applications, and long-term clinical success.
courses.location: COVE - The Center of Veterinary Excellence

courses.provider: SUSTAINABILITY IN EQUINE PRACTICE SEMINAR AND RETREAT
courses.title: The Sustainability In Equine Practice Seminar 2026
courses.description:
The Sustainability in Equine Practice Seminar & Retreat 2026 is a 2.5-day continuing education program designed specifically for equine veterinarians seeking practical strategies to build sustainable, successful, and fulfilling careers in equine practice. Hosted jointly by Sustainability in Equine Practice Seminars (SEPS) and Decade One, this retreat-style meeting combines business education, leadership development, wellness, communication skills, legal and financial guidance, and community connection in an immersive learning environment.
This program addresses many of the non-clinical challenges that directly impact career longevity, professional satisfaction, and practice sustainability within equine veterinary medicine. Through lecture-based presentations, facilitated discussions, and interactive learning opportunities, participants will gain actionable tools to improve personal well-being, strengthen leadership and communication skills, enhance financial literacy, increase practice profitability, navigate legal and ethical issues, and foster healthier workplace and client relationships.

courses.title: Pain Pathways and Analgesia (TECH435)
courses.description: Discover the art and science of pain management in both companion and large animals in this comprehensive course. This journey will take you from the basics of pain terminology to advanced, real-world understanding of how pain works in the body and how to treat it effectively. Instead of simply memorizing drug lists, you'll learn why each medication works by exploring pain pathways and receptor-level pharmacology in an engaging, easy-to-understand way. You'll gain practical insight into how different analgesic drugs work together to provide safer, more effective pain control and better patient outcomes.

courses.title: VOM Hands On Short Course
courses.description: Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation (VOM) is an instrument-based animal adjusting course that is precise and effective at rebalancing neurovascular imbalances to enhance healing and performance.

courses.title: Rhinebeck Equine Clinical Perspectives in Equine Practice
courses.description:
This continuing education program provides clinically relevant updates for equine practitioners. The program features nine 50-minute lectures delivered by specialists and experienced equine veterinarians who previously completed internships at Rhinebeck Equine. The event is part of the Rhinebeck Equine Internship Program 20th Anniversary celebration and alumni reunion. Presenters represent alumni of the Rhinebeck Equine internship program who have returned to share clinical updates and perspectives with regional practitioners.
This continuing education program is hosted by Rhinebeck Equine and provided by Cavalcade Management Group, an AAVSB RACE-approved continuing education provider.
The target audience is licensed veterinarians involved in equine clinical practice, including general practitioners and equine specialists. The program may also be of interest to veterinary interns, residents, and technicians.

courses.title: IACUC 101 PLUS
courses.description: IACUC 101 PLUS program is two six-hour days of didactic and interactive educational opportunities for both new and seasoned IACUC members, IACUC affiliates and others who contribute to their institution's animal care and use program. The "Plus" portion of this 2-day program includes additional Occupational Health and Safety, Wildlife and Post Approval Monitoring modules, as well as updates from USDA and OLAW. Didactic sessions address institutional responsibilities, IACUC charges, relevant informational resources, animal welfare laws, regulations and policies, and best practices. Students also are challenged to consider, deliberate, and develop action plans for a variety of potential IACUC scenarios. The course includes Q&A sessions with representatives from USDA and OLAW. This highly interactive, advanced program provides multiple opportunities to engage in real life applications of the basic concepts with the goals of learning new approaches and gaining new perspectives for managing issues that many animal care and use programs face.

courses.title: Postural Rehabilitation Professional
courses.description: Postural Rehabilitation Professional is a 6 week, high contact program designed to teach equine professionals how to evaluate and remediate equine abnormal compensatory posture (ACP). Participants will learn about how standing posture is generated and controlled by the CNS, the peripheral structures critical to posture that tend to become distorted by domestication, how to recognize and remediate abnormal anatomic structures (distal limb/hoof, stomatognathic system) and function of the cervical spine to restore normal neutral posture to equine patients. We will also teach team-building among equine professionals, professional communications and how to apply injury forensics to chronic cases.

courses.title: Oncology and Emergency Critical Care with Brianna Keller and Katie Osekavage
courses.description: Earn Veterinary Continuing Education on Oncology and Emergency Critical Care
courses.location: Bar Harbor Maine Acadia National Park

courses.title: Feed Real Summit 2026
courses.description:
Discover Practical Paths To Dog Longevity
Food is the basis of wellness, but even the best diet can be outdone by toxic chemicals found in everyday dog products, including shampoos, bedding, flea and tick topicals, and supplements. FRS26 is designed to provide 2.0 dog parents, veterinary professionals, and other canine professionals, including aspiring wellness coaches, trainers, and groomers, with practical and actionable tips for promoting dog longevity.
Speaker presentations, workshops, and the panel discussion will cover the following topics: The Basics of Ayurveda for Canine Longevity, Vaccines and Titers, Entangled Presence: Healing, Connection, and Longevity, Silver Muzzles, Golden Hearts: Understanding Your Aging Dog, Pets and Their Light Environments: Why Light is the Foundation to Health, Stem Cells as Secret Agents, DIY Fresh Food: Save Money and Make Your Dog's Food at Home, Mushroom Treats for Dogs: Sneaking Nutrition into Every Bite, Creating Herbal Tinctures and Infusions, and The Future of Canine Wellness Beyond the Veterinary Clinic.

courses.title: 2026 Advanced Equine Endocrinology
courses.description: Equine endocrinology is rapidly evolving, with new discoveries shaping how we diagnose and manage diseases. This 2-day ACE course offers an advanced, evidence-based update on endocrine disorders in equids from the neonatal to geriatric periods. Topics include nutrition, pharmacologic therapies, and both emergent and long-term management strategies. Interactive Q&A panels with leading experts will ensure participants leave with practical tools they can apply immediately in clinical practice.

courses.title: EXTRACAPSULAR (EXCAP) LATERAL FABELLO-TIBIAL SUTURE STABILIZATION OF THE STIFLE: WET LAB (195-41366)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn/refine the extracapsular (ExCap) lateral fabello-tibial suture stabilization technique and to understand the major advantages of PowerX Crimping System. Participants will perform the ExCap suture stabilization technique on canine cadavers under faculty supervision using a step-by-step high-resolution video demonstration. This laboratory will include arthrotomy for stifle exploration, removal of the CrCL remnants, inspection of the medial meniscus, proper placement of the ExCap suture and use of a precise crimping system and critique of your repair.

courses.title: COMPREHENSIVE BOVINE EMBRYO TRANSFER TRAINING COURSE (1484-39132)
courses.description: The 5-day Comprehensive Embryo Transfer Training Course teaches the student: superovulation techniques, estrous synchronization methods, collection, recognition, manipulation, classification, freezing, thawing and transfer of bovine embryos.
courses.location: International Embryo Technology School Training Facility

courses.title: Advanced Oral Techniques for the Horse
courses.description: The Advanced Oral Techniques for the Horse course is designed for a practitioner at any career level. This course will contain the vital information needed to successfully perform equine dentistry. It will cover pertinent anatomy of the teeth and oral cavity, regional anesthesia, radiography, sinus anatomy and straightforward extractions of the incisors.

courses.title: Navigating the World of Pet Supplements: Evidence, Safety, and Recommendations
courses.description: This course provides veterinarians and veterinary technicians with evidence-based guidance on pet supplement regulation, quality assessment, and clinical recommendations. The presentation addresses the unclear regulatory landscape involved with supplement manufacturing, production, and marketing. Veterinarians will learn to identify high-quality supplements through label evaluation, third-party testing indicators, and manufacturing standards while recognizing regulatory and marketing red flags. The course covers common supplement categories including skin and coat support, gastrointestinal health, allergy and immune support, hip and joint products, and multivitamins, with emphasis on evidence-supported ingredients and appropriate dosing. Trending ingredients are examined such as algae oil, fibers, biotics, CBD, and herbs, with critical review of peer-reviewed evidence, contraindications, and clinical applications. A clinical framework guides supplement selection based on therapeutic goals, patient safety, drug interactions, and realistic expectations for outcomes.
