courses.description: Playing the numbers game: Gaining confidence with interpretation of the serum biochemical profile. This course offers veterinarians a unique perspective on chemistry case interpretation from both an internist and a clinical pathologist teaching in tandem. Participants will gain confidence interpreting abnormalities of the serum biochemical profile using real life cases focusing on dogs and cats.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: IVECCS 2026 - Savannah, GA
courses.description: IVECCS 2026 will be held in person in Savannah, GA from September 14-17th. Through state-of-the-art education and collaborative learning opportunities, VECCS continues its mission of advancing the standards of care for critically ill and emergent large and small animal patients. The comprehensive scientific program is designed to meet the needs of attendees across all levels of experience and areas of interest. Educational sessions will be tailored for veterinarians, veterinary specialists, veterinary technicians and nurses, veterinary technician specialists, support staff, and practice or hospital managers with an interest in small and large animal emergency, critical care, and specialty medicine. Lecture-based sessions will cover a wide range of topics, including emergency medicine, surgery, critical care, anesthesia and analgesia, gastrointestinal and hepatic disease, renal care, urgent care, ICU management, and leadership development. In addition to lectures, hands-on workshops and small-group forums will provide practical training in advanced monitoring and surgical techniques, RECOVER CPR, VetATLS, POCUS, physical medicine modalities, and communication skills. These interactive educational experiences are designed to equip attendees with both the clinical knowledge and practical skills necessary to enhance patient care and outcomes in veterinary emergency and critical care settings.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR PUBLIC VETERINARY MEDICINE (CPVM), VAMD COLLEGE OF VET
courses.title: Virtual Veterinary Career Transition Workshop - Industry Focus
courses.description: This veterinary career transition workshop, hosted by the Center for Public Veterinary Medicine with the Virginia-Maryland College of Veterinary Medicine, is designed to help veterinarians understand the breadth of opportunities in veterinary medicine, and how to create a new career path. This online workshop includes information on career opportunities in public veterinary practice, with a particular emphasis on careers in industry. Topics covered also include career and self-assessment, resume building, professional networking, job searching, and other key career transition issues. It is conducted with a format of short lectures, individual and group activities, group discussions, and expert panels. While the program emphasizes career opportunities within industry, it also addresses key aspects of federal, state, and alternative career paths. Invited speakers include federal and state veterinarians, corporate and industry veterinarians, and more.

courses.title: COMPREHENSIVE BOVINE EMBRYO TRANSFER TRAINING COURSE (1484-39132)
courses.description: The 5-day Comprehensive Embryo Transfer Training Course teaches the student: superovulation techniques, estrous synchronization methods, collection, recognition, manipulation, classification, freezing, thawing and transfer of bovine embryos.
courses.location: International Embryo Technology School Training Facility

courses.title: EQ1200: Equine CranioSacral Therapy - Level 1
courses.description: This 5-day class will train students in the theory, concepts and practice of Craniosacral Therapy as it pertains to the equine population, while giving them the opportunity to integrate this knowledge with the Nervous System and Fascial System. This course is designed to teach participants the skills involved in evaluating and helping neuromusculoskeletal/fascial dysfunction in horses.

courses.title: Unleashing Progress: Taming Perfectionism in Vet Med (STAF205)
courses.description:
Perfectionism can feel like a strength in veterinary medicine. Our patients rely on us, and our clients trust us. But when "never making a mistake" becomes your personal standard, the pressure can be overwhelming. Over time, perfectionism can drain your energy, increase anxiety, and make it harder to feel satisfied with the work you do.
In this two-part course, we'll explore perfectionism through a personal lens-how it shows up in your daily work, how it impacts your mental and emotional well-being, and how to break free from the constant cycle of "never good enough". You'll gain insights and practical tools to quiet your inner critic, set realistic expectations, and care for yourself while still providing exceptional patient care.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Pediatric and Geriatric Toxicology: Age Matters in Poison Response
courses.description: This 1-hour continuing education course explores the unique toxicological risks facing pediatric and geriatric small animal patients. Participants will examine how age-related physiological differences alter susceptibility to toxin exposure, clinical presentation, and treatment response. The course is designed for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and students seeking to strengthen their approach to toxicology cases in age-specific canine and feline patients. Topics include developmental stage and aging impact clinical signs, diagnostic interpretation, treatment selection, and prognosis in toxicology cases. Practical case-based examples will highlight adjustments in diagnostic evaluation, medication use, fluid therapy, and supportive care for young and elderly patients

courses.title: CPR - A Team Approach (TECH449)
courses.description: This course provides a focused, evidence-based overview of small-animal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) aligned with the RECOVER 2024 guidelines. Participants will learn how to prepare their hospital and respond effectively as a coordinated veterinary team during cardiopulmonary arrest events. Core topics include patient recognition, high-quality basic and advanced life support, post-arrest patient stabilization, and newborn resuscitation. The course emphasizes practical, team-centered skills that enhance confidence, communication, and patient outcomes in emergency situations.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: The Vomiting Cat (DIAG433)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will cover using ultrasound to diagnose the underlying causes of vomiting in cats. The normal ultrasound appearance of the feline gastrointestinal tract will be reviewed and then contrasted with such topics as feline chronic enteropathies, gastrointestinal neoplasia, mechanical obstructions, functional ileus and pancreatitis.

courses.title: Pruritus Simplified: A Step-by-Step Approach to the Allergic Dog
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Joya Griffin will present a practical, step-by-step clinical approach to evaluating the pruritic dog, beginning with the initial diagnostic investigation and progressing through evidence-based treatment selection. Participants will learn how to systematically rule out common differential diagnoses and identify allergic skin disease. In addition, Dr. Griffin will discuss how to assess pruritus severity and inflammatory skin lesions to aid in the development of individualized treatment plans. Emphasis will be placed on practical decision-making to improve patient outcomes and client satisfaction.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: The Feline Urinary Tract (DIAG432)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will cover the use of ultrasound to assess the feline urinary tract, including the normal ultrasound appearance of the feline kidney and bladder, deviations from normal that are not clinically relevant, and the ultrasound appearance of diseases that affect the feline kidney and bladder. In addition, there will be a review of ultrasound-guided cystocentesis.

courses.title: PLE-ease: Just Change the Diet? A Practical Approach to Chronic Enteropathies and Protein-Losing Enteropathy
courses.description: Chronic enteropathies (CE) and protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) remain among the most common yet diagnostically challenging gastrointestinal disorders encountered in small animal practice. This lecture provides an evidence-based, practical framework for approaching patients with chronic gastrointestinal disease, emphasizing the recently published 2026 ACVIM Consensus Statement on chronic enteropathies. Attendees will learn how to localize gastrointestinal disease, prioritize diagnostic testing, recognize disorders that mimic PLE, and determine when dietary therapy alone is appropriate versus when advanced diagnostics are warranted. The lecture concludes with a practical discussion of nutritional management, lymphangiectasia, thrombosis prevention, and treatment strategies for dogs with protein-losing enteropathy.

courses.title: Controlling Controlled Drugs (TECH163)
courses.description: Are you sure the controlled drug policies for your practice comply with DEA regulations? This course provides practical guidance on controlled substance accountability in the veterinary hospital. Get an overview of current DEA regulations, including registration, ordering, security, dispensing, accountability, inventories, and common problem-resolution scenarios in a veterinary practice setting.

courses.title: Spinal Cord Trauma (EMRG220)
courses.description: This course will cover emergency stabilization, management and analgesia for acute spinal trauma patients, neurological evaluation, diagnostic procedures and prognosis for animals suffering from spinal trauma injuries and best anesthesia practices for those patients requiring advanced diagnostic imaging and/or surgery.

courses.title: Coaching, Reviews, and Feedback (STAF194)
courses.description:
When do we give coaching, reviews, or feedback, and how can we tell the difference between them?
In this course, we'll focus on how to nurture a perfect-10 superstar employee. We will discuss how and when to use coaching sessions, performance reviews, and feedback meetings appropriately to outline expectations and deliver information to employees. You'll learn how to calculate and give raises based on goal achievement, enhanced skill development, or positive behavior. We'll also address how to correct substandard performance - and when to call it quits and steer a substandard performer right out the front door of the practice for good.

courses.title: Occlusal Equilibration & Diagnostic Module 1
courses.description: Occlusal Equilibration & Diagnostic Module 1 is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: CANIS Conference
courses.description: Brought to you by Aggressive Dog and APDT International, the CANIS Conference (Canine Advocacy, Networking, Innovation, and Science) is not your average industry event. It is a celebration of all things dog. Over four energizing days, trainers, behavior consultants, veterinarians, shelter and rescue workers, sport dog handlers, and pet care professionals come together to learn, connect, and spark new ideas. With five engaging educational tracks, live demonstrations, and extensive networking opportunities, CANIS is where science meets passion, innovation sparks ideas, and the future of dog welfare takes center stage.

courses.title: 2026 BARC Behaviour and Rehabilitation Conference: Diagnosing & Treating Lameness and Behaviour Like A Pro
courses.description: This inaugural Canadian conference featuring the latest diagnostics, treatment options, and research for veterinarians interested in all aspects of behaviour or musculoskeletal issues, including those with certification in rehabilitation, acupuncture, chiropractic care, or those who focus on post-injury recovery, surgery, lameness, neurological issues, and arthritis. It will be held in person, in British Columbia, Canada, on Saturday, September 12 and Sunday, September 13, 2026. The CE sessions will cover new research, trends, and treatment plans for lameness, pain, rehabilitation, and behaviour, including behaviour affect on post-injury and surgery, neurological issues, and arthritis, providing attendees with immediately usable information. There are 11 sessions on two individual streams for rehabilitation and behaviour, as well as 3 dual stream sessions bringing together behaviour specialists, rehabilitation specialists, and general practitioners who will learn new ways of working together.

courses.title: LafeberVet Barron Sea Turtle Program Application
courses.description: Presented in conjunction with the Wildlife Disease Association, this webinar will outline the regulatory, anatomical, diagnostic, and therapeutic considerations involved in sea turtle rehabilitation. Sea turtle rehabilitation in the United States emphasizes the need for compliance with state and federal rules, often requiring special licensure. Seven sea turtle species are typically threatened or endangered, with anthropogenic threats driving conservation and clinical care efforts. Anatomy details cover the carapace, plastron, and shell structure, including scute patterns and bone derivation. Diagnostics prioritize a thorough physical exam, baseline temperature, imaging, blood work, and fecal analysis, with careful choice of sampling sites and anticoagulants to minimize stress. Critical care stresses graded fluid therapy, rewarming, analgesia, and cautious antibiotic use, while supportive care emphasizes rehydration, nutrition, and, if needed, enteric or parenteral feeding. Therapeutics discuss anesthesia protocols, multimodal analgesia, and a broad empiric antimicrobial/antifungal plan. Common presentations include fibropapillomatosis, plastic ingestion, buoyancy disorders, and trauma from human activities, all of which influence prognosis and potential euthanasia.

courses.title: Introduction to Ultrasound-Guided Cystocentesis (TECH461)
courses.description:
Urine collection and analysis may be part of a complete healthy pet screening panel or performed in patients with clinical signs associated with upper urinary tract or lower urinary tract. Ultrasound-guided cystocentesis increases the likelihood of obtaining a sterile urine sample in obese pets or pets with small bladders compared to manual palpation techniques. In addition, it provides an opportunity to assess the urinary bladder for common abnormalities. Because this procedure is often performed by veterinary technicians, they are often the first person on the medical team to evaluate a patient's bladder with ultrasound and should be aware of common abnormalities.
This course will review the normal ultrasound appearance of the canine and feline bladder, and contrast normal with common abnormalities, such as stones, wall masses or wall thickening. It will also review potential risks and complications of the procedure, and review in a step-by-step manner how to perform the procedure safely.

courses.title: Postural Rehabilitation Professional
courses.description: Postural Rehabilitation Professional is a 6 week, high contact program designed to teach equine professionals how to evaluate and remediate equine abnormal compensatory posture (ACP). Participants will learn about how standing posture is generated and controlled by the CNS, the peripheral structures critical to posture that tend to become distorted by domestication, how to recognize and remediate abnormal anatomic structures (distal limb/hoof, stomatognathic system) and function of the cervical spine to restore normal neutral posture to equine patients. We will also teach team-building among equine professionals, professional communications and how to apply injury forensics to chronic cases.

courses.title: EQ900: Equine Anatomy Discovery Workshop - Clay & Hands-On
courses.description: This course utilizes the brilliant system developed by Jon Zahourek, founder of ANATOMY IN CLAY Learning Systems. It is designed for professionals to help solidify their knowledge of equine anatomy and is regularly attended by veterinarians and veterinary technicians. This comprehensive class allows students to build individual muscles on the Equiken model in clay, as well as palpate (or locate) each muscle on the live horse.
courses.location: Keep Stables at Chapel View Farm

courses.title: Compassion Fatigue (STAF183)
courses.description: Have you ever felt numb after a euthanasia, gotten home from a hard day, and picked a silly fight with your partner, or realized you hadn't had a good night's sleep in weeks, but couldn't figure out why? These can all be signs of compassion fatigue, or a gradual state of physical and emotional exhaustion that accumulates over time as we take on the pain, trauma, and distress we see nearly every day as veterinary professionals. Compassion fatigue training is designed to help you recapture and hold onto your sense of purpose, joy, and hope. We will learn the difference between compassion fatigue and burnout, discuss secondary traumatic stress, and introduce evidence-based professional resiliency skills to help you manage stress and the emotional demands of this challenging but beautiful profession.

courses.title: Food as Medicine: The Power of Functional Nutrition
courses.description: This webinar will introduce functional nutrition as a practical, evidence-informed approach to using food as therapeutic support, offering a way to help patients thrive while avoiding harm from overconditioning and ultraprocessed diets. Through real-world examples, veterinary professionals will explore how to individualize recommendations based on genetics, breed factors, and more and implement clinic-ready strategies, including those on client communication, common nutraceuticals, responsive conditions/body systems, and outcome monitoring.

courses.title: ISELP One Day Seminar Featuring the Hock and Proximal Suspensory
courses.description: The seminar will focus on the Hock and Proximal Suspensory, detailing bone and joint structures, tendons, vessels and nerves. There will be clinical case presentations, lectures, and wet-lab where each attendee will have hands-on instruction led by Dr. Peters and Dr. Oakley. This is a unique opportunity to learn from two experts who specialize in locomotor pathology.

courses.title: Red Light, Green Light: Rapid Triage for Primary Care Practices
courses.description: This presentation covers all aspects of triage from phone triage to rapid assessment. It covers common triage sorting techniques and how to discuss emergency intervention and consent with owners for more critical cases.

courses.title: IVAS Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture - Labs
courses.description:
The Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture taught by the International Veterinary Acupuncture Society (IVAS) has been setting the global standard in veterinary acupuncture since 1974. The curriculum of the course integrates a background of the fundamentals and application of the scientific basis for acupuncture, as well as a background in the fundamentals and applications of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and acupuncture. The educational program provides acupuncture study and clinical applications for small animal, large animal, avian, and exotic species. The program prepares the participant for integration of acupuncture into clinical practice.
The curriculum of the course is not limited to the study of TCM theory. The curriculum incorporates current scientific acupuncture theory and biomedical science in its application and approach to patient assessment and treatment. A variety of methods of patient examination and treatment are taught and demonstrated. Students are reminded to always perform a Western medical examination first and obtain all necessary diagnostics prior to integrating acupuncture.
The IVAS certification process requires successful completion of all online content, 3 sessions of hands-on labs; attendance of the Mentored Internship; passage of the written exam and either one or two practical examinations depending on their area of focus; submission of a logbook documenting 10 cases and a peer-reviewed written case report. Graduates of the IVAS Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture will be certified in either Small Animal, Equine, or both.
Lectures begin with the anatomic, physiologic, and historical aspects of acupuncture. As the course progresses, patient assessment, and diagnosis from both a clinically western scientific perspective and TCM theory approach are introduced. courses.location: Embassy Suites San Antonio Brooks Hotel and Spa

courses.title: IVUSS 2026 Annual Meeting - Utrecht
courses.description: The annual conference of the International Veterinary Ultrasound Society. The goals of the lectures at this conference are to improve the knowledge base, skills, and diagnostic ability of small animal sonographers in the fields of abdominal sonography and echocardiography.

courses.title: BioMedtrix Universal Hip In-Person Mentorship Opportunity
courses.description: The BioMedtrix Universal Hip In-Person Mentorship Opportunity offers surgeons and their team technical feedback and support required to gain confidence in performing THR as they prepare to perform clinical cases.

courses.title: Dental Nerve Blocks (TECH359)
courses.description: This lecture will serve to provide veterinary technicians and veterinarians with instructions on performing safe and effective regional and local nerve blocks for painful dental procedures. Included in this discussion will be information on which drugs to use, drug doses, equipment needed, tissues blocked, and proper placement of the regional nerve block. Photos will be provided for visual aids.

courses.title: Controlling Controlled Drugs(TECH163)
courses.description: This course is designed to provide practical guidance on the administration of a controlled substance accountability program in the veterinary hospital. The course will present an overview of the DEA regulations, including registration, ordering, security, dispensing, accountability, inventories, and problem resolution scenarios that are likely to happen in a veterinary practice setting. **This course will discuss US federal (DEA) laws only. **

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers-Module 4
courses.description:
The Laboratory Retrievers Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine.
These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.title: Team Approach to Developing a Balanced Anesthesia Drug Protocol (TECH456)
courses.description:
A team-based approach to veterinary anesthesia is essential for ensuring patient safety, optimizing anesthetic outcomes, and promoting efficient clinical workflow. Members of the veterinary support team are frequently responsible for monitoring patients during anesthetic events, yet they are often excluded from the planning phase, which includes pre-anesthetic patient assessment, development of patient-specific anesthesia drug protocols, and anesthesia management strategies.
In this course, you'll explore all aspects of developing a balanced anesthesia drug protocol, beginning with pre-anesthetic patient assessment and progressing through commonly used drugs and techniques for premedication, induction, maintenance, and recovery. We'll incorporate weekly case-based discussions and practical applications to reinforce key concepts and promote real-world clinical applications.
By the end of the course, you will have gained the knowledge and confidence to participate actively in anesthesia planning and anesthesia drug protocol development - and you'll be ready to demonstrate to the veterinarians you work with that collaborative anesthesia management means better staff utilization, more efficient workflows, and enhanced patient outcomes.

courses.provider: CAREFREE DENTISTRY AND ORAL SURGERY FOR ANIMALS
courses.title: Introduction to Feline Dentistry and Oral Surgery
courses.description: This course provides comprehensive, hands-on training in feline veterinary dentistry and oral surgery, with emphasis on feline oral anatomy, common dental and periodontal pathology, regional anesthesia techniques, and methodical extraction procedures. Participants will learn evidence-based approaches to feline tooth extractions, including mucogingival flap design, sectioning multi-rooted teeth, alveolar bone removal, use of dental luxators, alveoloplasty, and tension-free closure, as well as strategies for managing common complications. The program combines focused lectures with extensive wet lab experience using feline cadaver specimens, allowing participants to build confidence and technical skill in diagnosing feline dental disease and performing extractions. Designed for DVMs seeking to improve their feline dentistry and oral surgery skills, this course emphasizes practical application, clinical decision-making, and improved patient outcomes in cats.
courses.location: Carefree Dentistry & Oral Surgery for Animals

courses.title: The many faces of FIP
courses.description: This session will discuss recent clinical experience with feline infectious peritonitis (FIP), emerging areas of knowledge with this virus, and a focus on the variety of clinical presentations of FIP. The session will utilize case discussions as a starting point for highlighting newly identified clinical manifestations of FIP, when to include FIP on the differential diagnosis list, and logical approaches to FIP diagnostic test selection and interpretation. We will review what is known in the literature and what is still not known, as well as upcoming areas of research to keep an eye on.

courses.provider: CAREFREE DENTISTRY AND ORAL SURGERY FOR ANIMALS
courses.title: Introduction to Canine Dentistry and Oral Surgery
courses.description: This course provides comprehensive, hands-on training in veterinary dentistry with a focus on pathology recognition, local anesthesia techniques, and surgical extraction principles. Participants will learn evidence- based methods for retained root retrieval, periodontal flap surgery, and root planing. The program also includes instruction on the clinical use of Doxirobe and the application of bonded sealants for advanced dental case management. Designed for DVMs seeking to improve their practical dentistry skills, this course combines lecture-based learning with guided clinical exercises to build confidence in performing common and advanced dental procedures.
courses.location: Carefree Dentistry & Oral Surgery for Animals

courses.title: CN1200: Canine CranioSacral Therapy - Level 1
courses.description: This 5-day class will train students in the theory, concepts and practice of Craniosacral Therapy as it pertains to the canine population, while giving them the opportunity to integrate this knowledge with the Nervous System and Fascial System. This course is designed to teach participants the skills involved in evaluating and helping neuromusculoskeletal/fascial dysfunction in dogs.

courses.title: EQ103: Advanced Equine Soft Tissue Techniques, Intro to Spinal Mobilization, Rehabilitation Concepts & Clinical Reasoning
courses.description: This 5-day course has a strong emphasis on the practical application of advanced equine bodywork/soft tissue mobilization (STM) techniques, including sports massage, stretching, mobilization and muscle activation techniques. It is designed for equine healthcare providers to incorporate the use of soft tissue work into their existing practices and elevate their skills to apply the advanced techniques.
courses.location: Keep Stables at Chapel View Farm

courses.title: Under the Microscope-Cytology for Veterinary Technicians (TECH263)
courses.description: Cytology is a common in-house testing tool in the veterinary practice in which veterinary technicians play a vital role in the collection process, data recording, and evaluation of specimens to aid the veterinarian in the preliminary diagnosis. The primary purpose of this course is to develop an understanding of the proper collection techniques, sample handling, processing, and evaluation of cytological specimens. Techniques to improve the diagnostic value of the specimen, submission to outside laboratories, cellular anatomy, and microscopic identification techniques will be covered.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: 10 Ways Cats Are Not Small Dogs (DIAG435)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will review the ultrasound appearance of 10 diseases/anatomic variations that are unique to cats and were not touched upon during the other Feline Ultrasound courses. There will be time provided at the end of the session for questions regarding feline ultrasound stemming from this or any of the other Feline Ultrasound courses.

courses.title: The Electrical System of the Heart: Principles and Applications of ECG Monitoring (TECH459)
courses.description: In practice, ECG rhythms often differ from textbook examples. Interpreting ECGs requires a gentle, detailed understanding of the heart's electrical workings. This engaging four-part course warmly guides you through the basics of conduction, pacing, and arrhythmias, and offers practical tips to help you become more confident in ECG interpretation.

courses.title: Real-World Topics in Small Animal Dermatology
courses.description: This course explores various topics in small animal dermatology. We will review the underlying causes, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, and evidence-based treatment strategies for different skin conditions and dermatological issues.

courses.title: Veterinary Abdominal Ultrasound Training Camp
courses.description: This hands-on, small-group veterinary abdominal ultrasound training program is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians of all skill levels, from beginners to advanced practitioners. Participants will gain practical experience performing diagnostic-quality abdominal ultrasounds using a structured, protocol-based approach. Over three immersive days, attendees will master core organ imaging, systematic scanning workflows, and advanced techniques for the liver, pancreas, adrenal glands, and gastrointestinal tract. The program includes interactive lectures, live-patient scanning labs, and 30 days of personalized feedback through mentored teleradiology, ensuring participants leave with confidence, improved efficiency, and skills that translate directly to clinical practice. This course emphasizes hands-on learning, real-world applications, and long-term clinical success.
courses.location: COVE - The Center of Veterinary Excellence

courses.provider: AMERICAN VETERINARY SOCIETY OF ANIMAL BEHAVIOR
courses.title: Clinical Animal Behavior Conference 2026
courses.description: The Clinical Animal Behavior Conference is a 2.5-day intensive event dedicated to advancing the field of veterinary behavioral medicine. Centered on the theme Evolving Together: Advancing our Understanding of Behavior, this conference provides veterinary professionals with actionable, compassionate, and science-based strategies to elevate patient care and improve outcomes. Throughout the conference, attendees will learn to identify behavioral disorders, devise treatment plans which include behavior modifications, environmental changes, the use of constructional affection, enrichment and psychoactive medications. In addition, attendees will learn strategies such as fostering a team approach and using inclusive language to build trust and empathy among the health care team and with clients in order to achieve effective and consistent long term behavioral care for patients.

courses.title: Veterinary Technician Utilization-Hey I Got This! (STAF196)
courses.description: How well is your practice utilizing veterinary technicians compared to other practices and current standards? Placing and utilizing vet techs in the appropriate role within the team is linked to better patient care, staff fulfillment, more manageable workloads, increased practice revenue, and team wellness. This course will identify obstacles to reaching higher standards and discuss how to have difficult discussions within the hospital to aid in increasing vet tech utilization.

courses.title: Backyard Poultry Basics (EXOT333)
courses.description: With a growing interest in self-sufficiency, the number of people keeping small flocks of backyard poultry is rising. With this rise in flock numbers is a growing expectancy for veterinary care at a level equivalent to what clients have come to expect for other companion animals. The first step for veterinarians to meet these expectations is to acquire the knowledge of the basics, without which it is difficult to understand the hows and whys of disease. By completing this course, veterinarians, technicians and students will have a thorough grasp of poultry, their care and nutrition, and the basics of providing veterinary care.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: The Yellow Cat and Ultrasound-Guided Fine Needle Aspirates (DIAG434)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will review two important concepts: scanning the yellow cat and how to perform ultrasound guided fine needle aspirates. We will review the 3 causes of icterus in cats and how to use ultrasound to narrow down the differential list. We will discuss the normal appearance of the feline liver, gallbladder, and pancreas on ultrasound, and review the ultrasound appearance of diseases causing hyperbilirubinemia in cats. The course will review when to perform fine needle aspirates and when to avoid the procedure. There will be a detailed overview of how to perform ultrasound guided FNA and how to prepare and submit slides, considerations and approaches to aspirating individual organs, and ideal case selection.

courses.title: Getting Through the Day: How to Make it Through the Day in GP Module 3 (SAIM803)
courses.description:
The VIN Foundation (https://vinfoundation.org) is a non-profit organization committed to helping you, and all new graduates, feel supported as you journey into and through our profession. Getting Through the Day is a VIN Foundation resource made possible through individual donations and grants. VIN membership is not required to access the VIN Foundation resources.
In this course different topics will be presented each week and the presentations will include highlights on pathophysiology, case presentation, differentials, diagnostic approach, treatment recommendations, and case examples where appropriate. Important non-technical skills will also be included.

courses.title: Backyard Poultry Medicine and Surgery (EXOT334)
courses.description: Most of us in clinical practice have realized by now that the backyard chicken is increasingly becoming a part of both our clients' lives and ours, as clinicians. But when you look back at your university training, you also realize that learning about commercial poultry and disease management doesn't prepare you for the reality of companion chicken practice, where the value of the patient cannot be measured in just dollars. This course will give you more in-depth knowledge on the medicine and surgery of backyard poultry than you have had to date, giving you the confidence to walk into your examination room, comfortable in your knowledge and abilities to offer the standard of care you believe in.

courses.provider: WEST INDIES VETERINARY CONFERENCE BY ROSS UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF VETERINARY MEDICI
courses.title: West Indies Veterinary Conference 2026
courses.description: The West Indies Veterinary Conference will include medical and non-medical interactive programming focusing on small animal and large animal veterinary care as well as practice management. Topics to include dentistry, small and large dermatology, emergency and critical care, equine sports medicine, gastrointestinal disease, small and large animal microbiology, point of care ultrasound, urgent care, cardiology, and practice management.

courses.title: Nutrition Poo-pourri: An Intro to Gastrointestinal Diets
courses.description: This lecture is intended to cover the various types of commercial diets available for veterinarians to choose from when managing cases of gastrointestinal disease. We will discuss the 4 main categories of gastrointestinal diets, as well as a few mock cases to help with identifying clinical applications to help veterinarians better cater dietary therapy to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: VLI Trek
courses.description: VLI Trek is a hands-on, immersive program developed by the Veterinary Leadership Institute (VLI) to help veterinary healthcare professionals experience more fulfilling careers. Why Trek? Veterinary professionals work in a vibrant and engaging profession. The same things that capture our hearts and minds can also weigh us down. We can lose our focus, energy and enthusiasm for our professional and personal lives. There are no easy fixes or one-stop shopping solutions to fix these problems. It takes personal work, reflection and a supportive community to help us. VLI Trek is about stepping off the treadmill, and in community with like-minded colleagues, to discover and develop new capacities to engage in our work and in our lives.

courses.title: Oral Surgery 1 Oral Pathology Oral Radiology
courses.description: Through presentations using a multitude of clinical images, interactive lecturing , video technique presentations and intensive hands-on wet labs, class participants will effectively learn how to recognize normal versus disease states and employ the most current techniques in their treatment. Intraoral radiographic skill in reading and technique is the foundation of diagnosis and treatment of oral disease. It is to this end that participants will be thoroughly grounded in this discipline through a multitude of clinical case studies. Videography of surgical extractions in the cat and dog and the step by step techniques in approaching the various teeth by creating pedicle flaps will be meticulously explained in order to enhance the practitioners ability to immediately apply them in their practices.

courses.title: Anesthetic Plan Creation
courses.description:
This program will detail the process for creating individualized and multi-modal
anesthetic plans for cats and dogs. The lecture will start with pre-procedure considerations (e.g. patient
assessment, patient optimization/stabilization, goals of anesthesia, and pre-visit pharmaceuticals). From
there, the lecture will outline commonly utilized drugs and drug dosages for the four phases of general
anesthesia (preanesthesia, induction, maintenance, and recovery). Finally, audience members will be
given the opportunity to create hypothetical anesthetic plans based on real world patients.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: DIAGNOSTIC MUSCULOSKELETAL ULTRASOUND (197-35962)
courses.description: Diagnostic Musculoskeletal Ultrasound will focus on how ultrasound can be used to make musculoskeletal diagnoses more precisely, accurately and efficiently. Basic skills in ultrasonographic assessment will be covered as well as how findings can be applied clinically. This will enable a more targeted treatment approach to patients suffering from soft tissue injuries such as Achilles tendinopathy and iliopsoas myotendinopathy. The course will include live dog labs, lectures, and hands-on experience with ultrasound.

courses.title: Anesthetic Considerations for Patients with Respiratory Disease
courses.description:
This program will review general anesthetic considerations for small animal
patients with respiratory disease. The lecture will begin with a brief overview of the respiratory system.
After that, common respiratory monitoring modalities will be discussed. Finally, both general and
specific anesthetic recommendations for this subset of patients will be provided and discussed.

courses.title: From Screening to Strategy: Advancing Preventive Care with Diagnostics
courses.description:
Preventive medicine is a cornerstone of high-quality veterinary care, yet it remains underutilized in many practices. This presentation explores the value of early disease detection through comprehensive diagnostic screening, including vector-borne disease testing with 4Dx and intestinal parasite screening with Fecal Dx.
Participants will learn practical strategies to better integrate preventive diagnostics into everyday workflows, improve team alignment, and effectively communicate their value to clients. By strengthening both clinical approaches and client engagement, veterinary teams can enhance patient outcomes, increase compliance, and elevate the standard of care.

courses.title: Blood Smear Evaluation: A Practical Step-by-Step Guide
courses.description: Blood smears remain one of the most valuable, accessible, and cost-effective diagnostic tools in veterinary medicine. This session provides a clear, practical approach to reading and interpreting smears in everyday practice. Participants will learn how to systematically evaluate smears, recognize key morphologic changes and infectious agents, and integrate findings into the broader diagnostic process. Additional tools for morphological evaluation will also be discussed.

courses.title: Practice Essentials to Managing Otitis
courses.description: In this session, we will discuss primary and secondary causes of otitis externa and best practices for treatment that address not only the current infection but also predisposing or perpetuating pathology.

courses.title: Veterinary Clinical Oncology
courses.description:
This course program provides a comprehensive and clinically oriented overview of veterinary oncology for general practitioners working with dogs and cats.
Participants can expect an in-depth review of cancer biology, diagnostic approaches, staging, and treatment modalities, surgery including, chemotherapy, metronomic therapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapies, and supportive care.The program places special emphasis on the tumors most frequently encountered in general practice addressing both canine and feline patients.
Throughout the course, attention is given not only to tumor control but also to treatment tolerability, management of adverse effects, paraneoplastic syndromes, pain control, and ethical decision-making. By the end of the program, attendees will be better equipped to diagnose cancer, discuss prognosis and treatment options with pet owners, initiate appropriate therapies, monitor response and toxicity, and prioritize patient welfare throughout the disease course.

courses.title: Basic and Point-of-Care Ultrasound: Abdomen, Thorax and Cardiac!
courses.description:
Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is a rapidly evolving field in veterinary medicine, especially in Emergency Medicine. Ultrasound machines are often available to practitioners, but training is lacking. There is limited training in veterinary school, and the post-graduate training is not uniform. Unfortunately, this means your brand-new shining machine may be sitting in a corner of your clinic collecting dust or being used only for cystocentesis.
In this course, you will work with experts in emergency medicine and critical care with many years of experience teaching POCUS and you will learn how to use your machine appropriately. This course is mainly designed to use the ultrasound machine as a point-of-care in an emergency but will also teach you to use it as a tool for abdominal ultrasound. The great thing about this course is that you will learn to ultrasound the abdomen, the chest, and the heart.
You will be provided in-person lectures on the three types of POCUS in the morning, followed by a 4-hours hands-on lab on anesthetized small to medium breed dogs. The same pattern will be repeated on Day 2, which allows for repetition and building on those motor skills. This lab is a great way to learn, practice or refine your skills in POCUS. After this course, you will be set to go back to your practice and start applying your skills from Day 1.

courses.title: Recognizing and Treating Pain in Senior Cats: A Practical Clinical Approach
courses.description: Pain in senior cats is often under-recognized and undertreated, yet it can significantly impact quality of life. This practical session will guide you through identifying, assessing, and managing pain in geriatric feline patients. Learn to recognize subtle behavioral and clinical signs, choose appropriate diagnostic tools, and develop multimodal pain management strategies that combine pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic approaches tailored to the senior cat. By the end of this lecture, you will feel confident in improving comfort and overall well-being in your aging feline patients.

courses.title: It's Not Always The Food . . . Or Is It? Navigating Food Hypersensitivities in Small Animals
courses.description: This course will cover how to clinically approach cutaneous adverse food reactions in both dogs and cats. We will highlight insights from the critically appraised topic on adverse food reactions of companion animals published in a nine-article series. We will weigh options and review diets available. Critically examine the best practices to maximize compliance with diet trials and communicate clear expectations with clients to accomplish shared goals. Lastly, we will review the most common missteps made during trials that lead to incomplete or inaccurate diagnoses.

courses.title: Introduction to Canine Arthroscopy
courses.description:
You know that arthroscopy is your next level for your clients and as an orthopedist, but there is something that you may not know-while there are some great arthroscopists in this world, nobody was ever born with natural arthroscopy skills. That is EXACTLY why we designed this course! Excellent arthroscopy skills flow from hours of hands-on training that reinforce your knowledge of fundamental principles. We know that great hands-on training from great trainers is the only way to rapidly grow your arthroscopy skills, so that is exactly what we did.
In this course, you will learn and practice the important principles and skills in triangulation, camera head & light post positioning, portal and fluid flow management, and so much more. You will also learn to how to select great cases for you to apply and grow your new skills. You will return to your practice or training program with strong arthroscopy skills based upon sound knowledge of the foundational principles of canine arthroscopy.

courses.title: We Need to Talk, Resolving Case Complications with Communication
courses.description:
Surgical complications are an unavoidable part of practice, but the way they are discussed among all parties often determines whether a challenging case becomes a source of collaboration, conflict, or fractured trust. This interactive lecture uses real-world large and small animal surgical scenarios to explore the difficult conversations that arise among surgeons, primary care veterinarians, clients, and clinical teams. Rather than focusing on the technical details of each case, the session invites residents to step back from the clinician cap and examine the communication decisions that shape client perception, referral relationships, case continuity, and professional collegiality.
Residents in both large and small animal surgery will gain practical strategies for navigating situations when expectations diverge, outcomes are imperfect, or communication is delayed, incomplete, or misunderstood. Emphasis will be placed on using the ACVS Collaborative Relationship Communication Tool to proactively clarify roles, timelines, follow-up responsibilities, client messaging, and shared decision-making between the specialist and primary care veterinarian. By examining difficult cases through a communication lens, this lecture aims to help residents build the professional habits needed to preserve trust, reduce conflict, and improve patient outcomes through stronger teamwork.

courses.title: Creeping Risks, Local Consequences: Emerging Parasites in Companion Animal Practice
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: New Thoughts on Old Diseases: Chronic Kidney Disease, Hyperthyroidism, Diabetes Mellitus, and Osteoarthritis.
courses.description: In this session, well focus on the things that affect geriatric cats the most. Older cats seem to collect diseases, which can make interpreting laboratory tests challenging. Once diagnoses are made, balancing treatments can be equally challenging! Well examine the most effective ways to use both classic and newer diagnostic tools and treatments to keep our older cats happy and healthy

courses.title: Feline Diabetes Deep Dive Managing DKA When the ER Isnt an Option
courses.description: Feline diabetes can be challenging to manage and diabetic ketoacidosis DKA adds a layer of complexity especially when referral to an emergency clinic is not an option. This lecture examines how to recognize treat and manage DKA patients in a general practice setting. We will cover how to differentiate DKA from uncomplicated diabetes interpret key clinical and laboratory findings and understand the pathophysiology driving this critical condition. Practical guidance will be provided for diagnostics that you can perform in clinic including blood glucose ketone testing blood gases and electrolyte assessments. Treatment and monitoring plans that dont require continuous insulin infusion fluid therapy electrolyte supplementation and practical insulin protocols that work in non ER practice settings will be discussed. By the end of this session you will have practical tools to manage DKA even when resources are limited.

courses.title: The Itch-hikers Guide to the Feline Galaxy vector-borne infections from fleas, ticks, and mosquitoes
courses.description: Tick and mosquito borne disease get a lot of attention when it comes to our canine friends, but dont forget about cats! Lets explore potential infectious diseases that lurk in common vectors, as well as how to recognize and manage these challenging infections.

courses.title: Premedication
courses.description: This program will take an in-depth look at the preanesthetic/premedication phase of general anesthesia for cats and dogs. After a brief discussion of basic definitions and goals, commonly utilized premedicates will be discussed in detail. Drug selection and suggested drug dosages will be provided. Finally, the lecture will answer commonly asked questions about specific premedicants.

courses.title: From Big Headlines to Small Animal Practice: Emerging Parasite Risks in the Exam Room
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: Implementing CancerDX into Clinical Workflows
courses.description: This presentation introduces IDEXX Cancer Dx testing and provides a practical roadmap for integrating it into everyday veterinary clinical workflows as both an aid in diagnosing sick patients and a screening tool for at risk dogs. It explores how earlier detection of canine lymphoma can improve patient outcomes and the pet parent experience while guiding teams through change management strategies that support adoption confidence and consistency. Using real world case examples protocol development and clear implementation steps the presentation helps practices move from reactive cancer detection to proactive care creating clarity aligning teams and embedding Cancer Dx as a sustainable part of diagnostic and preventive medicine.

courses.title: From Pitfalls to Profits: Reimagining Veterinary Business Success
courses.description:
As veterinary professionals, we often find ourselves caught in a "clinical whirlwind" where the demands of the day-to-day obscure the path to true practice health and personal fulfillment. This high-impact, two-hour session, delivered by CSUVetCE, distills a comprehensive three-part series into a strategic roadmap for alumni to move beyond operational survival and toward sustainable prosperity. We begin by unmasking common "profitability pitfalls," challenging the misconception that revenue growth alone equals business health and explaining why "Normalized Net Profit" (NNP) is the only metric that truly reflects your practice's value. Participants will learn to activate powerful levers for success, from mastering Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) to transitioning from reactive reminders to proactive pre-booking systems that slash client lapse rates.
The presentation further explores how to unlock human potential by addressing the "hidden drain" on productivity: the non-technical skills gap and the "Wallet Guardian" mindset. By recalibrating your "Why" around patient advocacy, you can improve clinical outcomes and professional self-worth while reducing the stress and anxiety that lead to high attrition rates. Finally, we provide practical tools for prioritizing "on-business" leadership over "in-business" technical tasks. By utilizing strategies like the Urgent/Important matrix and effective delegation, owners can reclaim 10 to 20 hours of their week to focus on high-value strategic planning. This session offers a proven pathway to enhance patient care, increase financial stability, and ensure a longer, more fulfilling career in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Introduction to Small Animal Laparoscopy
courses.description: Minimally-invasive surgery (MIS) is the standard of care for many human procedures and is increasingly the expectation of many of our more discerning pet-owning clients in progressive veterinary practices. Now is the time for you to reach for new professional horizons and discover the many advantages of laparoscopic organ biopsy, diagnostic techniques and surgical procedures. Your new skills will distinguish you and your practice within your community!

courses.title: Reducing Pain and Improving Mobility: Environmental Management for OA Patients
courses.description: Environmental modification is a critical yet often underutilized component of comprehensive osteoarthritis (OA) management in dogs. This program provides veterinary professionals with practical strategies to identify and address environmental factors that contribute to pain, impaired mobility, and increased risk of injury in canine OA patients. Participants will explore how common household challenges--such as slippery flooring, stairs, furniture access, and resource placement--can negatively impact joint health and daily function. The session will focus on simple, effective interventions that can be implemented to promote joint protection, improve mobility, and support safe movement within the home environment. Emphasis will also be placed on the role of caregiver education in successful OA management. Attendees will learn how to guide pet owners in recognizing environmental barriers and adopting sustainable modifications that enhance comfort, confidence, and quality of life for their dogs. Through practical, real-world applications, this program aims to reinforce the importance of integrating environmental management into multimodal OA treatment plans, supporting better long-term outcomes for canine patients.

courses.title: Rhino Dehorning Mission
courses.description:
Join our team on a week-long educational course about rhino care, management, and medicine whilst you help with an exciting dehorning mission. This is ideal for anyone wanting to support conservation, and developing clinical knowledge and skills around megaherbivore medicine. This mission is not just a training course. It's an experience that connects participants to the broader concepts of wildlife conservation, immerses them in the African wilderness, and fosters a sense of unity among those who share a passion for preserving the world's rhino population.
The majestic rhinoceros, one of the world's most iconic animals, has been pushed to the brink of extinction due to poaching, habitat loss, and the illegal trade of its horns. These magnificent creatures, revered for their strength and resilience, have become targets for poachers who seek to profit from the black-market value of rhino horn. Conservation efforts have intensified globally, and one of the most effective methods of protecting rhinos from poaching is dehorning.
Dehorning is bringing them back from the brink. This is the backdrop of the Rhino Dehorning Mission, a hands-on educational program designed to bring passionate people in the veterinary industry together in a collaborative effort to protect rhinos. For seven days, participants aim to dehorn at least 6 rhinos, whilst also carrying out practical training and immersive lectures about the science of rhino health, anatomy, physiology, and immobilization. When the sun sets, the evenings are filled with social and cultural activities, including bush walks, campfires, and traditional African dance performances so delegates can discover more about Namibian culture and history. The mission schedule may alter and change depending on the weather and animals. For example, we may do more dehornings on a single day than planned if many rhinos are found in one area. We may even dart multiple rhinos at once! In such instances, the lectures will be shifted around

courses.title: Anesthetic management of small animals with co-existing conditions and diseases
courses.description: Familiarity with the underlying disease conditions and their impact on anesthetics improves the outcome of the anesthetic procedure and is a necessary step for practicing veterinarians. In addition, controlling pain and appropriate analgesic medications and methods are essential for animals welfare and improving the outcome of the procedures. In this course, these topics will be discussed in detail to help clinicians design anesthetic and analgesic protocols tailored to the needs of the animal and the disease condition.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Introduction to Canine Rehabilitation
courses.description:
This course is the first of four modules for CCRT, CCRVT/CCRVN, and CCRA certification.
The course comprises online pre-course videos that must be watched before class and four days in class.
This course gives students a fundamental understanding of canine functional anatomy, physiology, and biomechanics. Using clay, students build relevant structures on canine skeletons and get hands-on experience palpating live dogs in class.
Common orthopedic and neurological disorders of the canine patient, including conservative and surgical treatment options. Canine rehabilitation therapies that apply traditional physical therapy techniques, including manual therapies, therapeutic exercise, and physical modalities, are taught along with ways to incorporate them into veterinary practice.

courses.title: A Complete Introduction to Safety-Focused TPLO
courses.description:
This hybrid course includes 3 comprehensive hours of bite sized online modules that provide valuable tips on pathophysiology of CrCL disease, diagnosis, positioning for TPLO radiographs, preoperative planning, meniscal injury and treatment, and reducing surgical site infections.
Once in our CE lab, you will develop your hands on surgical skills to perform stifle arthrotomy, meniscal treatment, and TPLO using plastic bone models and cadaveric specimens. This is the only TPLO course in North America that supports you each step of the way during and after your training. While here, you will also spend time in insightful radiographic review discussions of your TPLOs before repeating the procedure on your pathway toward mastery.
Ponder this, even if you were trained to fly a Boeing 737, would you pilot a commercial flight without the decision making support of a flight plan, a co pilot, control tower and ground crew? Of course not. So, why would you do a surgery as intricate as TPLO without using a support team to enhance the safety for your patient?
This course trains you to use patient specific pre, intra and post-operative support on your individual TPLO patients. You will learn how to receive case by case preoperative guidance and procedural planning, use patient specific instructions to perform a guided TPLO cut, and to use detailed postoperative critique to shorten your learning curve and more rapidly grow your skills. Curious what this is all about? Better check it out.

courses.title: Twisted Pathogens: Updates on Canine Lyme Disease and Leptospirosis
courses.description: This presentation will review the etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, and presenting complaints related to Lyme disease and leptospirosis in dogs. Detailed coverage of several algorithms for treatment and vaccination strategies for both Lyme disease and leptospirosis, as well as future testing in dogs that are Lyme positive will be presented. Practitioners will be able to describe the signs associated with Lyme infection and leptospirosis, describe testing and treatment options, and understand vaccination strategies. Learners will also explore how Lyme and leptospirosis are both wildlife associated diseases and what dogs could be at risk.

courses.title: From National Headlines to Local Exam Rooms: What's Creeping into Companion Animal Practice
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: Rethinking The Management of Osteoarthritis
courses.description: Attendees will gain an understanding of the importance of recognizing and managing chronic pain, as well as the benefits of early OA diagnosis. Scientific data on multimodal analgesia options will be shared. The importance of pain assessment, intervention, multimodal treatment, and patient follow up will be points of emphasis.

courses.title: Infection in Large Animal Fracture
courses.description: 90 minute webinar reviewing the implications, treatment options, and clinical decision making of infection in large animal orthopedic surgery. Discussion will focus on the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of infection in large animal orthopedic patients with internal fixation for fracture repair or arthrodesis.

courses.title: Induction Phase of Anesthesia
courses.description:
This program will provide an overview of the induction phase of general
anesthesia for small animal patients. Specific topics to be discussed include: goals, workflow,
equipment preparation, preoxygenation, commonly utilized induction agents, induction speed,
induction quality, intubation, and initial monitoring.

courses.title: Understanding and Treating OA Pain: Practical Strategies for Veterinary Teams
courses.description:
Effective pain management is fundamental to improving mobility, comfort, and quality of life in dogs with osteoarthritis (OA). This program provides veterinary professionals with a practical, clinically relevant approach to recognizing and managing OA-associated pain across the disease continuum.
Participants will review the mechanisms and clinical presentation of OA pain, with an emphasis on identifying both overt and subtle indicators that may impact patient function and welfare. The session will explore commonly used oral analgesics, including their roles, benefits, and limitations, as well as considerations for when injectable therapies may be introduced to enhance pain control.
In addition, the program will examine how these therapeutic options can be integrated into a multimodal treatment plan tailored to the individual patient. Attendees will also gain insight into when surgical intervention may be appropriate to address underlying joint pathology and improve long-term outcomes.
Through practical guidance and real-world application, this session aims to support veterinary teams in making informed, evidence-based decisions that optimize pain management strategies and improve overall patient care in canine osteoarthritis.

courses.title: A Journey into Indirect Reference Intervals: New Opportunities from Laboratory Big Data
courses.description:
Reference intervals are fundamental to the clinical interpretation of laboratory results. This presentation will take participants on a journey through historical and emerging concepts in veterinary and human reference interval development, exploring how novel indirect methods can leverage large laboratory datasets to generate representative and clinically relevant reference limits.
We will examine the principles behind indirect reference interval models and discuss how these approaches can be used to improve diagnostic accuracy through the development of breed-, age-, and sex-specific reference intervals. Practical applications will also include the use of indirect methods to verify externally sourced reference intervals within a laboratory's own patient population and support periodical refinement of existing reference limits.
