This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: Urethral Obstruction What We Know and What We Dont Know Yet
courses.description: Urethral obstruction is a common and potentially life threatening emergency in small animal practice and managing these patients can be challenging. This session takes a practical evidence based approach from stabilization to ongoing care. Well cover underlying causes systemic consequences and clinical decision making including cardiovascular assessment management of hyperkalemia and acid base disturbances fluid therapy and analgesia. Procedural techniques such as decompressive cystocentesis urinary catheterization troubleshooting and short term catheter care will be reviewed along with current medication strategies. Youll leave with a clear practical framework to confidently manage urethral obstruction in real world practice.

courses.title: Basic Bone Plating Techniques for Tibia, Radius and Femur Fractures
courses.description: In this workshop, discussion will focus on decision-making for fracture repair of the tibia, femur and radius using bone plates. We will teach instrumentation, plate contouring and application techniques and give valuable practical tips. This course will employ lectures, clinical case presentations and a laboratory repairing created fracture on plastic bone models. Following lecture and case review, participants will repair fractures on plastic bone models.

courses.title: Chronic Complications of Canine Infectious Respiratory Disease (CIRD)
courses.description: Learners in the program will be presented a case-based approach to reviewing chronic complications of canine infectious respiratory disease. Cases will include history, clinical presentations, diagnostics including imaging, videos, and more. A review of CIRD prevention measures, CIRD case evaluation and re-evaluation timelines, including diagnostic work-up recommendations will be reviewed.

courses.title: Feline CKD: Don't Wait for Weight Loss
courses.description: In this session, we will discuss the processes that regulate food intake and outline how these mechanisms are impacted by chronic kidney disease.

courses.title: Making Sense of CBC Dot Plots: From Technology to Clinical Action
courses.description: CBC dot plots provide critical insight into hematology results but theyre often underutilized in clinical practice. This session demystifies how dot plots are generated what normal and abnormal patterns look like and how to translate findings into meaningful diagnostic decisions. Participants will gain confidence in recognizing the limitations of automated results and applying appropriate next steps when abnormalities arise in house blood smear evaluation pathologist evaluation physical or scanned slides or slide free analysis of cellular morphology.

courses.title: SWVS 2026
courses.description: The Southwest Veterinary Symposium will once again welcome those who support veterinary medicine in our region, including DVMs, Technicians, Veterinary Assistants, Practice Managers, Office Staff, Speakers, Sponsors, and Exhibitors. A maximum of 28 CE credit hours are available for the SWVS General Symposium. Additional credit hours are available through the purchase of ticketed events (Interactive Labs, Workshops, Master Classes, and CE Tours).

courses.title: Navigating the cOAst: Current Consensus on Managing Canine Osteoarthritis
courses.description: So many tools in the toolbox for managing OA in dogs! So little guidance on what to utilize, when! Until now! Recent evidence-based Consensus Guidelines have been published to help clinicians make sense of and prioritize various interventions based upon patient risk factors and clinical signs. This presentation will summarize high-level expert opinion regarding OA treatment strategies for dogs, based on the validated Canine Osteoarthritis Staging Tool (COAST), to include a discussion of existing and new therapeutic modalities.

courses.title: Mountain to Sea Veterinary CE and Wellness Retreat - Costa Rica April 2027
courses.description: This program covers subject matter focused in small animal oncology and veterinary wellbeing and is suitable for the general practitioner. We will discuss bridging the oncology gap between general practice and specialty medicine, cytology, canine and feline lymphoma, canine mast cell tumors, measuring quality of life, and navigating emotional load and complex cases in oncology. In the wellbeing arena, this program will discuss true, pseudo-, and poor wellbeing, using practical tools to influence which branch of your autonomic nervous system is dominant, taming imposter syndrome, and converting burnout to buy in. This program will also include 6 hours of online coursework through Get MotiVETed University on topics of wellbeing and suicide prevention basics as veterinary professionals, which will be part of the overall program but will be taken through GMU (these 6 hours are already RACE approved and GMU will provide certificates).
courses.location: Encantada Ocean Cottages, Puntarenas, Costa Rica

courses.title: Advanced Surgical Procedures
courses.description: Come join us for a special 2-day, hands on advanced surgery experience with cadavers. We have designed the course so that you will be able to focus upon expanding your surgical skills and refining your surgical technique. You will watch a demonstration of each procedure before you perform it yourself. Featured procedures include fore and hindlimb amputations, gastropexy, nephrectomy, diaphragmatic hernia repair, salivary gland removal, scrotal urethrostomy in the dog, perineal urethrostomy (PU) in the cat, and anal sacculectomy. We will also discuss basic skin reconstruction techniques, and you will have the opportunity to perform advancement flaps and caudal superficial epigastric flaps. Esophagostomy tube and thoracostomy tube placement will also be reviewed.

courses.title: Regional analgesia of the Head and Neck in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This course is designed to give attendees the basic understanding of local and regional anesthesia for the head and neck in dogs and cats. The didactic portion of the course will include a discussion of local anesthetic pharmacology, additives to local anesthetics and appropriate use of local anesthetics to maximize efficacy while minimizing side effects. The prevention and treatment of LAST will also be discussed. Participants will also be introduced to appropriate landmarks, techniques and complications associated with regional analgesia of the maxilla, mandible, eye, ear and neck. This will include analgesia for procedures involving the oral cavity, nose, eye, ear and neck, with a special focus on oral analgesia. Participants will also be introduced to epidural analgesia at both the lumbosacral and sacrococcygeal injection sites.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Foundations of Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description: Foundations of Veterinary Acupuncture will teach the anatomy of the major points, including neurological, musculoskeletal, fascial, and lymphatic structures associated with each. Comprehensive patient evaluation will be discussed and practiced in depth, including orthopedic, neurological, and myofascial examination.

courses.title: Change as a Pathway to Growth
courses.description: This presentation explores change as a deliberate pathway to growth in veterinary practices focusing on why change feels difficult the hidden cost of staying stagnant and how culture ultimately determines whether new workflows succeed or fail. Using real world veterinary examples and established change management frameworks it helps teams understand the emotional and behavioral dynamics behind resistance reframe discomfort as a signal of progress and align assumptions values and daily behaviors to support adoption. Attendees leave with practical strategies to implement and sustain change building confident adaptable teams improving efficiency and patient care and embedding new ways of working into how we do things here.

courses.title: Feline Infectious Peritonitis: Cracking the FIP Code Diagnosis, Treatment, and Hope
courses.description: Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) remains one of the most challenging diseases in feline practice. This session will help you decode FIP by reviewing its pathophysiology, navigating complex diagnostics, and exploring current and emerging treatment strategies. Learn practical approaches to diagnosis, therapy, and patient monitoring, and gain insight into promising research that may shape the future of FIP management.

courses.title: Going Viral - What's New with FIP, Calicivirus, and FeLV
courses.description: Feline viral diseases have been part of our thought process as veterinarians forever, with not a lot of progress for how we can deal with them. Recent advances in therapy have provided hope and health for so many cats. In this session well talk about how best to approach these challenging infections and what options we have for treatment.

courses.title: The Do's and Don'ts of Canine Otitis Externa
courses.description: Otitis externa is a commonly diagnosed abnormality, affecting up to 20% of dogs. This presentation discusses predisopsing, primary, secondary and perpetuating factors, the diagnostic approach, and rationale treatment for acute and chronic otitis. A detailed review of available treatment options will be presented.

courses.provider: VETERINARY ASSOCIATION FOR FARM ANIMAL WELFARE
courses.title: Immunocastration of Pigs: Welfare Benefits, Industry Adoption, and Practical Lessons from Latin America
courses.description: Immunocastration is increasingly recognized as an effective alternative to surgical castration in pig production, offering significant animal welfare advantages while maintaining productive performance. This webinar will provide an overview of the scientific basis of immunocastration, its welfare and production benefits, and current challenges associated with implementation. Drawing on recent research conducted in Brazil and Colombia, countries with some of the highest adoption rates worldwide, the presentation will explore the motivations, perceived benefits, and barriers influencing on-farm implementation. Practical insights from producers and thought leaders in the production chain will be discussed, highlighting key factors that can facilitate wider adoption of immunocastration in commercial swine production systems.

courses.title: A Complete Introduction to Safety-Focused TPLO
courses.description:
This hybrid course includes 3 comprehensive hours of bite sized online modules that provide valuable tips on pathophysiology of CrCL disease, diagnosis, positioning for TPLO radiographs, preoperative planning, meniscal injury and treatment, and reducing surgical site infections.
Once in our CE lab, you will develop your hands on surgical skills to perform stifle arthrotomy, meniscal treatment, and TPLO using plastic bone models and cadaveric specimens. This is the only TPLO course in North America that supports you each step of the way during and after your training. While here, you will also spend time in insightful radiographic review discussions of your TPLOs before repeating the procedure on your pathway toward mastery.
Ponder this, even if you were trained to fly a Boeing 737, would you pilot a commercial flight without the decision making support of a flight plan, a co pilot, control tower and ground crew? Of course not. So, why would you do a surgery as intricate as TPLO without using a support team to enhance the safety for your patient?
This course trains you to use patient specific pre, intra and post-operative support on your individual TPLO patients. You will learn how to receive case by case preoperative guidance and procedural planning, use patient specific instructions to perform a guided TPLO cut, and to use detailed postoperative critique to shorten your learning curve and more rapidly grow your skills. Curious what this is all about? Better check it out.

courses.title: Ophthalmic Emergencies in Dogs
courses.description: This program will provide foundational, clinically relevant information regarding commonly encountered ophthalmic emergencies in dogs. It is designed to equip veterinary professionals with the knowledge and confidence to recognize, assess, and manage these ophthalmic emergencies. Through a focused exploration of urgent conditions affecting the orbit, adnexa, cornea, and intraocular structures, participants will learn to rapidly identify sight-threatening problems and initiate appropriate interventions. Emphasis will be placed on conditions that are reasonable to manage in practice and when referral should be initiated, if available. The curriculum covers a wide range of critical topics, including orbital and adnexal emergencies such as proptosis and eyelid trauma, corneal ulcers and perforations, acute glaucoma, anterior and posterior lens luxations, and the diagnostic approach to sudden blindness. By the end of the course, learners will be better prepared to stabilize patients, prioritize differential diagnoses, and make timely decisions that preserve comfort and vision. This program is ideal for primary care general practice and emergency veterinarians seeking to strengthen their emergency ophthalmology skills and improve outcomes for canine patients.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Clinical Skills & Applications for the Rehabilitation Therapist
courses.description: A particular focus is identifying orthopedic and neurologic conditions and building an effective therapeutic patient plan. Practical applications of joint mobilization, modalities, therapeutic exercise, neurorehabilitation, pain recognition and assessment, gait patterns and lameness, and pain management are covered. Students get hands-on experience with dogs on-site as they learn how to perform a comprehensive exam and apply rehabilitation techniques.

courses.title: Global FAST Hybrid Online course (AFAST-TFAST, and VetBLUE) with Hands On Live Scanning
courses.description:
The course covers AFAST and its image acquisition, its target-organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and its abdominal fluid scoring system with case-based applications; TFAST and its image acquisition, its echocardiography views, its use for the accurate diagnosis of pleural and pericardial effusion and pneumothorax, its target-organ approach of the heart and pleural space for obvious soft-tissue abnormalities; and Vet BLUE and its image acquisition, its regional, pattern-based approach integrating its B-line scoring system, and 6 lung ultrasound signs. Global FAST is the term used when AFAST, TFAST and Vet BLUE are combined as a single ultrasound format used as an extension of the physical exam. The terms AFAST, TFAST, Vet BLUE and Global FAST are registered service marks for education purposes with the US Patent and Trademark Office to uphold each exam's highest degree of integrity as a standardized ultrasound exam.
The 5-lectures cover AFAST, TFAST, and Vet BLUE, combined called Global FAST, plus a 1-hour Global FAST image acquisition supplemental module (7-hours total of online lectures). Quizzes must be passed with a score of 80% to move on to the next module.
The remote online course above is followed by a live hands on scanning session (4 hour scanning session).

courses.title: IMEX External Skeletal Fixation Level 1: Distal Limb Traumatology
courses.description: An introductory workshop designed to address both routine and challenging fractures of the distal limb using linear and hybrid external skeletal fixation. The course will cover ESF principles and application techniques, patient selection, instrumentation and implants, and postoperative care. Additionally, the workshop discusses the potential complications associated with external skeletal fixation and how to recognize and manage issues that develop in the postoperative convalescent period. Current theory and practice are reinforced through laboratory exercises using plastic bones and cadavers.

courses.title: Fear Free Handling: When to Pause, Pivot, and Reassess
courses.description: Learn how to recognize indicators that signal the need to pause or modify, how to differentiate between situations that require continuation, adjustment, or reassessment and how to apply strategies to pivot handling techniques to support reduced stress and patient safety.

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION CORRECTION: WET LAB (195-37676)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn, build and refine the knowledge and techniques necessary for safe and effective treatment of medial patellar luxation in small breeds of dogs. During the workshop attendees will perform the surgical approach, trochleoplasty, tibial crest transposition and soft tissue balancing techniques on canine cadavers under faculty supervision using a step-by-step high-resolution video demonstration.

courses.title: (LIVE COURSE) Oncological Emergencies in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Cancer patients don't just present for diagnosis associated with chronic illness - they can also present in crisis. This two-week online course will equip you with the skills to both diagnose and manage the acute complications of neoplasia in dogs and cats. You will focus on true emergencies: acute haemorrhage from tumour rupture, life-threatening electrolyte imbalances like hypercalcemia, sepsis from treatment-related neutropaenia, anaphylaxis and tumour lysis syndrome.
You will learn how to prioritize interventions for the oncologic emergency patient, interpret lab results in the context of cancer, and understand when emergency surgery or critical care is the immediate priority over a definitive cancer diagnosis. Guided by current peer-reviewed literature, this course will transform your approach to the acutely deteriorating cancer patient.

courses.title: Exploring Nonclinical Career Pathways in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: In today's rapidly evolving landscape of veterinary medicine, non-clinical career avenues have gained unprecedented significance. This program is designed to guide veterinary professionals - both veterinarians and veterinary technicians - through the transition from clinical to non-clinical roles. Attendees will explore diverse opportunities in industries such as pharmaceuticals, research, academia, government, animal health companies, veterinary journalism, medical writing, and consulting. The session will cover essential strategies for identifying interests and strengths, building a strong foundation, navigating the job search and application process, excelling in interviews, and overcoming common challenges. By leveraging their expertise, veterinary professionals can successfully transition into roles that offer personal growth, professional fulfillment, and improved work-life balance. Join us to unlock new potential in your veterinary career and contribute to innovative solutions in animal health.

courses.title: TIBIAL PLATEAU-LEVELING OSTEOTOMY: WET LAB (195-36639)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn/refine the tibial plateau-leveling osteotomy technique and to understand the major advantages of PAX Polyaxial Locking TPLO Plate System. Participants will perform the TPLO technique on bone models and canine cadavers under faculty supervision. This lab is only for veterinarians who already have a thorough knowledge of the relevant stifle anatomy, extensive stifle surgery experience, and prior training in bone plating techniques and principles.

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION CORRECTION: WET LAB (195-37676)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn, build and refine the knowledge and techniques necessary for safe and effective treatment of medial patellar luxation in small breeds of dogs. During the workshop attendees will perform the surgical approach, trochleoplasty, tibial crest transposition and soft tissue balancing techniques on canine cadavers under faculty supervision using a step-by-step high-resolution video demonstration.

courses.title: 52nd Annual IVAS Congress
courses.description:
The objective of the 52nd Annual IVAS Congress is to provide top quality continuing education which advances the knowledge and skills of veterinarians in the areas of acupuncture, science of acupuncture, research, acupuncture related and East-Asian medical therapy, including Chinese herbal medicine, laser and Chinese food therapies.
Continuing education is provided through live lectures led by presenters known as experts in the field of veterinary acupuncture medicine. Session tracks include small animal and large.
courses.location: Harpa Concert Hall and Conference Center

courses.title: Hematuria: Clearing the Path to Urinary Health (SAIM717)
courses.description: How much should you worry about hematuria? In this course, we'll focus on top differential diagnoses, a diagnostic approach, and long-term management strategies for hematuria in dogs and cats. You'll learn how to distinguish true hematuria, utilize urine sediment analysis and point-of-care ultrasound, identify triggers, and avoid unnecessary antibiotic use, along with emergency stabilization of patients with acute, severe urinary blood loss.

courses.title: ADVANCED TWO DAY CANINE AND FELINE WET LAB
courses.description: This lecture and wet lab will provide the veterinarian with the skills needed to treat the advanced dentistry cases seen in practice. This LIVE wet lab event provides Veterinarians with equipment, specimens, etc.

courses.title: Global FAST Hybrid Online course (AFAST-TFAST, and VetBLUE) with Hands On Live Scanning
courses.description:
The course covers AFAST and its image acquisition, its target-organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and its abdominal fluid scoring system with case-based applications; TFAST and its image acquisition, its echocardiography views, its use for the accurate diagnosis of pleural and pericardial effusion and pneumothorax, its target-organ approach of the heart and pleural space for obvious soft-tissue abnormalities; and Vet BLUE and its image acquisition, its regional, pattern-based approach integrating its B-line scoring system, and 6 lung ultrasound signs. Global FAST is the term used when AFAST, TFAST and Vet BLUE are combined as a single ultrasound format used as an extension of the physical exam. The 5-lectures cover AFAST, TFAST, and Vet BLUE, combined called Global FAST, plus a 1-hour Global FAST image acquisition supplemental module (7-hours total of online lectures). Quizzes must be passed with a score of 80% to move on to the next module.
The remote online course above is followed by a live hands on scanning session (4 hour scanning session).

courses.title: 13th The Gulf-Atlantic Veterinary Conference 2026
courses.description: FVMAs TGAVC 2026 offers continuing education for veterinarians and veterinary technicians through lecture sessions and hands-on wet labs.
courses.location: Fort Lauderdale Marriott Harbor BEACH RESORT & SPA

courses.title: 21st Promoting Excellence Symposium 2026
courses.description: The Florida Association of Equine Practitioners (the equine division of the Florida Veterinary Medical Association) PES 2026 offers continuing education for veterinarians and veterinary technicians/staff through in-person lectures and wet labs to attain required continuing education.

courses.title: Optimal Imaging at VICSD
courses.description:
VICSD Optimal Imaging - Optimal Imaging means providing our best diagnostic imaging (Ultrasound vs CT) and AI-enhanced data disease detection for your patients/pets. It's about analyzing our imaging outside the vacuum because imaging results mean much more when analyzed in the context of all the other pertinent information (from you, the referring veterinarian, pet lab results and VICSD's in-house data). Optimal Imaging is about providing better diagnostics for your pet and giving you a more complete understanding of your pet's health.
I-131 Treatment for hyperthyroid cats: I-131 therapy for hyperthyroid cats provides a cure, replacing daily methimazole therapy. I-131 therapy has been shown to increase life-span of hyperthyroid cats compared to methimazole therapy. Confirmation of hyperthyroidism is recommended via bloodwork and a thyroid scan prior to I-131 treatment. Evaluation of left ventricular wall thickness and left atrial size prior to I-131 therapy is also recommended as a baseline.
courses.location: Veterinary Imaging Center of San Diego

courses.title: VetQuest Travel CE Hopsice & Palliative Care Medicine
courses.description:
This will be over 3 days and include
Saturday 1-2pm: It's Not Just Another 2:00 Euthanasia
Saturday 2:10-3pm: Making the "Comfort" Room Truly Comforting & Experiential
Saturday 5-6pm: Common (and easy!) Integrative Medicine Tools for Your Palliative Care Toolbox
Sunday 11-11:50am: Unraveling Frailty Syndrome: A Clinical Compass for Managing the Aging Patient
Sunday 12-12:50am: Translating Quality of Life: Tools to Guide Clients Through the Toughest Decisions
Monday 11-11:50am: Comfort First: Evolving Strategies for Pain Management in Hospice and Palliative Care
Monday 12-12:50pm: Ketamine in Comfort Care: Case Studies in Veterinary Hospice and Palliative Medicine

courses.title: Complete Compounding Guidance: Balancing Benefits, Managing Risks, and Choosing the Right Pharmacy
courses.description: This 2 hour course will feature two one hour lectures on common drug compounding topics covering risks, providing clinical framework, patient fit criteria and practical guidance on what to look for when partnering with a compounding pharmacy for veterinarians. Part 1 (1 Hour CE): Balancing Benefits and Risks Reviews pros and cons of commonly compounded drugs; delineates risks associated with their use. Provides a framework for evaluating when compounded products are appropriate and criteria to ensure a compounded preparation best fits an individual patient's needs. Compounded Medications, Part 2 (1 Hour CE): Risky Dosage Forms Defines characteristics that render certain dosage forms high risk, with an emphasis on additional considerations for transdermal compounds. Concludes with practical guidance on what to look for when selecting a compounding pharmacy.

courses.title: Complete Compounding Guidance: Balancing Benefits, Managing Risks, and Choosing the Right Pharmacy

Part 1 (1 Hour CE): Balancing Benefits and Risks Reviews pros and cons of commonly compounded drugs; delineates risks associated with their use. courses.title: Invasive Aspergillosis and Other Invasive Mold Infections in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: This presentation will include discussion on the epidemiology, clinical findings, diagnosis, treatment and treatment monitoring of sino-nasal, sino-orbital, and systemic aspergillosis in dogs and cats. Other invasive mold infections will also be discussed, where appropriate.

courses.title: The 41st Muller-Ihrke-Kwochka Veterinary Dermatology Seminar, The 26th Veterinary MEDicine Seminar & The JOINT Meeting
courses.description: VETS presents 13.5 CE Units in Dermatology from Board Certified DVMs and 13.5 CE Units in Internal Medicine (also Board Certified DVMs)-- this year with an emphasis on Brachycephalic Issues, Small Animal Ophthalmology and Diseases and Aging of the Cat. Attendees may choose the Dermatology Track or the MEDicine Track or BOTH-- which is what we call The JOINT Meeting.

courses.title: Biennial Inventory: Your DEA Recordkeeping Baseline
courses.description:
If the Drug Enforcement Administration ("DEA") shows up to conduct an inspection or audit, one of the FIRST documents they will request to review is your most recent biennial inventory. Your ability to produce a current, accurate, biennial inventory documentation upon request has the power to start a DEA visit off with success...or distress (if you have not completed one).
Completing a biennial inventory is a federal requirement and matter of regulatory inspection readiness that ALL DEA registrants ordering and maintaining a controlled substance inventory must adhere to every two years (at minimum). The Biennial inventory sets the baseline for all controlled substances on hand. Still, confusion persists over the biennial inventory process, what it is, why it matters, and how to properly perform and document it.
This 50-minute webinar provides a practical overview and step-by-step guide to understanding and properly executing upon DEA biennial inventory requirements to ensure regulatory inspection readiness. Participants will learn why conducting "inventory" and "DEA biennial inventory" are not synonymous processes, including what constitutes "on-hand" stock, when to count, how to properly document biennial inventory, and how to avoid common, costly mistakes. Navigating proper separation of drug schedules and state-only scheduled drugs on inventory documentation will also be covered, followed by best practices for implementing processes and systems that support a stress-free, consistent biennial inventory trail. Webinar content will be presented in the following four key areas:
1. DEA Registrant: Who is required to physically conduct biennial inventory. What aspects of biennial inventory are "delegable". Understanding the role of witnesses and individuals to whom power of attorney has been granted within the biennial inventory process.
2. Biennial Documentation (Paper): The DEA provides biennial inventory regulatory requirements, not a template. How biennial inventor

courses.title: Everyones Least Favorite Appointment: The Cat Whos Urinating Out of the Box
courses.description: Is it the cats bladder or brain? In this session, well discuss the best ways to approachout of box urination. From signalment to diagnostics and treatment, youll leave this session ready to face thenext cat presented for this problem, armed with tools to make the most effective and appropriate treatmentrecommendations.

courses.provider: PURPLE MOON HERBS AND STUDIES, LLC
courses.title: Wholistic Pain Management and Rehabilitation
courses.description: This course will introduce an integrative approach to pain management and rehabilitation. We will learn to incorporate herbal medications, acupuncture, and other rehabilitation modalities in addition to conventional allopathic pharmaceuticals. We invite you to join us in the beautiful Outer Banks of North Carolina and enjoy the beach while learning about pain management and rehabilitation in animals. The beaches are beautiful and serene, wonderful restaurants abound and there are plenty of other activities throughout the barrier islands. Visit the Corolla Wild Horses or Jenette's Pier, walk through one of the nature preserves or on the beach, or just sunbathe and shop. Continental breakfast is included each morning. Lectures include an overview of the multimodal approach to pain management in which we look at the whole animal - body, mind, and spirit. The wholistic exam including the history and findings are the stepping off point that will help guide patient recommendations and treatments. We will have more in-depth discussions regarding the theory behind common modalities found in rehabilitation medicine as well as how and when to utilize these for your patients. There will be in depth discussions on herbs that are utilized in pain management and palliative medicine specifically, but also in the general support of chronically ill and geriatric animals. There will be an organoleptic portion to these lectures to see and taste the herbs in tea, dried and tinctured forms. We will discuss how the herbs can be used as safe, effective alternatives to non-steroidals and the differences in the body's physiologic response to both. To tie everything together, we will review specific cases of various conditions, as well as cases that incorporate a variety of the above modalities

courses.title: Veterinary Anaesthesia and Analgesia Mentorship Program
courses.description:
The Veterinary Anaesthesia and Analgesia Mentorship Program is a comprehensive, postgraduate-level continuing education course designed to guide small-animal veterinarians from foundational principles of safe anaesthesia to confident clinical application.
The program runs from September 2026 through May 2027 and is delivered across multiple European locations. It combines on-site teaching, simulation-based training, supervised practical experience, and continuous online mentorship to ensure progressive learning, consolidation of skills between modules, and durable clinical competence.
Across five modules, participants progress from equipment checks, monitoring, thermoregulation, and ventilation to pharmacology and protocol design, peri-operative pain management and cardiopulmonary cerebral resuscitation (RECOVER-based), loco-regional techniques, and the recognition and management of anaesthetic complications in patients with common comorbidities. The program concludes with a summative theory and practical examination using a simulator-based format.
Practical training is delivered through an ethically robust framework, including high-fidelity simulation scenarios (e.g., changes in heart rate, blood pressure, capnography, and oxygenation), task training using phantoms, cadaver-based anatomical and block technique training, and a welfare-positive live clinical module involving routine canine castration of shelter animals in collaboration with local partners. All live-animal practical activities are performed under direct veterinary supervision and in accordance with local legislation and welfare standards.
The overarching goal of the program is to enable veterinarians to plan and conduct anaesthesia safely, interpret monitoring trends accurately, anticipate and manage complications promptly, and implement effective analgesic strategies and resuscitation protocols aligned with current best practice.

courses.title: The Hospital Environment, Part 1: Exploring Sensory Exposure
courses.description: This is the first lecture in a two-part series that does a deep dive into real, physical, objective environment in which we work as veterinary professionals. We will explore the external environment in terms of sensory exposure, and the internal environment in terms of culture.

courses.title: Matching Diet to Disease: Dietary Strategies for Gastrointestinal Disease
courses.description:
This webinar will focus on discussing the different nutritional strategies for the management of gastrointestinal disease, focusing on acute gastroenteritis and pancreatitis. We will also talk about the different dietary options for these conditions and how to choose the right diet for each case.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Hydrolyzed Diets in the Management of Dermatologic Diseases
courses.description:
In this webinar, Dr. Noli will discuss many aspects of hydrolyzed diets, including how they are produced; why, how, and when they should be used; how to choose the best diet; and the expected benefits for both the skin and the gut.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: New Concepts in Minimally Invasive and Interventional Approaches to Chylothorax
courses.description: This 1.5-hr course will present the newest information in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and other interventional approaches regarding small animal chylothorax from two experts in the field. This will be an interactive webinar with designated a questions and answers session.

courses.title: Improving Mobility in the Aging Patient
courses.description: This lecture will focus on the aging canine and feline patient, and how to assess for sarcopenia and mobility impairment with an emphasis on preserving muscle health, mobility, and quality of life. Multimodal therapy and client education related to the aging patient will be emphasized.

courses.title: Case Rounds: Diagnostic Strategy for the Vomiting Dog and Cat LIVE
courses.description: In this course learners will work through acute and chronic vomiting presentations in dogs and cats while strengthening clinical reasoning, prioritizing differential diagnoses, interpreting diagnostic findings, developing treatment plans, and navigating client communication. The program emphasizes practical decision-making and evidence-based approaches that participants can immediately incorporate into everyday small animal practice.

courses.title: VetQuest Glacier Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
courses.description: This conference will be over 3 days and cover topics related to Orthopedic Medicine & Surgery as well as Physical therapy/Rehab for small animals

courses.title: Chronic Pain for the General Practitioner: Identification, Monitoring, and What's New in Treatment Options for Dogs and Cat
courses.description: This lecture is designed to introduce the General Practitioner to pain management in companion animals. Specifically, it will address the difficulties and nuances in identifying pain in dogs and cats, methods to obtain history and utilize clues from the physical exam to confirm the existence of pain and help localize it, and the selection of appropriate treatments. Furthermore, the general practitioner will gain insight into how to set up a pain management game plan with owners. This "treat and track" approach helps to ensure early intervention and knowing when to refer. Physiology of pain, the nociceptive pathway, and how to design a pain management protocol utilizing this knowledge will be discussed. Currently available pharmaceuticals as well as physical modalities will be presented.

courses.title: Stabilization of the ECC Patient in General Practice
courses.description: This lecture will discuss common emergencies that present to general practice. It will include stabilization, diagnostics and immediate interventions and treatments of these emergencies and when the ideal time is to transfer to a referral hospital. It will also discuss a team approach to these situations between doctors and veterinary technicians. Examples of the common emergencies that will be discussed include patients that have sustained trauma, GI foreign bodes and other GI diseases, pyometra, GDV, and spontaneous hemorrhage (hemoabdomen/pericardial effusion).

courses.title: Vacuolar Hepatopathy in Dogs
courses.description: Increases in serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity are a common finding in dogs with or without clinical illness. These increases often signal the presence of vacuolar (glycogen and/or lipid ) in the liver. This lecture will provide an algorithm to use in investigating the underlying cause of vacuolar change in the liver with range from endocrine disorders, acquired liver disease, drug induction or as a consequence of primary gastrointestinal disease or neoplasia in the splanchnic bed. Special attention will be given to the consequences of corticosteroid induction of vacuolar changes. Finally what is known about the pathology and clinical sequela of the idiopathic vacuolar hepatopathy that occurs in Scottish Terriers, Miniature Schnauzers, Shih Tzus and occasionally mixed breed dogs will be discussed.

courses.title: VetQuest Travel CE Behavior
courses.description:
This will be over 3 days and include:
I know it's normal, but how do I make it stop? Managing normal but unwanted behaviors in cats
Feline elimination problems
Understanding Canine Aggression Concepts & Examples
Puppy socialization or infectious disease prevention - we can have both!
Psychopharmacology Daily Drugs & Event Meds
Chemical Restraint and handling for difficult dogs in the clinic

courses.title: Traveling Vet Retreats Paris France 2026
courses.description: Traveling Vet Retreats provides destination continuing education conferences for veterinarians. We host small group lectures with boarded specialists in unique, once in a lifetime locations. Attendees also have the opportunity to participate in group yoga sessions and a relaxing group trip after completing 15 hours of continuing education.

courses.provider: PHOENIX VETERINARY SURGICAL SPECIALISTS & ACUTEVET KANSAS CITY
courses.title: Veterinary Electrochemotherapy: Scientific Training & Clinical Applications
courses.description: This 24.0 hour online seminar series will feature 24 online powerpoint sessions, 24 quizzes, over 36 chapters and articles required reading materials, and four two-hour interactive practical online sessions. The course will provide a comprehensive overview of electrochemotherapy (ECT) in canines and felines.

courses.title: Spill the proTEIn. An Update on Proteinuria Management
courses.description:
This will provide a review of current management protocols for
proteinuria. We will discuss the pathophysiology and etiologies of proteinuria development as well as recommendations for adjunctive diagnostics, dietary management, medication protocols, and follow up guidelines.

courses.title: Leadership in the Trenches: Managing Up and Down
courses.description: Middle managers in veterinary medicine face the unique challenge of balancing the needs of their team with the expectations of higher up hospital leadership. This lecture discusses the communication skills, consistent expectations, frequent feedback needs and understanding of both the team and hospital leadership in order to succeed in the role. Effective leadership depends on balancing both directions: advocating for the team while contributing to hospital-wide goals, fostering collaboration, and maintaining transparency.

courses.title: 2026 EDPA CONTINUING EDUCATION CONFERENCE
courses.description: Annual continuing education program structured for veterinarians, vet techs, and equine dental practitioners.

courses.title: Feline Low Stress Handling in a Shelter Environment (LIVE)
courses.description: Cats are not small dogs. They have a lower tolerance for frustration and a much shorter window before physical restraint stops helping and starts causing harm. Feline Low Stress Handling meets cats where they are. This session offers practical, in-the-moment applications for shelter veterinary exams: reading the feline communication signaling, from fear to frustration, applying the 2-second rule and the least-restraint principle, adjusting the examination approach to the individual, and creating a low stress environment.

courses.title: VetQuest Grand Cayman Anesthesia & Neurology
courses.description: This conference will be over 3 days and cover anesthesia & neurology topics in small animals.

courses.title: All Paws In: Why Inclusive Teams Are More Resilient, Skilled, and Connected
courses.description: Even strong team members can falter when they feel they don't belong, their contributions don't matter, or they aren't safe asking questions or sharing ideas. These situations are rarely intentional, but their impact is real. Step into the shoes of a team member who's quietly struggling and explore the key moments shaping their experience. Identify what went wrong, what could have gone differently, and which inclusive behaviors help lift the whole team. Discover how to create a workplace where everyone feels welcome to learn, grow, and thrive.

courses.title: Managing Obesity in Patients with Comorbid Conditions: A Case-Based Approach
courses.description: This case-based course reviews the management of obesity in dogs and cats with concurrent disease. Participants will follow two patients from initial assessment through long-term management. The program will discuss species-specific considerations in weight management, selection of appropriate therapeutic diets, necessary calculations, and monitoring strategies. Emphasis will be placed on developing individualized weight-loss plans, implementing nutritional interventions, and troubleshooting common challenges encountered during treatment. Attendees will gain practical strategies for managing obesity in medically complex patients and optimizing long-term outcomes.

courses.title: The Constipated Cat: From Backed up to Back on Track
courses.description: A comprehensive discussion on acute and chronic management strategies for feline constipation. Techniques including the use of polyethylene glycol (PEG 3350) administered as a constant rate infusion via nasoesophageal tube in the acutely obstipated patient will be shared. Additionally, using a case-based approach, we will discuss how the use of fiber and diet therapy can help with chronic management and prevention.

courses.title: Practical Management of Acute Diarrhea in Dogs: The Role of Probiotics and Fiber
courses.description: This course reviews practical approaches to managing acute diarrhea in dogs with an emphasis on the use of probiotics and fiber supplementation. Participants will learn when to consider these therapies and what outcomes to expect in general practice. The session highlights current evidence, clinical recommendations, and real-world case applications.

courses.title: Behavioral or Medical: Are They One in the Same?
courses.description: This presentation examines the medical contributors to common behavioral presentations in dogs and cats. A change in behavior is often the first sign of an underlying medical condition. Using a case-based approach, this 90-minute presentation will cover common behavior conditions such as aggression, separation-related behaviors, noise phobias, compulsive behaviors and age-related behavioral changes along with how to diagnose and treat them.

courses.title: Paws and Plan: Mastering Time and Delegation in Veterinary Medicine LIVE
courses.description: Few of us have extra time within our days. This session aims to help veterinary professionals enhance time management and delegation skills for improved efficiency and wellness. You will learn key strategies, including prioritization, scheduling, and using tools such as the Eisenhower Matrix and Pomodoro technique. Delegation is addressed as a crucial part of time management, with a focus on choosing the right person, providing clear expectations, and fostering empowerment through shared responsibility. The importance of operational efficiency is highlighted, showing that streamlining processes can lead to higher productivity and revenue. The presentation encourages participants to reflect on their current practices, overcome resistance to delegation, and create systems to ensure long-term success.

courses.title: Focused In-Clinic Focused Ultrasound, Radiography, and Computed Tomography Training
courses.description: This course will provide personalized in-clinic instruction for basic through advanced ultrasound, radiography and computed tomography to veterinarians and veterinary technicians. Each day session will allow attendees to complete abdominal, non-cardiac and musculoskeletal ultrasounds, thoracic, abdominal, spinal and musculoskeletal radiography, and computed tomography (skull, spine, thorax, abdomen, musculoskeletal) under the guidance of an ACVR Diplomate. Participant skill level will be confirmed by the instructor and targeted guidance to refine and improve diagnostic ultrasound, radiography and computed tomography skills will be provided.

courses.title: Traveling Vet Retreats Maine
courses.description: Traveling Vet Retreats provides destination continuing education conferences for veterinarians. We host small group lectures with boarded specialists in unique, once in a lifetime locations. Attendees also have the opportunity to participate in group yoga sessions and a relaxing group trip after completing 15 hours of continuing education.

courses.title: Advanced Abdominal
courses.description: Advanced Small Animal Ultrasound is designed for veterinarians and technicians with an intermediate level of ultrasound experience. Emphasis is on advanced ultrasound of the abdomen with particular focus on small and superficial structures, the use of Doppler, and optimization of technical parameters to maximize image quality. Limited enrollment and 3 participants per ultrasound station ensure dedicated instruction and ample scanning time. The highest quality ultrasound equipment will be used for the course.

courses.title: Practical Oncology for General Practice: Common Tumors in Dogs and Cats: What to Do, When to Refer, and How to Help
courses.description: This presentation will provide a practical, general-practice-focused approach to managing common tumors in dogs and cats, including mast cell tumors, urothelial tumors, mammary tumors and soft tissue sarcomas. For each tumor type, it will review typical presenting signs, appropriate diagnostics and staging that can be performed in GP, and guidance on case management when referral is not pursued. Emphasis will be placed on supportive care, quality-of-life discussions, clear referral decision points, and effective client communication around diagnosis, prognosis and treatment options.

courses.title: VetQuest Puerto Rico Emergency & Critical Care Conference 2027
courses.description: This conference will cover 3 days on topics related to Emergency Critical Care in small animals.

courses.title: Nutritional management of acute vomiting and diarrhea
courses.description: Vomiting and diarrhea are two of the main reasons owners bring their pets to the hospital. It is important for veterinary team members to identify these clinical signs and ascertain a complete history and evaluation regarding these frequent signs in presenting pets. Nutritional management is a crucial part of therapy in the management of vomiting and or diarrhea. Specific key nutritional factors play a role in managing vomiting and diarrhea in cats and dogs through enteral and parenteral nutrition and veterinary technicians should recognize the circumstances and reasoning for the KNFs to ensure a positive outcome for the vomiting and diarrheic patient.

courses.title: After the Error: How Veterinary Teams Respond and Recover
courses.description:
This program gives veterinary hospital leaders a practical framework for responding to medical error within their teams. Grounded in just culture and patient safety research from both veterinary and human medicine, the session treats error as a team and system event rather than an individual failing. Participants will learn to lead the response in the first hours after an error is identified, disclose to clients honestly while protecting the client relationship, support the team member involved (often called the second victim), and build the psychological safety and reporting culture that helps prevent the next error. The session is anchored by a take-home response playbook and quick-reference checklist that leaders can adapt and use in their own hospitals.
Keywords: medical error, just culture, patient safety, psychological safety, error disclosure, second victim, root cause analysis, error reporting, veterinary teams, leadership.

courses.title: Managing the Emotions Around the Human-Animal-Bond
courses.description: Taking time to understand and develop the skill for conflict management in vet med is critical to the path in truly honoring the human-animal-bond. The emotions related to the human-animal-bond can be strong. These emotions are repeatedly the fuel in which drive individuals through great sacrifice to be a part of the veterinary profession. While also being the reason for clients, and ourselves, to be triggered thereby creating these moments of conflict. When individuals feel they are failing to support the bond, they often look on where to send the shame. Frequently leading people into a space of judgment, both internally and externally. Unfortunately, when clients follow this path, the veterinary professional is not uncommonly on the receiving end of an undeserving focus of anger and frustration. Learning to navigate these moments is imperative in partnering with others in the shared end goal of helping animals. Understanding the emotions related to conflict is the first step in recognizing the path to a common solution through these conflicts. Finding ways to embrace the emotions from both ourselves and the other party involved, brings sustainability within the profession. Staying connected to a common goal to support the human-animal-bond allows for longevity in the well-being of all involved.

courses.title: The 41st Muller-Ihrke-Kwochka Veterinary Dermatology Seminar, The 26th Veterinary MEDicine Seminar & The JOINT Meeting
courses.description: VETS presents 13.5 CE Units in Dermatology from Board Certified DVMs and 13.5 CE Units in Internal Medicine (also Board Certified DVMs)-- this year with an emphasis on Brachycephalic Issues, Small Animal Ophthalmology and Diseases and Aging of the Cat. Attendees may choose the Dermatology Track or the MEDicine Track or BOTH-- which is what we call The JOINT Meeting.

courses.title: Update on Canine Osteoarthritis: Recognition, Assessment and Management 2026
courses.description: Stay current on the latest evidence-based approaches to diagnosing and managing canine osteoarthritis in this live veterinary CE webinar. This session reviews the most up-to-date concepts in osteoarthritis recognition, assessment, staging and treatment. Learn how to effectively apply the Canine Osteoarthritis Staging Tool (COAST) in clinical practice, optimize NSAID use for long-term patient management, and explore anti-NGF monoclonal antibody therapy, including current applications and ongoing controversies. Gain practical strategies you can immediately implement to improve mobility, comfort and quality of life for your canine patients.

courses.title: Heritage Vet Partners Cattle First Summit
courses.description: This program is being offered to provide a range of continuing education topics to practitioners in the Heritage Vet Partners Group. Topics will include research updates on transboundary animal diseases, bovine respiratory updates, clinic best practices in relation to necropsies, and personnel management issues specifically related to bridging generational gaps in practice teams.

courses.title: From Itch to Insight: Practical Updates on Food Allergies
courses.description: This continuing education program provides an evidence-based review of adverse food reactions and food allergies in dogs and cats. The lecture will discuss common clinical presentations, diagnostic approaches, elimination diet trials, and long-term management strategies for veterinary patients with suspected food allergies. Additional focus will be placed on improving client compliance, reducing caregiver burden, and selecting appropriate dietary therapies using current veterinary dermatology literature and clinical recommendations.

courses.title: Don't Poison Man's Best Friend: Medication Poisonings in Canines
courses.description: While many pharmaceuticals are used in multiple species, they do not always provide themsame effects or have the same margin of safety. This session will provide veterinarians and veterinary technicians information regarding unique characteristics of the canine species in regards to ADME and therapy needs. With this, attendees will be able to better recognize differences in prescribing methods. We will also discuss 3-4 common human medication poisonings in canines through case examples.

courses.title: Practical cardiology for the general practitioner
courses.description: In this CE qualified 60 minute lecture we make veterinary cardiology easy to understand and fun. Cardiac issues are very common in pets with approximately 1o percent of the dogs veterinarians evaluate experiencing heart disease. We will discuss many of the common cardiology scenarios that pets present in everyday practice. We will provide you easy to understand and executable plans to help pets live long and happy lives. Our goal is for everyone involved in the case to truly understand the big picture of what is going on, what signs to look for and what to expect. Some of the specific cardiology scenarios we will be discussing include congestive heart failure in little dogs, big dogs and feline patients, degenerative valve disease vs DCM, HCM, pulmonary hypertension and common arrhythmias. And we promise to make cardiology fun

courses.title: Advanced Echocardiography
courses.description:
This is an immersive three-day course focused on advanced echocardiography. Lectures cover scanning, echocardiographic diagnosis, using Echo for disease staging, and principles of patient management. It will cover advanced aspects of imaging and cardiovascular medicine. Two scanning laboratory periods will help participants with their own imaging challenges or learn new techniques. The course does not review ultrasound basics or physics (aside from how these relate to instrumentation, obtaining quality images, and recognizing artifacts).
Participants will learn how to integrate imaging with aspects of medical management, while building a stronger understanding of clinical cardiology and echocardiographic diagnosis.

courses.title: Hill's 2025 State of Shelter Pet Adoption Report: Trends and Opportunities
courses.description: This 1 hour webinar will provide an overview of insights from Hill's 2025 State of Shelter Pet Adoption Report. The session will explore current trends and opportunities in animal sheltering, discuss challenges facing shelter professionals, and touch on innovative approaches being adopted across the industry. The program is designed for veterinary professionals and others interested in the landscape of shelter pet adoption. A portion of the session will be dedicated to participant questions and discussion.

courses.title: AAEP XP Series NeuroXP
courses.description: This intensive two-day program provides equine practitioners with practical, clinically focused training in the diagnosis and management of neurologic disease in horses. Through a combination of preparatory materials, targeted lectures, interactive case discussions, and extensive hands-on laboratory sessions, participants develop a structured approach to neurologic examination, neurolocalization, diagnostic planning, and treatment decision-making. Learning will include foundational concepts, diagnostic interpretation, and hands-on skills using live horses, cadavers, and imaging modalities with advanced case-based discussions, procedural training, and real-world clinical scenarios, including client communication and risk management. Small-group laboratories and expert faculty guidance ensure individualized instruction and immediate clinical applicability, enabling participants to confidently assess, diagnose, and manage complex equine neurologic cases in practice.

courses.title: RVG Diarrhea! Case Rounds: LIVE
courses.description: Join Dr. Gershon Alaluf for an interactive case-based discussion exploring the diagnostic and treatment approaches to diarrhea across various life stages. Using real-world examples, participants will refine their clinical reasoning, improve client communication, and strengthen decision-making skills for patients with acute and chronic diarrhea.

courses.title: The role of nutrition and feeding strategies for cats with FIC
courses.description:
Using clinical case examples, this Collaborative Care webinar will focus on nutrition as a component of multimodal management of feline idiopathic cystitis (FIC), including research related to dietary strategies used in the management of FIC, as well as hydration and feeding behavior strategies that optimize the indoor environment. Topics will include an overview of FIC pathophysiology and its impact on the human-animal bond, along with evidence-based nutritional strategies that support cats with chronic lower urinary tract disease. Discussion will focus on the role of therapeutic urinary diets, practical methods for increasing hydration, and feeding and environmental strategies that align with Multimodal Environmental Modification (MEMO).
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion

courses.title: Optimizing Use of Hydrolyzed and Amino Acid-Based Diets
courses.description:
This Collaborative Care webinar will provide an overview of how hydrolyzed and amino acid-based pet foods are produced, including variations in base protein, type, and degree of hydrolysis and how this may affect digestibility, and the gastrointestinal immune response. An overview of how amino acid-based diets differ from hydrolyzed diets will also be discussed. Presenters will then discuss clinical cases for which hydrolyzed, or amino acid-based diets are indicated, discussing the indications for each. The cases will reinforce the applications of hydrolyzed diet, the scientific basis for more than one hydrolyzed diet trials for specific cases (such as suspected food allergies), and when amino acid-based diets are indicated.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Veterinary Laser Therapy in Clinical Practice: Science, Safety, and Applications in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description:
Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) is a type of laser therapy increasingly utilized in veterinary medicine as an adjunctive modality in a variety of situations, including pain management, inflammatory conditions, wound healing, and rehabilitation. This continuing education course provides a practical overview of PBMT and its clinical application in veterinary patients.
Participants will review the biologic and physics of PBMT, including wavelength, power density, energy dosage, and proposed mechanisms of action at the cellular and tissue levels. Current veterinary literature will be discussed to evaluate the indications and therapeutic effects of PBMT across common clinical scenarios.
The course will address practical considerations for clinical use of PBMT, including patient selection, treatment protocols, safety standards, and contraindications. Common applications such as musculoskeletal pain, osteoarthritis, wound management, and post-operative care will be presented to illustrate appropriate integration into veterinary practice. Additionally, the course shares newer modalities for the use of PBMT, including internal medicine usage, allergic dermatitis, as well as dental disease.
Designed for both veterinarians and veterinary technicians, this course emphasizes safe, ethical, and informed use of PBMT while supporting interprofessional collaboration within the veterinary healthcare team.

courses.title: From Chaos to Control: Strategic Planning for Veterinary Practices; Part 3
courses.description:
From Chaos to Control: Strategic Planning for Veterinary Practices is a three-part, live webinar program designed to help veterinary leaders transition from reactive daily operations to intentional, sustainable practice leadership. Delivered as a progressive learning series, each session builds upon the previous to guide participants through the foundational elements of strategic planning, team alignment, operational accountability, and long-term organizational resilience.
Veterinary medicine often operates in a constant state of urgency, leaving little time for proactive planning or leadership development. This program provides practical frameworks and actionable strategies to help veterinary professionals clarify priorities, improve communication, strengthen culture, enhance team utilization, and create measurable organizational goals that support both financial health and team well-being.
Participants will learn how to identify barriers that prevent practices from achieving strategic alignment, translate vision into daily operational behaviors, and develop systems that create accountability, adaptability, and long-term sustainability. The program is designed specifically for veterinary professionals seeking practical tools that can immediately be applied within clinical practice settings.
Attendees must complete all three sessions to receive continuing education credit, as each session builds upon the concepts and application work introduced in prior sessions.

courses.title: Veterinary Ventures CE Acadia 2026
courses.description: This course covers two specialty topics commonly encountered by the general practitioner & ER veterinarian - Emergency/Critical Care and Internal Medicine. Dr. Megan McClosky will discuss CKD, FIP, and managing comorbidities in older patients. Dr. Katie Mauro will discuss AKI and maternal and neonatal emergencies. This will be an interactive medical presentation. This is a 3 day conference that will provide 15 hours of RACE approved CE credits.

courses.title: The 41st Muller-Ihrke-Kwochka Veterinary Dermatology Seminar, The 26th Veterinary MEDicine Seminar & The JOINT Meeting
courses.description: VETS presents 13.5 CE Units in Dermatology from Board Certified DVMs and 13.5 CE Units in Internal Medicine (also Board Certified DVMs)-- this year with an emphasis on Brachycephalic Issues, Small Animal Ophthalmology and Diseases and Aging of the Cat. Attendees may choose the Dermatology Track or the MEDicine Track or BOTH-- which is what we call The JOINT Meeting.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Comorbidities in Cats
courses.description:
Nutritional management is critical in managing feline disease conditions. The diets role in these nutrient sensitive conditions vary, as diet may be a primary intervention or hold a supportive management role. Cats presenting with multiple concurrent disease conditions exhibit an added degree of clinical complexity. These comorbidities frequently occur in senior feline patients, as multiple diseases demonstrate increased prevalence with advancing age in cats. These disease conditions include chronic kidney disease, joint disease, cognitive dysfunction, neoplasia, and endocrinopathies.
Selecting the most suitable diet for a feline patient involves thoroughly evaluating their nutritional needs, understanding the nutrients involved in managing disease conditions, and knowledge of nutritional profiles available in helping to manage the disease conditions.

courses.title: Clinical approach to chronic enteropathy in the dog
courses.description:
Chronic GI disease is common in dogs and can be a frustrating issue for both owners and veterinarians. This lecture will discuss updates from the recent ACVIM-endorsed guidelines on chronic inflammatory enteropathy in dogs. Attendees will develop an understanding of diagnostic testing and therapeutic trials for management of chronic
inflammatory enteropathy.

courses.title: Communication Principles
courses.description: This training is designed to equip veterinary professionals and leaders with foundational communication knowledge and skills to improve collaboration, team effectiveness, and workplace interactions within veterinary practice settings. Participants will review core communication principles, learn techniques to improve clarity and engagement, and explore strategies to strengthen professional communication in high-paced veterinary environments.

courses.title: Navigating Parvovirus: Updates, Challenges, and Innovations
courses.description: This lecture will provide a comprehensive update on parvovirus, focusing on recent research, diagnostic advancements, and evolving treatment strategies in critical care settings. Topics will include epidemiological trends, emerging variants, novel therapeutic approaches, and the latest clinical guidelines for managing severe cases. Attendees will gain valuable insights into recognizing and treating parvoviral infections, particularly in immunocompromised patients and high-risk populations. Case studies and real-world applications will be discussed to enhance clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.

courses.title: Tricks and Treats: Tasty Tales from the Palatable Pharmacy
courses.description: As the human-animal bond has evolved through time, so too has veterinary care and creative patient management. Among other practice evolutions, our veterinary pharmacies have grown to include a myriad of well targeted drugs in an array of formulations to accommodate ease of administration for our animal owners. Through a case-based approach, this presentation will discuss the toxicological consequences of palatable and flavored veterinary pharmaceutical overdoses. We'll more closely assess the consequences and management of flavored or chewable oclacitinib maleate (Apoquel), NSAID, antibiotic, phenylpropanolamine (PPA, Proin), and joint supplement overdose ingestions.

courses.title: Senior Pet Con
courses.description: Senior Pet Con is the first event to bring the whole world of senior pet care together: pet parents and the veterinarians who care for their animals. It's virtual and runs across two days. Day One is built for pet parents, so they can learn from expert vets without leaving their pet's side. Day Two is continuing education for veterinarians so they can get better at caring for nearly half their patients without travel, cost, or missed time in clinic. It's led by Dr. Monica Tarantino, a senior dog veterinarian and co-founder of the Senior Dog Veterinary Society, and Adam Greenbaum, founder of WhiskerCloud and Love, Baxter. Nearly half the pets in this country are seniors. This is the event built for them.

courses.title: AAEP XP Series: DentistryXP (TX)
courses.description: This intensive two-day program provides equine practitioners with practical, clinically focused training in the diagnosis and management of neurologic disease in horses. Through a combination of preparatory materials, targeted lectures, interactive case discussions, and extensive hands-on laboratory sessions, participants develop a structured approach to neurologic examination, neurolocalization, diagnostic planning, and treatment decision-making. Learning will include foundational concepts, diagnostic interpretation, and hands-on skills using live horses, cadavers, and imaging modalities with advanced case-based discussions, procedural training, and real-world clinical scenarios, including client communication and risk management. Small-group laboratories and expert faculty guidance ensure individualized instruction and immediate clinical applicability, enabling participants to confidently assess, diagnose, and manage complex equine neurologic cases in practice.

courses.title: The Hidden Cost of Masking: Neurodiversity, Mental Health, and Being Unseen LIVE
courses.description: Veterinary professionals are often expected to be calm under pressure, highly capable, emotionally resilient and endlessly adaptable. But for many neurodivergent individuals, meeting these expectations can require a tremendous amount of invisible effort through masking. Masking can help people stay employed, avoid judgment, and feel safer in environments that were not built with their needs in mind. Over time, though, masking can come at a significant cost. This CE webinar explores why neurodivergent professionals feel forced to hide their true selves, how this obscures mental health struggles, and how we can redesign our teams to be truly supportive, safe spaces where everyone can thrive without pretending. The program is especially relevant in the context of suicide prevention and awareness.

courses.title: Periodontal Disease Review
courses.description: This will be a 1 hour lecture to veterinarians with an emphasis on periodontal disease diagnosis and treatments in dogs and cats. We will review current theory and also discuss new treatments available.

courses.title: The Purr-fect Balance of Nutrition and Weight Management in Cats
courses.description: Feline obesity is a common and preventable nutritional disorders in veterinary medicine. This lecture will provide an overview of the pathophysiology of obesity, emphasizing the metabolic, hormonal, and behavioral factors that contribute to excessive weight gain. This presentation will review the nutritional requirements and formulation principles underlying effective feline weight loss strategies, including caloric restriction, macronutrient balance, and satiety management. The session will also examine commercially available therapeutic diets, highlighting their key nutritional features, indications, and clinical outcomes. By integrating physiological understanding with practical dietary planning, participants will be equipped to develop individualized and sustainable weight management programs for feline patients.

courses.title: Traveling Vet Retreats Thailand
courses.description: Traveling Vet Retreats provides destination continuing education conferences for veterinarians. We host small group lectures with boarded specialists in unique, once in a lifetime locations. Attendees also have the opportunity to participate in group yoga sessions and a relaxing group trip after completing 15 hours of continuing education.

courses.title: Why Cats Are Not Small Humans: Medication Poisoning in Felines
courses.description: While many pharmaceuticals are used in multiple species, they do not always provide the same effects or have the same margin of safety. This session will provide pharmacists and pharmacy technicians information regarding unique characteristics of the feline species in regards to ADME and therapy needs. With this, attendees will be able to better recognize differences in prescribing methods. We will also discuss 3-4 common human medication poisonings in felines through case examples.

courses.title: Triaditis from Exam Room to Food Bowl: Integrating Nutrition into Clinical Case Management
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical, case based overview of feline triaditis, integrating diagnostic evaluation, clinical decision making, and nutritional management. Participants will review clinical case examples, with discussion centered on diagnostic choices and treatment strategies. The program emphasizes applying nutritional intervention as part of comprehensive case management.

courses.title: VetQuest Travel CE Oncology & Oncologic Surgery
courses.description: These lectures will be over 3 days and cover topics related to diagnosing neoplasia in small animals, diagnostics for treatment planning and outline non-surgical and surgical therapies.

courses.title: Veterinary Ultrasound and Radiography Mentorship Program
courses.description:
The SkillVet Veterinary Radiology and Ultrasonography Mentorship Program is a 9-month postgraduate continuing education program designed for small animal veterinarians who wish to develop a structured, clinically applicable approach to diagnostic imaging. The program combines radiology, ultrasonography, case-based learning, supervised practical training, and longitudinal mentorship to help participants progress from foundational interpretation skills to confident clinical application in daily practice.
The program is delivered across five in-person modules between October 2026 and June 2027, taking place in Prague, Warsaw, Bucharest, and Cluj. The curriculum begins with thoracic and abdominal radiology, including normal anatomy, lung patterns, pleural and mediastinal disease, thoracic masses, cardiac radiology, gastrointestinal and genitourinary radiography, and abdominal mass interpretation. The radiology component then progresses to musculoskeletal imaging, including aggressive versus non-aggressive bone lesions, diseases of the growing and mature patient, trauma, and extensive case-based revision.
The ultrasonography component introduces ultrasound physics, artefacts, machine optimisation, and scanning technique before progressing through a systematic small animal ultrasound curriculum. Participants receive supervised training in abdominal ultrasonography, including the liver, biliary tract, spleen, gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, urinary tract, reproductive tract, adrenal glands, and lymph nodes. Advanced practical sessions also cover ultrasound-guided fine needle aspirates and biopsies, ocular ultrasound, thyroid and parathyroid ultrasound, neck ultrasound, salivary glands, larynx and trachea, lymph nodes of the head, and selected musculoskeletal ultrasound applications such as tendon scanning.
The teaching format combines structured lectures, live demonstrations, case-based discussions, small-group practical sessions, guided image interpretation, and continu

courses.title: VetQuest Travel CE Brachycephalic Conference Nashville 2026
courses.description: These lectures will be over 3 days and cover topics related to brachycephalic anesthesia, surgery, and ophthalmology.

courses.title: Change Management

courses.description: The clinical management of canine allergic dermatitis remains a complex challenge for veterinary practitioners and a significant concern for pet owners. This session provides a comprehensive review of the current clinical landscape, including epidemiological trends and the latest expert consensus guidelines for differentiating between allergic and atopic disease. Participants will evaluate various pharmacological classes, focusing on their specific mechanisms of action and indications based on clinical presentation. Furthermore, the program introduces novel therapeutic interventions for the treatment of dogs with allergic and canine atopic dermatitis.
