courses.title: Veterinary Herbal Medicine Onsite
courses.description:
Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) is a major branch of Chinese Medicine. Although most associate Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) with acupuncture, the majority of cases in TCM clinics in China are treated with herbs, either with acupuncture or alone, rather than with just acupuncture. In the States, more and more TVCM practitioners are following suit by incorporating herbs in their veterinary practice. CHM therapies have their historical origins with TCM and date back 4,000 years. Herbs today are prepared with the benefits of modern technology but are still guided by the historical wisdom underlying TCM. In CHM practice, herbs are used to correct imbalance underlying a disease pattern and to promote the body's ability to heal itself. Each herb has a different effect on the body and can fall under a number of classifications such as warming, cooling, sour, or bitter and can affect a variety of organs, including the liver, lungs, or heart. TCVM utilizes herbal formulas that are a combination of single-herb ingredients to treat a specific pattern of disease.
The increasing popularity of CHM lies in the fact that it is an all-natural treatment option that is generally safe and effective when prescribed correctly. An extensive body of clinical research has shown CHM to be extremely effective in treating chronic veterinary medical issues in the fields of gastroenterology, cardiology, dermatology, endocrinology, reproduction, oncology, and animal behavior. CHM is also commonly used to treat respiratory issues and sports injuries. In addition, CHM increases the quality of life for geriatric patients, especially those diagnosed with terminal cancer, as it assists the body's ability to reduce tumor size when chemotherapy may not an option. CHM can be combined with acupuncture and/or Western Medicine to enhance clinical results.

courses.title: Certified Myofascial and Manual Therapy Veterinarian Onsite
courses.description:
The Certified Myofascial and Manual Therapy program is a comprehensive course designed to train veterinarians in a wide range of manual and myofascial therapy styles and techniques. The program integrates foundational science, evidence-based practice, and extensive hands-on application to address soft tissue dysfunction, movement restriction, and pain, while promoting overall patient well-being. Participants will develop advanced palpation skills and learn to select and apply appropriate techniques based on individual patient presentation and clinical goals.
This program emphasizes real-world clinical integration, teaching veterinarians how to incorporate myofascial and manual therapy into diverse practice settings, including general practice, acupuncture/TCVM, rehabilitation and sports medicine, and integrative medicine services. In addition, the course also addresses practical considerations for building, integrating, and sustaining myofascial and manual therapy services within a successful veterinary business model.

courses.title: The Pressure is On: The Ins and Outs of Blood Pressure and Management
courses.description: Understanding blood pressure values fairly straightforward, but interpreting abnormal readings, their implications, and appropriate treatments can be challenging. This course will explain what blood pressure is, various methods for monitoring it, and provide detailed insights into systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressures. Hypotension, in particular, is complex, and with this knowledge, you will be better equipped to identify what your patient needs to address it effectively. We will also explore case-based examples to clearly illustrate the appropriate treatments and the reasons behind them.

courses.title: Urinary Catheter Placement in Cats and Dogs (Male and Female)
courses.description: Urinary catheterization is a common procedure in veterinary medicine, essential for managing urinary tract obstructions, monitoring urine output, and facilitating diagnostic sampling. This presentation will provide a comprehensive overview of urinary catheter placement in both male and female cats and dogs. Topics include indications, equipment selection, aseptic technique, step-by-step catheterization procedures and troubleshooting complications. Emphasis will be placed on minimizing patient discomfort, preventing infection and ensuring accurate placement through anatomical understanding and practical tips.

courses.title: Invironmeant: Building a Resilient Team
courses.description: A resilient team is built upon culture and decisions. What skills and knowledge are needed to support and strengthen your team against the difficulties of that work that you do daily? This workshop goes over key elements of building a resilient team for a healthy and happy practice. Leaders live the values and set the vision of their team. What is it that the team aligns around? The elements of a successful team are shared and measured during the presentation. Elements include creating an inviting and invincible culture, supporting, and strengthening your team and defining your hospital's meaning and purpose.

courses.title: Spread of the Spirochetes: Update on canine leptospirosis and Lyme disease
courses.description:
As the geographic range of continues to expand and reservoir wildlife have more access to dogs, the threat of spirochetal diseases like leptospirosis and Lyme disease is no longer confined to rural settings. Today's veterinary teams face the dual challenge of diagnosing these "great pretenders" - which often present with vague clinical signs or subclinical infections - and addressing the rising risk in urban and small-breed populations.
This session provides a comprehensive update on the epidemiology of Leptospira serovars and Borrelia burgdorferi. We will dive into latest ACVIM consensus guidelines for diagnosis and treatment. Finally, we will explore the science behind vaccine technologies and how highly purified, 1/2 mL combinations can provide protection and minimize vaccine injections.

courses.title: Essential Skills in Surgery & Ophthalmology
courses.description:
This EUVETCE Experiences seminar offers veterinarians and technicians a combined program in soft tissue surgery and ophthalmology for canine and feline patients.
The surgical sessions include practical approaches to abdominal exploratory procedures and organ biopsies, decision-making in gastrointestinal obstruction, and a review of core principles in gastrointestinal and urinary tract surgery. Emergency management is also addressed, with dedicated sessions on urinary obstruction, uroabdomen, thoracic trauma, chest tube placement, and feeding tube placement.
The ophthalmology sessions cover the diagnosis and management of deep and non-healing corneal ulcers, corneal lacerations, and ruptured globes. Other topics include practical approaches to glaucoma, conjunctivitis in dogs and cats, and acute-onset blindness. Surgical techniques such as entropion correction, cherry eye repair, eyelid tumor excision, and enucleation are discussed. Additional lectures offer updates on cataract management, long-term treatment strategies for keratoconjunctivitis sicca, and a review of essential ophthalmic medications for daily practice. The program ends with case discussions on complex ophthalmic conditions and guidance on referral decisions.

courses.title: Equipment Controls and Protocol for Soft Tissue Ultrasound - Intermediate to Advanced - Scan Only
courses.description: This program will cover machine functions and measurements needed for a complete abdominal exam. We will discuss the purpose of the different probes. We will cover how to scan the liver, spleen, kidneys, and bladder, pancreas, adrenals, and GI following a scanning protocol for these organs, so that the attendee can create a complete soft tissue ultrasound exam. This will be a Medical Program, that is hands-on scanning in a wet lab format for 8 hours of RACE CE.

courses.title: Stronger for Longer: Maintaining Muscle & Mobility in the Aging Feline
courses.description: Are you missing the subtle signs of muscle loss and pain in your senior feline patients? In this free, one-hour session, Dr. Ashlie Saffire delves into the critical, yet often underdiagnosed, issues of feline mobility and muscle health. Attendees will learn how to differentiate between disease-associated cachexia, age-related sarcopenia, and frailty. The presentation emphasizes the crucial role of utilizing both Body Condition Score (BCS) and Muscle Condition Score (MCS) during every senior exam to catch early downward trends. Discover how to implement environmental modifications, structured mobility exercises, tailored nutritional support, and the science behind an innovative supplement to inhibit muscle atrophy and keep your feline patients stronger for longer!

courses.title: Equine Ultrasound-Guided Joint Injections, Objective Gait Analysis & Rehabilitation Workshop
courses.description:
COURSE DESCRIPTION
This intensive and hands-on, one-day programme is designed for equine practitioners who want to advance their diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities in sports medicine and rehabilitation with the world's leading specialists, and apply these skills immediately in their daily clinical work.
With a strong emphasis on hands-on workshops and clinical panel discussions, this course provides a unique opportunity to learn and refine practical techniques under the guidance of international key opinion leaders in equine sports medicine and rehabilitation.
From ultrasound-guided joint injections to objective portable gait analysis using Consteed's revolutionary Smart Sneaker measuring ground reaction forces in real time, and the clinical application of modern rehabilitation modalities, each component of the programme is focused on delivering skills that can be implemented from day one after returning to practice.
Morning Lecture Sessions
The morning lecture sessions offer a concise, clinically focused overview of:
Practical tips and techniques for ultrasound-guided injections
New roles and applications of objective gait analysis
Matching the most appropriate rehabilitation modalities with specific lesions
Development of structured treatment plans and effective therapeutic monitoring
Clinical Case Panel Discussions
One of the highlights of the course is the Clinical Case Panel Discussions, where participants will engage directly with several world-leading specialists from diverse backgrounds.
These highly interactive sessions explore real-life clinical cases in an open and frank atmosphere, focusing on critical decision-making, treatment strategies, and optimisation of outcomes in everyday practice.
Afternoon Practical Sessions
The afternoon is dedicated to small-group practical sessions on live horses and high-fidelity anatomic replica simulators, ensuring a high level of individual hands-on participation and detailed instructor feedback.

courses.title: Principles of Fracture Stabilization
courses.description: Are you interested in learning or improving your approach and reduction of long bone fractures? Are you interested in learning simple techniques designed for the general practitioner to stabilize the most commonly seen fractures in dogs and cats? This laboratory is the one for you! The participant will learn reliable techniques and valuable practical tips helpful in repairing simple and more challenging comminuted fractures of the long bones. New implant designs have made fracture repair much simpler and more affordable. In addition, postoperative management of patients has also been simplified, and complications are rare if the principles of fracture repair are followed. This course will familiarize participants with fracture repair techniques, including IM pin/cerclage, tension band, bone plating, and External Skeletal Fixation (ESF), through lecture and clinical case presentations. Following the lecture and case review, participants will repair fractures on plastic bone models and cadavers. Postoperative radiographs will be taken to evaluate the participants' repair technique

courses.title: Surgical Procedures for General Practitioners: Urinary, Gastrointestinal and Basic Oncology Techniques
courses.description: During this course, participants will receive the most up-to-date information on urinary tract and gastrointestinal diseases with a focus on surgical management of both benign and malignant conditions. Lectures will be followed by laboratories that focus on having participants perform the same procedures that were highlighted during the lectures. At the end of this course, participants will be comfortable with many different urinary tract and gastrointestinal procedures, with a focus on procedures such as cystotomy, cystostomy tube placement, urethrostomy, gastrotomy, biopsy, enterotomy, intestinal resection and anastomosis, local flaps, digit amputation, and vulvoplasty.

courses.title: Nutrition in Equine Health and Performance
courses.description: Nutrition for the healthy horse is fairly straightforward; however, in the equine patient, a more scientific and clinical case approach is often needed. This presentation will offer an overview of the science behind nutrition and medical conditions of the horse, offer case studies of certain clinical conditions, as well as focus on the specific needs of the performance horse including guidelines to assist the equine veterinarian or veterinary technician in determining the best feeding options. Discussions will explore the pathophysiology of these conditions to better understand the role that nutrition can play in not only helping the athletic performance horse, but also our everyday equine companions and patients.

courses.title: Emergency Techniques for the General Practitioner
courses.description:
This cadaver-based course covers emergency management of penetrating thoracic and abdominal trauma through hands-on practice and discussion. Procedures include thoracostomy tube placement, tracheostomy, laryngeal foreign body removal, cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillation, abdominocentesis, nasoesophageal tube placement, and endoscopic foreign body removal.
By the end of this course, participants will be able to:
- Perform Abdominal and Thoracic FAST (AFAST/TFAST) examinations to identify free fluid
- Perform thoracocentesis and abdominocentesis using appropriate technique and landmarks
- Place and manage nasogastric (NG) tubes and esophagostomy (E) tubes
- Perform urinary catheterization in male and female patients
- Demonstrate central venous catheter placement and surgical cutdown techniques
- Perform nasotracheal oxygen supplementation and basic airway management
- Perform emergency tracheostomy and chest tube placement
- Deliver high-quality CPR using current BLS and ALS principles
- Select and prioritize appropriate emergency procedures based on clinical presentation

courses.title: Brachycephalic Upper Airway Surgery - Optimizing Outcomes
courses.description: This course delivers hands-on training for managing brachycephalic patients requiring upper airway surgery. Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) is common, and careful perioperative assessment and management is essential for good outcomes. Anesthesia can be challenging and requires several peri-operative considerations and interventions. Concurrent and related aerodigestive disorders are also critical to understand and diagnose appropriately. Led by a world-renowned soft tissue surgeon, an internal medicine specialist focused on airway disease, an anesthesiologist and experienced resident, this team will guide you through their approach to brachycephalic patients, using case-based scenarios and proven methods, so you leave with the confidence and tools for your next pug or bulldog surgery.

courses.title: Equipment Controls and Protocol for Soft Tissue Ultrasound - The Fundamentals
courses.description: This program will cover basic machine functions and measurements for those that are new to ultrasound. We will discuss the purpose of the different probes. We will cover how to scan the liver, spleen, kidneys, and bladder, and following a scanning protocol for these organs, so that the attendee can create a basic soft tissue ultrasound exam. We will also cover scanning a grid of the abdomen, artifacts, and different probe uses. This will be a Medical Program, that is hands-on scanning in a wet lab format for 8 hours of RACE CE.

courses.provider: SOUTH CAROLINA VETERINARY SPECIALISTS & EMERGENCY CARE
courses.title: Canine Cruciate Ligament Rupture: Is Surgery Needed?
courses.description: This presentation will discuss cranial cruciate ligament disease in dogs. It will cover ways to identify a cranial cruciate ligament injury, pathophysiology of CCL disease, pros and cons of various surgical treatment options, non-surgical treatment options, and recent literature on CCL disease

courses.title: The Hospital Environment, Part 2: Exploring Culture
courses.description:
This is the second lecture in a two-part series that does a deep dive into the real, physical, objective environment in which we work as veterinary professionals. We will explore the external environment in terms of sensory exposure, and the internal environment in terms of culture.
In this second part, we tackle veterinary workplace culture. Culture, by its simplest definition, is everything that is thought of by a group of individuals. It contains all of our ideas, modes of expression, values, hopes, fears, assumptions, and misconceptions as they affect our living and working together. The quality of each of those items (and countless others) gives a sense of the health of a culture and where changes ought to occur. From an organizational perspective, the quality of leadership determines the quality of the culture, and in turn the health of the workforce.

courses.title: Bereavement: Saying a Good Bye
courses.description:
Euthanasia is a procedure in Veterinary Medicine that can be a gift, but it also causes a lot of grief, in owners and in the veterinary team. This talk goes over what bereavement is, how to help clients handle it, and how make sure the pet gets the most respectful passing.
It also discusses how the veterinary team needs to care for themselves after any loss of a patient.

courses.title: The Impacts of Vaccination on Fertility and Profits
courses.description: This presentation discusses the concept of "Lifetime Immunity" and how sequence of vaccination may be critical for a robust immune response. We will also discuss how vaccination of cattle must not only be about risk mitigation, but also immune system development. This includes the idea that some vaccine presentations may not be appropriate for all cattle ages or production phases. We will reference the concept of heterologous prime-boost. Further discussions will remind the attendee about the intricacies of the relationship between the immune system and the reproductive system of cattle.

courses.title: Pain Management
courses.description: Attendants will be expected to learn how to better assess pain in veterinary patients, better recognize and treat chronic pain in pets, localize painful lesions and use pharmaceutical and other modalities for pain management.

courses.title: Flexible and Rigid Endoscopy
courses.description:
This 4-day course combines flexible GI endoscopy and rigid endoscopy to create a comprehensive course comprised of lecture and hands-on lab covering the following areas:
Basic Flexible Endoscopy: Introduction to endoscopy, including indications, endoscopic instrumentation, techniques for examining the upper and lower GI tract, plus a 7-hour wet lab to provide hands-on experience in both upper and lower endoscopy.
Intermediate Flexible Endoscopy: One-day course (lecture, demonstration, & laboratory session) on intermediate endoscopy techniques, including canine airway exam, additional experience in gastrointestinal examination, and foreign body retrieval and biopsies. This lab will also include a gastrointestinal examination of cats.
Rigid Endoscopy: One-day course (lecture, demonstration & laboratory session) on rigid endoscopy, including laparoscopy, rhinoscopy, video-otoscopy, and urethroscopy/cystoscopy.

courses.title: Equine Surgical Congress 2026
courses.description: Morbidity and mortality reporting of equine lameness surgical cases through presentations of case studies and case series by each presenter attendee in an open discussion round table format. Each attendee and presenter are Diplomates of the American College of Veterinary Surgeons. See below for summaries of each attendees presentations and specific learning objectives. Each presentation will last 60 minutes for a total of 14 hours of class time and 14 CE credits.

courses.title: A Technicians Guide to Epithelial Cancers
courses.description: Round cell tumors are among the most common cancers seen in veterinary practice and include lymphoma, mast cell tumors, plasma cell tumors, histiocytomas, and transmissible venereal tumors. This lecture will review their distinguishing features, common presentations, and typical treatments. Technicians will learn to interpret basic cytology findings, understand criteria of malignancy, and appreciate the nuances of diagnosing these cancers. The course emphasizes the technicians vital role in staging, sample collection, client communication, and treatment of the different diseases.

courses.title: Aortic Thromboembolism in Cats
courses.description:
In this course, participants will review the pathogenesis of thromboembolic disease in cats. We will describe the risk factors that preclude cardiac cats to this particular complication, prevention mechanisms and treatment courses.
Learning Objectives:
* Identify how to prevent aortic thromboembolism in cats
* Determine prognostic indicators that help dictate client conversation and expectations
* Learn various courses of treatments for aortic thromboembolism cases

courses.title: Understanding the Connection Between Health and Behavior
courses.description: We constantly assess and monitor our patient's physical health but what if any decline in health jeopardized their social relationships and wellbeing? Every action of every individual is the result of genetics, development, learning history, and health. We can actively help our patients stay healthy both physically and mentally.

courses.title: Radiographic Techniques of the Veterinary Patient
courses.description: This on-site hands-on radiograph instruction is given to technicians and/or veterinarians providing the information and technical radiographic skills to acquire images for diagnostics. At the end of the presentation/lab the participant should be able to understand the importance of radiation safety, how to operate an x-ray machine properly, and recognize the value of well positioned radiographs as a diagnostic tool for the veterinary patient.

courses.title: Small Animal Ophthalmology: Ophthalmic Examination and Surgical Techniques
courses.description: Ophthalmology does not have to feel foreign. This course equips general and emergency practitioners to recognize and manage common eye conditions. We will begin with a thorough ophthalmic exam, taught via lecture and live animal labs, then tour key diagnoses and their medical and surgical treatments. In cadaver labs, you will practice techniques for entropion, cherry eye, eyelid masses, proptosis, eyelid lacerations, and enucleation. You will leave ready to perform these procedures confidently in everyday practice.

courses.title: Small Animal Ophthalmology: Ophthalmic Examination and Surgical Techniques
courses.description: Ophthalmology does not have to feel foreign. This course equips general and emergency practitioners to recognize and manage common eye conditions. We will begin with a thorough ophthalmic exam, taught via lecture and live animal labs, then tour key diagnoses and their medical and surgical treatments. In cadaver labs, you will practice techniques for entropion, cherry eye, eyelid masses, proptosis, eyelid lacerations, and enucleation. You will leave ready to perform these procedures confidently in everyday practice.

courses.title: Feline Osteoarthritis Pain Management: NGF Signaling, Anti-NGF Antibodies, and Practical Clinical Decision-Making
courses.description:
Osteoarthritis affects up to 60% of cats over the age of six - yet most go undiagnosed because cats mask pain in ways that are subtle and easily overlooked. For many feline patients, chronic OA pain is quietly diminishing quality of life long before it is recognized in the exam room.
In this session you will learn how to recognize feline OA earlier, explore the role of NGF in perpetuating OA pain, and be introduced to the science of long-acting monoclonal antibodies. We'll cover new safety data and clinical evidence regarding the use of antiNGF mAbs in cats and understand how to apply proper patient selection criteria.
By the end of this session, participants will be able to identify OA in feline patients earlier and more consistently and confidently integrate monoclonal antibodies into their pain management protocols to improve outcomes for cats living with chronic OA.

courses.title: guidED 2026 | Edmonton Alberta
courses.description:
guidED Veterinary Leadership Conference is a comprehensive leadership development program designed specifically for veterinary practice leaders, including practice owners, managers, medical directors, and emerging leadership team members.
Scheduled for September 26-28, 2026, in Edmonton, Alberta, guidED provides an integrated learning experience focused on strengthening leadership effectiveness, team performance, organizational culture, client experience, and long-term practice sustainability.
The program is built around three interconnected learning components that support knowledge acquisition, practical application, and implementation of learning within veterinary practice settings.
Virtual, Online (On-Demand / Self-Paced)
What we call our Integral Learning Experience
The first phase is a virtual self-paced learning experience delivered approximately four weeks before the conference through the Octopoda learning platform. Developed in collaboration with subject matter experts, this component introduces foundational concepts, encourages early engagement, and helps identify participant questions and learning needs before the live event.
Classroom, Face-to-Face (Real Time)
What we call our Immersive Learning Experience
The second phase is the in-person conference experience. Participants engage in interactive workshops led by experts in leadership, professional wellbeing, communication, organizational development, client experience, and practice performance. All attendees participate in a shared curriculum with no concurrent sessions, creating a consistent learning journey and encouraging collaboration among veterinary leaders from diverse practice environments. Educational methods include facilitated discussion, reflective exercises, practical application activities, and peer learning opportunities designed to support immediate translation into practice.
Virtual, Online (Real Time)
What we call our Implementation Experience
The final phase is a live virtual impleme

courses.title: From Rookie to All-Star: Designing the Veterinary Excellence Operating System LIVE
courses.description:
Veterinary clinics everywhere are investing in CE, onboarding, and skills training, yet many still struggle with inconsistent competency levels, staff frustration, leadership fatigue, and a revolving door of support team turnover. The missing piece isn't more information - it is structure.
Rookie to All-Star: Designing the Veterinary Excellence Operating System is a six-week, implementation-focused hybrid program designed for veterinary leaders ready to build a sustainable team through an intentional, tiered development program. This program emphasizes purposeful team design, progressive skill development, competency validation, and a culture of excellence.
Participants will learn how to evaluate their current team structure, identify training breakdowns, design progressive learning pathways, integrate adult learning principles, build measurable competency systems, and create recognition programs that drive engagement and retention - leaving with a fully built Veterinary Excellence Operating System ready to launch in their practice.

courses.title: Is Your Osteoarthritis Patient Still a Puppy? Rethinking Pain, Behavior, & Early Intervention
courses.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is not limited to senior dogs. Developmental orthopedic disease, joint instability, abnormal conformation, and injury can initiate OA during puppyhood, when pain may appear only as subtle changes in play, activity, posture, and/or movement. This webinar will help clinicians identify at-risk young dogs, recognize early pain behavior and functional change, and implement a practical multimodal plan that preserves joint health, muscle function, and mobility while establishing sustainable lifelong care.

courses.title: Canine Infectious Respiratory Disease Complex: 5-Star Care on a 2-Star Budget
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Carol Reinero will provide a practical framework for diagnosing and managing canine infectious respiratory disease complex (CIRDC) in a variety of patients and clinical settings, including the otherwise healthy dog with acute respiratory signs, dogs with pneumonia, and groups of dogs affected by large outbreaks. Emphasis will be placed on recognizing the different clinical presentations of CIRDC and selecting diagnostic tests that provide meaningful information while considering case severity, diagnostic yield, and financial constraints. Dr. Reinero will explore strategies for delivering high-quality patient care without unnecessarily increasing diagnostic and treatment costs, with an overall goal of helping clinicians make thoughtful, cost-conscious decisions that maximize patient outcomes while remaining practical and accessible in real-world settings.

courses.title: Medical Math and CRIs: Removing the Fear Factor (TECH432)
courses.description: Does the thought of performing medical math, especially calculating a Continuous Rate Infusion (CRI), fill you with dread? It doesn't have to be that way! You have the power to master medical math! This lecture will illuminate the essential role of math in your practice, provide a brief review of key medications whose use often involves math, and guide you through each step of the calculation process with confidence.

courses.title: Nutrigenomics & Obesity: It's About Prediction, Not Restriction
courses.description: The field of nutrigenomics is a growing science that holds promise for health management in people and pets. A therapeutic weight loss food for pets was developed using nutrigenomic technology; the steps needed to create such a food using this advanced science will be reviewed. Clinical studies in dogs and cats using a nutrigenomic approach to weight loss will be discussed.

courses.title: The Burnout Conversation We Should Be Having
courses.description: Burnout remains one of the most significant challenges facing the veterinary profession, yet it is often oversimplified as a workload issue. This session rethinks the conversation around burnout by exploring organizational influences, individual responses, compassion fatigue, and self-awareness. Participants will explore practical strategies to recognize burnout earlier, respond more effectively, and build a more sustainable career in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: What does the changing landscape for accessible veterinary care mean for general practice?
courses.description: The idea that the veterinary industry as a whole has an obligation to provide care for all companion animals in the United States, regardless of their owner's ability to pay, is gaining acceptance. The veterinary oath requires us to use our skills and abilities for the betterment of society and the protection of animal health and wealth regardless of the animals' circumstances. For veterinarians confronting the daily economic realities of private practice and/or for any veterinarian who wants to practice high quality medicine, it can be difficult to understand how to balance owner limitations with the desire to provide care. The growing field of accessible veterinary care recognizes that for our profession to meet the professional obligations to provide care for all companion animals the industry needs to change. These changes involve rethinking the way care is delivered and developing new models for care. For veterinarians in practice who want to expand services to underserved clients, key strategies include offering flexible treatment plans and/or accepting alternative payment options.

courses.provider: TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY OFFICE OF VETERINARY CONTINUING EDUCATION
courses.title: 2026 Foundations of Avian Medicine and Nutrition
courses.description: A Continuing Education Course offered by the College of Veterinary Medicine, Texas A&M University, College Station TX. This one-day, virtual symposium is designed for veterinarians ranging from those new to working with birds to those already holding board certifications. The symposium will provide a practical progression through the foundations of avian medicine and nutrition. We will begin with an overview of avian care and clinical decision-making, followed by a nutrition primer covering the most important dietary considerations for captive psittacines and other avian species. A dedicated session on avian emergency medicine will focus on patient assessment, stabilization, and other essential techniques for managing critical cases. A lunch session will include information about captive parrot diets, supporting parrot wellbeing and aiding avian conservation. After lunch, participants will explore how research on wild and captive parrot foraging behavior and welfare can inform husbandry and nutritional management. The symposium will conclude with a practical feeding session focused on translating these concepts into clear, actionable dietary recommendations.

courses.title: It's Not the Injection, It's the Selection: Optimizing 2.5% iPAAG Outcomes in Canine OA
courses.description:
As the management of canine osteoarthritis continues to evolve, veterinarians are seeking therapies that provide long-term improvements in mobility, comfort, and quality of life. While intra-articular 2.5% iPAAG offers a novel approach to joint management, achieving optimal outcomes begins with selecting the right patient and setting appropriate client expectations.
This webinar will review the clinical considerations that support successful use of 2.5% iPAAG in canine patients, including patient selection criteria, diagnostic workup, joint-specific considerations, and treatment planning. Through real-world case examples and practical insights, attendees will learn how to identify ideal candidates, recognize factors that may influence outcomes, and integrate 2.5% iPAAG into a multimodal osteoarthritis management strategy.
Participants will leave with a framework for improving case selection, enhancing client communication, and maximizing the likelihood of positive clinical outcomes.

courses.title: Advances in Canine Urinary Incontinence Management: Understanding Bulking Therapies and what makes Mictamid different
courses.description:
Urinary sphincter mechanism incompetence (USMI) remains a common challenge in veterinary medicine, and advances in bulking agent technology continue to expand treatment options for affected patients. Join Dr. Roger Dmochowski, a recognized leader in female urology and reconstructive outcomes, and Dr. JD Foster, a veterinary specialist in nephrology and urology, for an in-depth discussion of the evolution of urethral bulking therapies.
This webinar will review the history and classification of bulking agents, exploring their mechanisms of action, benefits, and limitations. The faculty will discuss how Mictamid differs from traditional bulking agents, including its clinical application and potential role in managing canine urinary incontinence. Attendees will gain practical insights into patient selection, treatment positioning within current therapeutic strategies, and considerations for integrating procedures and documentation into everyday clinical workflows through electronic medical record (EMR) systems.
Designed for veterinary practitioners seeking to enhance their understanding of interventional options for urinary incontinence, this session will provide evidence-based perspectives and actionable takeaways for clinical practice.

courses.title: The Before, During, and After of Obtaining a Veterinary Technician Specialty Nutrition
courses.description: Veterinary Technician Specialties (VTS) provides an opportunity for credentials technicians to enhance their skills and knowledge in specific areas of practice. Obtaining these credentials include gathering experience, increasing knowledge and skills mastery through case development, practical skill exposure, and validated accreditation testing which can take anywhere from 3-5 years. The question many pre-applicants have is, and then what? Is there a guaranteed pay increase? What career opportunities are there? This session will discuss the story of a VTS Nutrition applicant from the preparing years, the application year, and what possibilities lie ahead.

courses.title: Managing Uncertainty: Four Ways to Optimize Practice Success
courses.description:
Throughout the world, this is a time of radical uncertainty. Wave after wave of disruption creates continual changes to the global economy, resulting in shrinking paychecks as costs continue to increase in all parts of life. Due to economic stressors, pets are receiving less veterinary care and the costs of operating a practice continue to increase.
Course corrections are necessary when turbulence sets in. What are four areas that practice leaders can map out today to help them weather this storm?

courses.title: Resident & Specialists Only: Soft Tissue Ultrasound Camp
courses.description: This course will cover a basic to intermediate level of the abdomen, emphasis on anatomy, physics, principles, knobology, image acquisition and protocols, normals, abnormals, case studies, scenarios, and touch on basic Doppler. This course is designed for Residents and Specialists with an interest in 40 hours of abdominal ultrasound with a Board Certified Radiologist to build their level of proficiency and satisfy the requirements of the ACVIM. Taught by Martha Larson, DVM, MS, DACVR

courses.title: Shaping the Diagnosis Series: Morphology Mystery
courses.description: Automated hematology analyzers provide powerful quantitative data, but important diagnostic insights can be missed when blood morphology is not assessed. This presentation explores the clinical value of blood morphology assessment as a complement to automated CBC results. Through one canine case study, participants will examine how morphology findings altered diagnostic pathways, improved interpretation of laboratory data, and influenced patient management. Practical guidance will be provided on when morphology review is most important and how morphology findings can be integrated into everyday clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Advanced TPLO
courses.description:
This course is for the experienced TPLO surgeon that wants to expand their understanding of TPLO and stifle surgery.
Prerequisites:
1. Online Tibial Plateau-Leveling Osteotomy series*
*Tibial Plateau-Leveling Osteotomy Series

courses.title: Is it Neoplasia or Not? The oncology world from the clinical sonographer's perspective.
courses.description: Attendees of this live lecture course should expect to learn their imaging responsibilities and expectations regarding a local vs. a multi-centric clinical presentation. What is overtly surgical, potentially surgical, or non-surgical. What meets neoplastic criteria, diagnostic sampling vs. surgical intervention, and sampling types depending on clinical presentations; FNA for cytological pathology and core biopsy for structural pathology.

courses.title: FiberMaxxing: When should pets do it?
courses.description: In this online CE event, Dr. Adam Rudinsky, MS, DACVIM reviews the properties of dietary fiber and how they can be implemented in small animal practice with specific focus on case based application of fiber diets and supplements and dosing protocols. The systemic health of animals and maintenance of gastrointestinal tract (GIT) homeostasis heavily relies on influences from dietary fiber. Dietary fiber includes a diverse assortment of non-digestible carbohydrates. Primary roles of dietary fiber in the GIT include physically altering the digesta, modulating appetite and satiety, regulating digestion, and acting as a microbial energy source through fermentation. Beyond the GIT, dietary fiber also has widespread systemic effects throughout the body. This review will focus on how to modify fiber in dogs and cats with gastrointestinal disease. The goal being to provide clinically relevant information for practical application in clinical practice. Join us to get a clinical update on appropriate strategies to identify and manage your fiber-responsive gastrointestinal patients.

courses.title: Unlocking MDR1 Mutations in Cats: Prevalence, Perils, & Protocols
courses.description: Join us for an evidence-based update on the feline multidrug sensitivity gene (MDR1 gene, also known as ABCB1 gene). Dr. Jeba Chelladurai will discuss the feline ABCB1 1930_1931del TC variant, a key loss-of-function mutation that can cause neurotoxicity following exposure to certain antiparasitic and other commonly used drugs. Dr. Chelladurai will review the MDR1 essentials, including how this 2-base pair deletion may place cats carrying 2 copies of the variant at high risk, and share new data from the largest screening study to date of 12,000 US domestic cats. Actionable takeaways will include how to identify which feline patients warrant genotyping and how to approach prescribing decisions with confidence.

courses.title: Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine
courses.description: The Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine enables practitioners to develop competency in utilising Western herbal medicine and Western herbal medicine principles in the assessment, treatment and management of animals in their care. Successful completion of this course will enable practitioners to safely and effectively integrate a core group of 40 important herbs into a veterinary practice. The course is orientated towards applied theory, which can be implemented in a veterinary practice almost immediately. Practitioners will be able to develop confidence and competence over time during the course, with continuous case support, guidance and feedback from tutors with both simulated and active case forums and subsequently their own clinical cases.

courses.title: A Fresh Perspective: A Discussion on Feeding Fresh
courses.description: This course provides veterinary professionals with a balanced, evidence-based look at fresh pet food diets compared to fresh-homemade and traditional dry food. Topics include a review of pet food safety; effective strategies for navigating popular nutrition trends; the practical benefits of fresh feeding; and key considerations for tailoring to a patients needs. Attendees will leave equipped to objectively counsel clients on fresh versus dry feeding options.

courses.title: VetCE Virtual: Beyond Bad Behavior - Understanding Canine and Feline Behaviour Disorders
courses.description: This VetCE Virtual set of 3 live distance presentations includes topics of interest presented by experts. The presentations are held on separate dates. Attendees enroll in all three and must attend all to earn the completion certificate. The first presentation is on September 14, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Easy as one, two, pee: Solving Feline Housesoiling. The 2nd is on September 21, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Resource Guarding of Food. The 3rd and final presentation is on September 28, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Addressing the Medical Components of Behavior Cases. The VetCE Virtual series of micro-conferences are a convenient alternative to in-person events and are designed to deliver multiple RACE and/or CVPM approved CE credits in a virtual format with three one-hour presentations. They provide educational sessions presented by expert speakers, and an easy way to learn and earn credits in the comfort of your home or office.

courses.title: From Cells to Signals: Innovations Transforming Cancer Diagnostics in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Recent advances in artificial intelligence, computer vision, and biomarker science are transforming the way cancer is detected, characterized, and monitored in veterinary patients. This presentation will explore emerging technologies that enhance diagnostic testing and clinical decision-making, including AI-enabled cytology interpretation, novel statistical approaches that objectively quantify diagnostic confidence, and blood-based biomarkers that support cancer screening, diagnosis, and disease monitoring. Together, these innovations are creating new opportunities for earlier detection, more informed clinical decisions, and improved patient care across the cancer journey.

courses.title: Canine Veterinary Ophthalmology: Adnexa, Cornea, and Intraocular Disease
courses.description: This 4-hour continuing education program provides veterinarians and veterinary technicians with a practical review of common adnexal, corneal, and intraocular disorders in dogs. The adnexal section addresses eyelid conformation and hair disorders, eyelid masses and lacerations, and third-eyelid disease. The corneal section reviews systematic assessment and management of simple, indolent, infected, melting, deep, and ruptured corneal ulcers as well as other clinically important corneal disease. The intraocular section covers examination techniques and the recognition and management of uveitis, glaucoma, cataracts, lens luxation or subluxation, retinal disease, and blindness.

courses.title: Dental Radiographs (TECH343)
courses.description:
Even for technicians experienced in radiography, dental radiographs are a whole different animal - and these images play a crucial role in conducting thorough oral exams on every patient.
This course will empower veterinary technicians and assistants with the essential skills needed to obtain diagnostic dental radiographs. Together, we will explore the normal anatomy and terminology of the mouth before embarking on the journey of mastering full mouth radiographs for both canine and feline companions. We will discuss and demonstrate proper positioning techniques to ensure the highest-quality images, while also addressing common challenges you may encounter and providing invaluable tips and tricks for capturing dental radiographs in brachycephalic breeds. Finally, we will delve into the various types of dental radiography equipment and the importance of radiation safety, equipping you with the knowledge to excel in this vital aspect of veterinary care.

courses.title: The Balance Between Art and Science in Seizure Management (NEUR101-1026)
courses.description:
The primary purpose of this course is to improve the ability and comfort of participants to manage seizure patients by providing an in-depth understanding of diagnostic workflows and approaches, how various anticonvulsants work, and how contextual factors of the patient and pet owner affect decisions regarding drug selection, monitoring, and alteration. The course will include a discussion of seizure definitions and classification, formulating a diagnostic plan for the seizure patient based on signalment and history, and general principles of seizure management. This course will focus on three major domains:
1. Classification and Diagnostic Approaches to Seizures, Medication Selection and Monitoring
2. Non-pharmacological Interventions
3. Discussion of Real-Life Cases and Approaches

courses.provider: THE AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF FISH VETERINARIANS
courses.title: ISAAH AAFV SESSION:Fish Veterinary Medicine in North America: Diversity in Production and Practice
courses.description: AAFV is hosting a session during ISAAH Norway with the topic Fish Veterinary Medicine in North America: Diversity in Production and Practice.

courses.title: Level Up: 2026 Veterinary Nurses and Technicians LIVE
courses.description: Veterinary nurses and technicians are the heartbeat of every practice - and this summit is built for you. Join our annual Level Up: Veterinary Nurses and Technicians Summit to learn while sharpening your clinical knowledge and fueling your professional growth. From emesis and Cushings disease to periodontal care, senior wellness, traumatic burn injuries, radiologic positioning, neurodiversity, burnout, and more, you will come away with clinical updates, new skills, fresh confidence, and ideas you can use on your very next shift. Because the future of veterinary medicine is not waiting - and neither should your career!

courses.title: Spectrum of Care: Steering the Conversation to Navigate for Better Outcomes
courses.description: As veterinary professionals, we are trained to offer and plan for the highest level of care for our patients. While that is what we ideally want to offer to every client and patient, the reality is that not every client can pay for or even manage such "Ideal" care. This lack of adherence to our recommendations for care contributes to meaning burnout and moral injury within the profession. Spectrum of Care refers to discovering what the client can or can't do for their pet - financially, physically, and emotionally. Understanding this enables an honest and non-judgmental conversation between the veterinary team and the client so that a mutually agreed upon treatment plan can be made for the shared focus of both - the Pet. Embracing a Spectrum of Care strategy with our clients means that we can help more patients and clients, and ultimately, can help ourselves by finding more fulfillment and satisfaction in our work.

courses.title: Foundations of Vaccination
courses.description: This educational program provides a comprehensive overview of the core principles of veterinary immunology and vaccinology. Designed for veterinary professionals, the session explores the physiological mechanisms of immune protection, the classification of modern vaccine technologies, and best practices for implementing effective vaccine protocols. Participants will gain the foundational knowledge necessary to support evidence-based vaccination strategies and confidently communicate the vital role of vaccination in lifelong pet wellness.

courses.title: Ethical disagreements in veterinary practice settings
courses.description:
Ethical disagreements are common in veterinary practice and arise when members of the veterinary team, clients, or other stakeholders hold differing views about what ought to be done in a particular situation. These disagreements may occur in relation to animal welfare, treatment decisions, resource limitations, financial constraints, client preferences, workplace policies, or professional responsibilities. When unresolved, ethical conflict can contribute to moral stress, moral distress, and reduced wellbeing among veterinary professionals.
This webinar will examine the nature and sources of ethical disagreement in veterinary practice settings. Participants will be introduced to common factors that contribute to differing ethical viewpoints, including variations in professional roles, values, ethical frameworks, experiences, and perceptions of animal welfare. Through discussion of practical veterinary scenarios, attendees will explore how ethical disagreement can reveal underlying welfare concerns and competing obligations that require careful consideration.
The webinar will also provide a structured approach for identifying and analyzing sources of ethical conflict within veterinary teams. Emphasis will be placed on recognizing disagreement as a potentially constructive component of ethical decision-making and as an opportunity to improve communication, support team wellbeing, and enhance animal welfare outcomes.

courses.title: APV 54th Annual Workshop
courses.description: Each fall since 1973, the Association of Primate Veterinarians has held its annual Workshop. During the four days of the meeting, members and nonmembers come together to enjoy the lectures, poster sessions, case reports, and roundtables. The program is designed to have topics relevant to the entire membership. The workshop will be held in Houston, Texas from Wednesday, October 21st to Saturday, October 24th.

courses.title: Kidneys and adrenals: Diagnostic challenges and therapeutic interventions in chronic kidney disease and canine hyperadrenocor
courses.description: In this 4-hour, LIVE seminar with Dr. Christina Marino, DVM, DACVIM (SAIM), participants will review advanced diagnostic and management strategies for complex endocrinopathies, polyuria/polydipsia (PU/PD), and chronic kidney disease in dogs and cats. The program re-evaluates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, covering diagnostic innovations for canine hyperadrenocorticism, atypical Cushing's disease, and alternative monitoring protocols that move beyond the traditional ACTH stimulation test. It provides a structured diagnostic approach to PU/PD, including the step-by-step execution and interpretation of a modified water deprivation test. Finally, the seminar details the pathophysiology and progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), providing updated therapeutic strategies including novel phosphate binders and erythropoietin-stimulating agents.

courses.title: Shockwave Therapy for Post-Surgical Treatment
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with: 1. A basic understanding of the various applications and techniques for delivering therapeutic shockwave 2. A review of conditions treated with shockwave therapy and specific positioning of the device and patients that optimize treatment outcomes 3. In-depth focus on palpation skills and advanced treatment techniques. 4. Provide the post-surgical indications for shockwave therapy, with particular attention to TPLO and non-healing bone cases. 5. Provide hands-on positioning and treatment practice for post-surgical patients using the PiezoWave Vet.

courses.provider: DBA VETERINARY DENTISTRY EDUCATION AND CONSULTING SERVICES
courses.title: Intermediate Canine Dentistry Beyond the Fundamentals in Practice
courses.description: This 16-hour CE course (8 hours of lecture and 8 hours of laboratory) is for veterinarians only. It is recommended that registrants have completed a fundamental course with us, or equivalent course with another Diplomate of the American Veterinary Dental College, as basic fundamental concepts are presumed and built upon. It is instructed by two Board Certified Veterinary Dentists. The 8-hour didactic course curriculum will start with a visual photographic and radiographic tour of hidden canine oral pathology. Step-by-step oronasal fistula repair will be presented. Fractured teeth and bonded resin sealants will be discussed and covered step-by-step. Surgical extraction of the maxillary molars and surgical site closure will be presented. Surgical complications, prevention, and management will be presented. Periodontal treatments beyond periodontal cleaning, including but not limited to, bone augmentation, guided tissue regeneration, osseous resective surgery, open root planing, and periodontal treatments will be presented. The course will provide canine dentistry education and skills for primary care veterinary practice.

courses.title: Understanding Client Communication in Real-World Practice
courses.description:
Exceptional veterinary care extends beyond medical knowledge it requires the ability to connect with people. Every client brings their own experiences, emotions, expectations, and unseen circumstances into the exam room. By learning to meet people where they are, veterinary professionals can build trust, strengthen rapport, and create a shared vision for their pet's care.
This practical session explores communication strategies that empower and educate pet parents while supporting optimal patient outcomes. Participants will learn how to guide conversations with confidence, simplify complex medical information without sacrificing accuracy, and bridge the gap between recommendations and understanding. Discussion will include navigating emotionally charged conversations, financial limitations, difficult diagnoses, and other challenging interactions with empathy and professionalism.

courses.provider: MELISSA SHAPIRO, DVM, PIGLET INTERNATIONAL INC
courses.title: A Veterinarian's Guide to Disabled Pets and Their People: Caring for the Disabled Patient
courses.description:
Pet parents of disabled animals face a unique hurdle, finding a veterinary team willing to embrace and partner in the care of their disabled pets. This might be due to differences in perceptions of quality of life and a lack of experience working with pets who are disabled.
This 60 minute session offers an empowering overview showing that disabled pets share the same foundational medical needs as typical patients, and that general and specialty practices are fully equipped to manage them. Through real life examples of disabled pets in authentic photos and engaging videos, attendees will start to reframe traditional quality of life conversations around a pets capacity for adaptation and happiness.
Attendees will learn to leverage external community resources and build an in clinic peer mentorship network to alleviate client stress and prevent premature euthanasia. The SHIFT Framework for Care of Disabled Pets will be introduced to give veterinarians, vet techs, and vet students an action plan for welcoming disabled pets into their practice.
The audience will leave feeling inspired, with a better understanding of the veterinarians role in supporting and guiding clients who choose to care for profoundly disabled pets.
The SHIFT Framework for Care of Disabled Pets
Secure appropriate medical care
Honor relative quality of life
Implement in home accommodations for individual needs
Find external online guidance and support networks
Tap into client base for peer mentorship

courses.title: The Fresh Food Alternative: Nutritional Strategies for Dogs with Protein-Losing Enteropathy
courses.description: For dogs with protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), commercial dry and canned diets don't always deliver the results patients need. Pet parents and the veterinary team are often left searching for alternatives. This webinar explores the role of fresh food diets as a therapeutic option when conventional commercial diets fall short. Attendees will learn how to approach diet selection for PLE patients, key nutritional considerations (fat restriction, protein source and digestibility, caloric density), and how to monitor response to fresh food interventions. Whether you're a veterinarian, veterinary nutritionist, or technician looking to expand your toolkit for managing difficult GI cases, this session will provide actionable guidance for incorporating fresh diets into a PLE treatment plan.

courses.title: The Art & Science of the Neurologic and Orthopedic Exam from a Practical Perspective
courses.description: This live, interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review methods for identifying the source of lameness. Case presentations will highlight orthopedic and neurologic evaluation, plus feature practical tips that are invaluable when determining surgical or conservative treatment for various disabling conditions. This course will also include methods drawing on techniques passed down from renowned practitioners of veterinary orthopedics and neurology.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: 36th Southcentral Davis-Thompson Meeting
courses.description: This 2 day meeting will feature 3 guest speakers and 20 veterinary pathology short case reports with a Friday lunch and dinner for in-person attendees. Zoom participation is also welcome.

courses.provider: THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE SPECIALISTS NORTH SCOTTSDALE
courses.title: Arthrocentesis and Joint Injection Wet Lab
courses.description:
2. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: In this cadaver wet lab, participants will learn and practice arthrocentesis and joint injection techniques for the hip, stifle, tarsus, shoulder, elbow, and carpus.
3. LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
1. Understand the indications for arthrocentesis and joint injections
2. Be able to confidently and successfully perform arthrocentesis and joint injection of the hip, stifle, tarsus, shoulder, elbow, and carpus.
4. PROGRAM AGENDA:
1. Divide participants into small groups, 4 per instructor and cadaver
2. Discuss the indications for arthrocentesis and joint injections
3. Demonstrate proper patient positioning and arthrocentesis and joint injection (using saline) technique for the hip, stifle, tarsus, shoulder, elbow and carpus. Participants to follow after instruction of each joint.

courses.title: Fetch Encore - NAVLE - Preparation, Placement & Professional Growth For the Vet Student and New Grad
courses.description:
Passing the NAVLE is one thing but being ready for real practice is another! This Fetch Encore virtual symposium focuses on the professional skills veterinary students and veterinary technician students need but rarely get taught:
Start making stronger calls with case-based learning, including:
- Managing the transition into practice
- Testing strategies
- Clinical reasoning
Expect honest conversations about confidence, imposter syndrome, and how to think like a doctor under pressure.

courses.title: Increased Liver Enzyme Activities in a Dog: Help! What Should I do Next?
courses.description: This presentation focuses on a practical, stepwise approach to dogs with persistently elevated liver enzyme activities. Common diagnostic tests used in evaluation of canine hepatic disease will be reviewed, with emphasis on their appropriate application and interpretation. A staged diagnostic framework will be presented, including when to pursue advanced testing such as liver biopsy and how to maximize diagnostic yield from the procedure.

courses.provider: AMERICAN KENNEL CLUB CANINE HEALTH FOUNDATION
courses.title: Protecting the Aging Brain: IGF-1 and Canine Cognitive Dysfunction
courses.description: Older dogs often develop a form of dementia that is similar to Alzheimer's disease. We currently know little about this condition which limits our ability to prevent or manage it. IGF-1 is a hormone that regulates body size in dogs. In studies with humans and other animals, this hormone has been shown to protect the aging brain. This webinar will explore research investigating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), a hormone that regulates body size in dogs and has been associated with protective effects on the aging brain in humans and other animals. Attendees will learn how researchers are evaluating whether lower IGF-1 levels are associated with increased risk for cognitive dysfunction in dogs and what this could mean for future research and treatment.

courses.title: When Weight Loss Stalls: Practical Strategies for Challenging Cases
courses.description: Obesity management is often complicated by challenges such as inconsistent weight loss, food-seeking behaviors, multi-pet households, feeding inaccuracies, and declining owner adherence. This case-based presentation will explore practical strategies for overcoming common barriers encountered when weight loss stalls in dogs and cats. Through real-world clinical examples, participants will review methods for assessing weight loss progress, identifying factors limiting success, and implementing evidence-based interventions, including gram-scale feeding, feeding enrichment, automated feeders, and individualized nutritional adjustments. Presented from both the veterinarian and veterinary nurse perspectives, the session will emphasize the collaborative team approach needed to support successful weight management and long-term client engagement. Effective communication strategies, client preferences for decision-making, and practical methods for improving adherence will also be discussed. Attendees will gain tools to troubleshoot challenging cases and improve weight management outcomes in companion animals.

courses.title: Urine Trouble: Navigating Urethral Obstruction in Cats & Dogs
courses.description: Urethral obstruction is a common and potentially life-threatening urinary emergency requiring rapid recognition, stabilization, and relief of obstruction. This lecture will review clinically relevant urinary anatomy and physiology before providing a practical approach to the diagnosis and management of urethral obstruction in cats and dogs. Feline urethral obstruction will be discussed with emphasis on pathophysiology, diagnostic evaluation, stabilization, urinary catheterization, and management of associated metabolic complications. The canine section will address common causes of urethral obstruction, diagnostic investigation, and treatment options. Practical tips and techniques for managing challenging obstructions and reducing complications will be incorporated throughout the lecture.

courses.provider: MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Practice with Confidence: Leveling Up Veterinary Teams
courses.description: Practice with Confidence: Leveling Up Veterinary Teams is a collaborative CE experience designed to help veterinary professionals strengthen team utilization, improve workflow efficiency, and practice with greater confidence through a clearer understanding of licensure and scope of practice. Bringing together veterinarians, veterinary nurses, and team members for a shared learning experience, the program focuses on practical, real-world knowledge and strategies that empower individuals to work to their full potential and practice to the full extent of their license. Through sessions focused on delegation, leadership communication, risk management, workforce sustainability, and emerging animal health threats, participants will explore evidence-based approaches to optimizing team performance while maintaining high standards of patient care. Participants will leave with actionable tools and follow-up opportunities to support long-term implementation and success.

courses.title: VSC Veterinary Nutrtition Conference
courses.description: This five hour continuing education program will cover a wide variety of topics related to nutrtion for dogs and cats including - how to read pet food labels; healthy pet loss; evaluating raw, home-made and natural diet options; role of diet in pet allergies; and the role of diet in treating common diarrhea.

courses.title: Canine Atopic Dermatitis - Is it the Perfect Situation for a Spectrum of Care Approach?
courses.description: One hour discussion session with Christina M Gentry, DVM, DACVD, Craig Teller, MD and Lori Teller, DVM, DABVP along with the moderator, Kristin Jankowski, VMD, CCRP. During the hour we will discuss their publication, How does canine atopic dermatitis provide a unique opportunity to study spectrum of care? as well as the related JAVMA publication, Multiple factors, including client financial constraints, play a role in clinician decisions for canine atopic dermatitis: spectrum of care in a chronic and relapsing disease. We will review barriers to care, care burden clients experience when managing dermatologic conditions in their pets, spectrum of care dermatology, as well as strategies that can be used in veterinary medicine aligned with the human dermatology field to manage costs with good outcomes. There will be 10-15 minutes of the session where attendees will ask the panelists questions related to the topic.

courses.title: Becoming a Veterinary Technician Specialist (VTS): Pathways, Possibilities, and Passion
courses.description: Veterinary technicians are increasingly seeking advanced recognition for their knowledge, skills, and impact on patient care. The National Association of Veterinary Technicians in America (NAVTA) responded to this need by establishing the Committee on Veterinary Technician Specialties (CVTS), which provides the framework for creating and maintaining veterinary technician specialty academies. This webinar will walk you through the VTS journey--from understanding the history and structure of veterinary technician specialties, to deciding which discipline aligns with your passion, to navigating the application, examination, and recertification processes. We'll explore all currently recognized VTS academies, and outline what it takes to start a new specialty when one doesn't yet exist. Blending practical guidance with real-world experience, including a personal case example in veterinary nutrition, this session is designed to help you determine whether a VTS is right for you, how to prepare, and how specialization can advance both your career and your practice.

courses.title: Hyaluronic Acid in Practice: A Veterinary Dental Case Round Table LIVE
courses.description:
This is a case-based round table exploring the use of hyaluronic acid as an adjunct to a variety of dental and oral procedures.
Through a series of canine and feline cases, our panelists will share their clinical experiences using hyaluronic acid alongside established dental treatments, including closed root planing, gingival curettage, bone grafting, guided tissue regeneration, and full-mouth extractions. Cases will highlight applications involving advanced periodontal disease, furcational bone loss, feline chronic gingivostomatitis, and significant oral inflammation.
Participants will see how hyaluronic acid has been incorporated into treatment plans to support soft-tissue healing, manage local inflammation, promote periodontal and alveolar bone regeneration, and, in select cases, help preserve teeth that may otherwise have required extraction.
This interactive discussion will go beyond the theory and into the clinical decision-making behind each case, including patient selection, treatment techniques, outcomes, and practical considerations for incorporating hyaluronic acid into veterinary dental procedures.

courses.title: Comparative Speed of Kill of the Lone Star Tick (Amblyomma americanum)
courses.description: This presentation considers the importance of speed of tick kill to safeguard pets against tick-borne diseases and protect the human-animal bond. Tick-borne disease transmission and the unique characteristics and geographical expansion of Amblyomma americanum (lone star tick) will be reviewed. Details of a recent study on A. americanum comparing the relative immediate and residual speed of tick kill following administration of three monthly-use isoxazoline-containing products will be discussed, including methodology and key study findings. This new data will be utilized to highlight the importance of rapid and consistent speed of tick kill.

courses.title: Zennovation in Sedation: Rethinking What is Possible
courses.description: In this educational presentation, we will discuss sedation in dogs. The foundation will be set by reviewing the basic physiology behind commonly used sedatives in dogs. We will discuss the most commonly used sedatives and reversal agents, and introduce the novel sedative Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan hydrochlorides).

courses.provider: ACCESS SPECIALTY ANIMAL HOSPITAL PALM BEACH COUNTY
courses.title: Introduction to Interventional Radiology
courses.description: This course offers a concise review of key interventional radiology procedures and their indications. Topics include tracheal, nasopharyngeal, urethral, and ureteral stenting (including SUBS), treatment of intrahepatic shunts, and percutaneous laser disc ablation. Post-procedure care and complication management are also covered.
courses.location: ACCESS Specialty Animal Hospital Palm Beach County

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Dentistry Faux Pas
courses.description: The second hour of our eight-part series will review dentistry faux pas that practitioners commonly encounter. Participants will learn how to distinguish normal radiographic anatomy from pathology, properly diagnose and close an oronasal fistula, and perform extractions of the canine tooth and maxillary fourth premolar while avoiding common mistakes. The discussion will also cover the causes and treatment options for feline chronic gingivostomatitis, equipping clinicians with strategies for one of the more challenging conditions in feline dentistry.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Feline & Canine How To - Extraction Lab Focused
courses.description: This two-hour discussion (of our eight-part series) will walk attendees through the principles and practical steps of performing extractions in both feline and canine patients. The feline portion begins with a review of surgical fundamentals, including proper suture selection, knot placement, and spacing, before moving into the instruments best suited for feline dentistry such as elevators, periosteal elevators, burs, and root tip picks. A step-by-step guide will cover how to approach full-mouth extractions when indicated, with an emphasis on recognizing and preventing potential complications. High-quality video demonstrations will provide a clear visual of techniques for several types of feline extractions. The canine portion builds on these same principles, with discussion of the specialized equipment required for canine extractions and a focused look at more advanced procedures, including extraction of the canine teeth and maxillary fourth premolars. Throughout, the session emphasizes efficiency, precision, and patient safety, ensuring that participants leave with a solid foundation to approach complex extractions in practice.

courses.title: Updating Your Ocular Surgery Techniques.
courses.description: This program will review the ophthalmic surgical procedures that can be performed by a general practitioner or an emergency clinician. Each procedure will be discussed in detail and time will then be given to perform them on cadaver pig eyes. This will be a lecture plus wetlab

courses.title: CKD: Therapy Beyond Diet and Fluids
courses.description: The goal of this one-hour CE course is to review chronic kidney disease therapeutic options, outside of diet and fluids. IRIS diagnosis and staging will briefly be reviewed, as well common treatments for symptoms of kidney disease for both dogs and cats, including hypertension, proteinuria, and gastrointestinal signs. The main advantages and disadvantages of renal diets will also be summarized. The focus will then turn to the gut kidney axis and dysbiosis that occurs in chronic renal failure and the possible benefit of probiotics to support kidney health. The importance of phosphate management in chronic kidney disease will be described and research presented on the longevity of patients and phosphate target levels. Attendees will learn how to incorporate FGF-23 testing for improved phosphate control in feline patients. Different phosphate binding options, beyond renal diets, will be discussed. Hypokalemia management will also be presented.

courses.title: (LIVE COURSE) Updates in The Diagnosis and Management of Sepsis
courses.description: This 3-week online course covers current approaches to recognising and managing severe systemic illness and sepsis in dogs and cats. We will move from the initial systemic inflammatory response through septic shock and into multiple organ dysfunction. Each week addresses practical diagnostics, fluid and vasopressor therapy, antimicrobial selection, and organ-specific support. This course is ideal for anyone seeing patients with severe illness, and provides a sound, evidence-based approach to patient management based on the very latest literature - all designed to optimise patient outcome.

courses.title: Innovate with Intention 2026 Virtual Conference
courses.description: This year's conference offers more than 49 hours of RACE-eligible CE content across medical and non-medical categories. Medical sessions cover evidence-based clinical topics including pharmacology and analgesic protocols for dogs, cats, exotic companion animals, birds, and small mammals; palliative nutrition for patients with kidney and gastrointestinal disease; physical rehabilitation and therapeutic exercise for geriatric and hospice patients; management of endocrinopathies, respiratory conditions, and degenerative disease at end of life; cannabinoid therapy; rational NSAID use; and the latest research in euthanasia protocols and decision-making. Non-medical sessions address professional development, practice management, and professional wellness topics including communication strategies for end-of-life conversations, cultural competency, grief theory and bereavement support, ethics, technician career pathways, practice management and workflow systems, and mental health for veterinary professionals.

courses.title: Intro to TPLO
courses.description: TPLO has become a favorite technique of general and specialty veterinarians to treat CrCL tears in all sizes of dogs. TPLO stabilizes the stifle by eliminating cranial tibial thrust. TPLO is an excellent technique for treating partial and complete tears of the CrCL. This interactive course includes lectures and laboratories to teach participants the theory and method of tibial plateau leveling osteotomy TPLO. Participants will perform TPLOs on plastic bones and cadavers using state of the art equipment and implants. Participants will use locking plate technology to simplify increase precision and reduce complications of the procedure. Participants should have a basic knowledge of anatomy and surgical approach to the stifle and principles of bone plate application. Postoperative radiographs will be taken to assess the participants' repair technique. Postoperative management will also be discussed.

courses.title: Hands-On, Ears Up: Mastering the Physical Exam in Exotic Companion Mammals
courses.description: Physical exams can be your most powerful diagnostic tool, if you know what to look for. This session focuses on refining your approach to exotic mammals, with tips for minimizing stress, recognizing subtle abnormalities, and adapting techniques for various species.

courses.provider: FISH HEALTH SECTION, AMERICAN FISHERIES SOCIETY
courses.title: ISAAH 2026 - Fish Nutrition Workshop
courses.description: The continuing education program "Fundamentals of Nutrition: Better Feeds for Healthier Fish" will offer veterinary and fish health professionals a working knowledge of fish nutrition and guidance for achieving better outcomes in the field. The workshop will cover core nutritional principles, common nutritional diseases, interactions between nutrition and infectious diseases, and practical strategies for improving fish health and performance.

courses.title: Ocular Emergencies (OPHT206)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss how to tackle the dreaded red eye that shows up on the emergency schedule and much more. Topics covered will include the most common ophthalmic emergencies in veterinary practice, how to triage them, treatment and management options available, and what to tell the owner in a crisis.
