courses.title: Management of Common Anesthesia Complications (part 1 of 2)
courses.description: Anesthetic complications are common, predictable, and often caused by the very drugs used to provide safe anesthesia. This lecture reviews the most frequent peri-anesthetic complications, including hypotension and bradycardia, and provides practical, case-based strategies to recognize them, understand their physiologic causes, and intervene effectively to support safer outcomes from induction through recovery.

courses.title: There's No Such Thing as Just Behavior
courses.description: There's No Such Thing as "Just Behavior" explores the critical connection between physical health and behavior, challenging the assumption that behavior problems exist in isolation. Using current research and real-world case studies, Dr. Lisa Radosta demonstrates how gastrointestinal, dermatologic, and endocrine disease can contribute to changes in behavior and how recognizing these underlying medical conditions can lead to more successful patient outcomes. Participants will also learn practical strategies for discussing the relationship between medical and behavioral health with clients, helping them understand why a comprehensive diagnostic approach is essential to effective Fear Free care.

courses.title: Techniques for Managing Behavior in the Treatment area
courses.description: Fear Free doesn't stop at the exam room door. In this session designed for the entire veterinary team, we'll explore what it takes to manage fear, anxiety, and stress in the treatment area -- from reading stress signals and building a calmer environment, to creating team workflows that keep patients at the lowest possible FAS throughout their visit. With real-world examples, attendees will leave with practical tools and a shared framework for advocating for patient emotional health at every step of the back-of-house experience.

courses.title: Selecting Therapeutic Diets for GI and Skin Disease: An Iterative Approach to Nutritional Management
courses.description: This course reviews the nutritional strategies available for common GI and skin disorders and provides practical guidance on when and how to use them. Participants will learn how to obtain a diet history, perform a nutritional assessment, and use this information to guide diet selection. The course emphasizes an iterative approach to dietary management, helping clinicians evaluate patient response and fine-tune nutrition plans to achieve optimal outcomes.

courses.provider: FISH HEALTH SECTION, AMERICAN FISHERIES SOCIETY
courses.title: ISAAH 2026 - Fish Pathology Workshop
courses.description: The Fish Pathology Workshop will take place, in conjunction with the 10th ISAAH, on Monday September 21 2026 at The Noatun laboratory building is a new, modern laboratory facility at the Bodo campus of Nord University. Lectures and laboratories will be delivered by Dr. David Groman Section Head of the Aquatic Diagnostic Services at the Atlantic Veterinary College in Prince Edward Island, Canada, Dr. Jeff Wolf Senior Pathologist from Experimental Pathology Laboratories, Inc. (EPL) located in Sterling, Virginia, USA, and Dr. Ginevra Brocca Fish Pathology Consultant from Glasgow (UK). The workshop is designed for entry and midlevel fish health researchers and workers, as well as students. Demonstrations on diagnostic necropsy protocol with reference to diagnostic lab submissions will be the focus in the morning, using Atlantic salmon and Wolffish specimens. The afternoon session will include sessions on Zebrafish histo-anatomy and physiology as well as case studies of unusual Atlantic salmon and Wolffish pathologies. Scanned slides of diagnostically interesting cases will be available for participants to follow during afternoon lectures and as such participants are encouraged to bring laptops.

courses.title: Pet Insurance Misconceptions
courses.description:
Pet insurance has never been more relevant to veterinary practice - yet misconceptions about how it works continue
to create friction at the exam table and erode client trust. This session addresses the most common myths veterinary
professionals encounter, from beliefs about pre-existing condition exclusions and claim complexity to the idea that pet
insurance "never pays out." Drawing on nearly two decades of veterinary medicine experience and six years inside a
leading pet insurance company, speaker Britni Bardin offers a perspective on where the industry falls short in
communicating its value, and how veterinary teams can guide clients toward coverage decisions that serve their pets.
Attendees will leave with a practical understanding of how pet insurance policies work, what to look for when
comparing plans, and how to have more confident, accurate conversations with clients about coverage.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF LABORATORY ANIMAL MEDICINE
courses.title: Building A Culture of Care Through a Formal Global Strategy
courses.description: In 2023, Comparative Medicine initiated a strategy to build an active and robust Culture of Care at all US Pfizer sites conducting animal research. It consists of three pillars: intentional, consistent progress in animal care and welfare while maintaining study quality, colleague care and wellbeing, and openness and transparency internally and with the public. This presentation will include how activities and goals under each pillar were prioritized and resourced over the past three years as well as how we utilize tools such as formal colleague surveys to gauge our progress in building our Culture of Care.

courses.title: Held Together by Heroes: Redesigning Inventory, Compliance, and Technology in the Veterinary Hospital
courses.description: Held Together by Heroes: Redesigning Inventory, Compliance, and Technology in the Veterinary Hospital is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Feeding Management for Pets with Kidney Disease
courses.description:
This lecture will discuss feeding management and strategies for pets with kidney disease. Attendees will learn how to compare products on the market to make the
best choice for their patient to help slow the progression of the disease and keep pets feeling well for as long as possible. Technicians should be familiar with the specific nutrient modifications in a renal-friendly diet so that information can be shared with clients. Being able to educate clients that food is the medicine for pets with renal disease will help clients feel better about feeding the recommended diet and sticking to the recommended treatment plan. Feeding management tips and tricks will also be covered. Pets with renal disease often have selective appetite, and different feeding management strategies need to be used to help keep pets eating
the proper diet will be shared. A discussion on various ingredients in the diets will also be covered. When technicians remember that pets do not need ingredients, they need nutrients, they can better educate their clients on why a specific diet was selected.

courses.title: A Picture Is Worth 1,000 Words
courses.description: A Picture Is Worth 1,000 Words is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Reducing Burnout in Veterinary Medicine: Practical Strategies for Sustainable Wellbeing
courses.description:
Burnout remains one of the most significant wellbeing challenges facing veterinary care providers, affecting one-third to one-half of individuals working in the profession. While burnout is often discussed as an individual struggle, research increasingly recognizes it as a complex workplace phenomenon influenced by factors such as workload, psychological safety, team culture, autonomy, and organizational practices. Addressing burnout requires more than individual resilience; it requires meaningful strategies at both the personal and organizational levels.
In this 1-hour webinar, participants will explore the current evidence on burnout in veterinary medicine and examine the contributing factors that influence wellbeing in clinical practice. Through a practical, solutions-focused approach, attendees will learn strategies that veterinary professionals can implement to support their own wellbeing, as well as approaches that leaders and organizations can use to create healthier, more sustainable workplaces.
Participants will leave with actionable tools to reduce burnout risk, strengthen protective factors, and foster a culture where veterinary teams can thrive while continuing to provide compassionate care.

courses.title: VetQuest Anesthesia, Dentistry & Oral Surgery
courses.description: These lectures will be over 3 days and cover topics related to anesthesia, dentistry & oral surgery in small animals.

courses.title: 2026 Surgery Summit
courses.description: The American College of Veterinary Surgeons (ACVS) defines the standards of veterinary surgical excellence, promotes advancements in veterinary surgery, and provides surgery continuing education programs. The ACVS Surgery Summit features seminars focused on all areas of patient care, from diagnosis, pain management and anesthesia, to surgery, postoperative care, and rehabilitation. The entire practice team can gain invaluable skills and exceptional continuing education.

courses.provider: SHREIBER SCHOOL OF VETERINARY MEDICINE OF ROWAN UNIVERSITY
courses.title: When They Can't Just Shake It Off: A Practical Approach to Status Epilepticus and Cluster Seizures in Dogs
courses.description: What do you do when a dog's seizures will not stop? Status epilepticus in dogs (continuous seizure activity of greater than 5 minutes or greater than 2 generalized seizures without recovery of consciousness) is one of the most challenging neurological emergencies veterinarians encounter. Recent advances in our understanding of the mechanisms underlying prolonged seizure activity have challenged traditional approaches and reshaped treatment protocols. This practical talk will discuss how to prevent and treat cluster seizures and status epilepticus in dogs.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF LABORATORY ANIMAL MEDICINE
courses.title: Anesthesia and Analgesia of Laboratory Fish
courses.description:
This session will focus on anesthesia and analgesia of laboratory fish. Included in this session is discussion of species-specific anatomical, physiologic, and behavioral considerations as it relates to the anesthetic event and pain management. Available health and welfare monitoring tools and different types of analgesic drugs and techniques will be covered. Learning objectives include:
-Review fish-specific considerations for anesthesia provision.
-Discuss available methods and protocols for anesthesia.
-Discuss available methods for assessing pain.
-Determine analgesia protocols for management of pain.
After completing this webinar, participants will have had the opportunity to refine species-specific knowledge, to advance understanding of animal assessment, and to enhance the quality and safety of fish anesthesia and pain management

courses.title: Diamonds in the Ruff
courses.description:
Those of us in the veterinary profession constantly find ourselves under significant pressure from self and others. The effect of that stress can either be unfortunate or of value to us. Like Diamonds, the stress that we endure can aid us in developing into brilliant and valuable caregivers.
This conversation goes over the 4 C's of being in the veterinary profession and how to use them to shine and succeed in practice.

courses.title: Mobility, Obesity and Pain
courses.description:
Learners will understand the role of obesity on its role in pain management and mobility.
Program Agenda:
Highlight clinical pain assessment
Role of cytokines with pain and joint health and changes that occur with obesity.
Highlight means to address nutritional aspects of obesity and the role of the veterinary team.
Learning Objectives:
Understand pain assessment
Clinical approach to pain exam.
Role of cytokines in obesity and pain
Nutritional options for obesity

courses.provider: INTERNATIONAL SOCIETY FOR COMPANION ANIMAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE
courses.title: Companion Animal Antimicrobial Stewardship and Infection Control 2026-2027 Seminar Series
courses.description: This seminar series provides ten (10) approximately monthly, one (1) hour-long seminars led by an expert in the field of veterinary antimicrobial stewardship and/or infection prevention and control over the course of eleven (11) months beginning in September 2026 and concluding in July 2027. Participants are not required to attend every seminar and can attend seminars of interest, earning credit for only the seminars attended. Seminars deliver clinically relevant information and cutting-edge research updates on topics surrounding antimicrobial resistance, antimicrobial stewardship, and infection control within companion animals. Seminars are designed to support the implementation and expansion of antimicrobial stewardship and infection control programs within general practice and specialty veterinary hospitals.

courses.title: 2026 AETA - CETA/ACTE Joint Annual Convention
courses.description: The AETA & CETA/ACTE 2026 Joint Convention aims to present a unified voice for those involved in the embryo transfer industry in the promotion of mutual interests and objectives, provide continuing education and information regarding current issues in the embryo transfer industry for members. The American Embryo Transfer Association embraces its responsibility as the resource for embryo transfer in the United States. This authority is developed and supported through our commitment to excellence in several broad areas: education and standards of quality.
courses.location: Monona Terrace Community and Convention Center

courses.title: A Pain in the Gut: A Discussion on Managing Chronic Canine Enteropathies
courses.description: This course will discuss and review primary enteropathies in the canine patient. Specifically, we will review pathophysiology/ predisposing conditions and diagnosis. Furthermore, while focusing on common comorbidities, developing an appropriate nutritional support based on the individual patient will be discussed. An emphasis is also placed on client communication throughout the entirety of the lecture.

courses.title: Confident Conversations: Communication Strategies for Increasing Trust and Wellness Compliance
courses.description: Helping clients understand the value of preventive care isn't always easy. Questions about vaccines, parasite prevention, and other wellness recommendations can lead to difficult conversations that leave veterinary professionals feeling discouraged. Join Dr. Donnelly as she shares practical approaches for navigating these everyday communication challenges. Using real-world wellness appointment scenarios, attendees will learn how to help clients feel heard, respond to concerns with empathy, and communicate recommendations in ways that foster trust and improve compliance.

courses.title: 47th Annual AAV Conference & Expo
courses.description: The 47th Annual AAV Conference & Expo will cover avian veterinary techniques and avian medicine. This conference is hosted by the Association of Avian Veterinarians (AAV). The program will focus on advancing avian health, welfare, and conservation through education, advocacy, and science.

courses.title: Creating Your Own Veterinary Style While Remaining Authentic
courses.description:
Graduation marks the beginning of a career, not the end of learning. As veterinary professionals transition from the classroom into clinical practice, they quickly discover that medicine is only one part of the job. Every day presents opportunities to communicate, adapt, lead, make difficult decisions, and navigate uncertainty while remaining true to themselves.
This interactive session explores the development of a professional identity rooted in authenticity, emotional intelligence, resilience, and self-awareness. Rather than prescribing a single "right" way to practice, participants will be encouraged to reflect on their own values, communication and working styles, and approaches to professional and personal growth.
Through practical discussion, guided reflection, and real-world examples, students will gain tools for approaching challenges with greater confidence, professionalism, and adaptability regardless of their role, personality, or career path. Whether entering practice as a veterinarian or veterinary technician, participants will leave with strategies to intentionally develop their own veterinary style while building a sustainable and fulfilling career.

courses.title: Wild West Vet 2026
courses.description: The Wild West Vet Show brings together veterinarians, veterinary technicians, practice owners, practice managers and animal health professionals for four days of high-quality continuing education, networking and product discovery in Reno, Nevada. Explore expert-led sessions covering small animal medicine, large animal medicine, equine care, exotics, emergency medicine, dentistry, practice management, leadership and more, alongside hands-on learning opportunities and a dedicated veterinary technician program.

courses.title: Thoracic Radiology Cardio/Pulmonary (DIAG408)
courses.description: This course is for veterinarians who are interested in building a solid foundation interpreting cardiopulmonary abnormalities in thoracic radiographs of dogs and cats. The course while going over anatomy of the thorax, cardiac interpretation, pulmonary patterns such as interstitial, bronchial and alveolar. By the end of the course you should be able to understand the normal anatomy of the thorax, by able to recognize interstitial, bronchial, and alveolar patterns and be able to describe these patterns to aid case management.

courses.title: Pivot with Purpose: Reimagining Your Veterinary Career
courses.description: Many veterinary technicians reach a point where they question whether this is the career they want to build a future around. This session is for anyone asking that question. Veterinary technicians develop an incredible set of skills, but we do not always recognize how many places those skills can take us. Those skills are more transferable than most people realize, and there are real opportunities worth considering outside the traditional path. Whether you are feeling stuck, considering a change, or simply curious about your options, this session can help you reconsider what your experience makes possible beyond the exam room.

courses.title: Navigating Construction, Design, and Financing Challenges for Veterinary Hospitals
courses.description:
This should briefly describe what a participant can expect during the course. This will be used in the CE Broker website search for upcoming CE/CME, and should have searchable keywords, so an attendee is able to locate the course based on their interest. For example, if this program was about the RACE Standards, I might state, "This course covers who qualifies to give a Medical presentation based on the 2023 RACE Standards. We will discuss when letters of reference are needed and what may disqualify an individual from being accepted as a presenter of a RACE program".
This course covers the construction, design, and financing decisions veterinary practice owners face when starting up, expanding, or relocating a hospital. We will discuss how to evaluate real estate and buildout options, assemble the right team of real estate, lending, and construction partners, compare SBA, conventional, and 504/504 Green loan structures, and build realistic project budgets. Attendees will also learn how lenders evaluate borrowers using the five C's of credit so they can prepare stronger, better-supported loan applications.

courses.provider: DBA VETERINARY DENTISTRY EDUCATION AND CONSULTING SERVICES
courses.title: Fundamental Canine and Feline Dentistry and Surgical Extractions
courses.description: This 16-hour CE course (8 hours of lecture and 8 hours of laboratory) is for veterinarians only. It is instructed by two Board Certified Veterinary Dentists. The 8-hour didactic course curriculum will start with canine and feline nomenclature and examination for foundation followed by lectures that will include canine and feline malocclusions, periodontal disease and management, fractured teeth, intraoral radiography interpretation, canine and feline tooth resorption and treatment, oral inflammation and stomatitis, regional analgesia, miscellaneous common dental and oral pathology (e.g., dentigerous cysts, retained deciduous teeth, feline pyogenic granulomas), and step-by-step mucoperiosteal flaps and surgical extractions. The laboratory portion will be hands on wet lab (canine cadavers and teaching models) with regional nerve block administration, intraoral radiographic positioning, surgical extraction of teeth with mucoperiosteal flaps, and subgingival crown amputation with intentional root retention. The course will provide canine and feline dentistry education and skills for primary care veterinary practice.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Acute to Chronic: Practical Internal Medicine and Emergency/Critical Care in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: This EUVETCE Experiences seminar is designed to provide attending veterinary professionals (veterinarians and technicians) with practical and up-to-date insights on internal medicine and emergency/critical care in feline and canine patients. The seminar focuses on a practical approach to the acute abdomen, recognition and management of shock with a current update on fluid therapy, common cardiac emergencies in cats and dogs, localizing dyspnea, diabetic ketoacidosis in cats, diagnosis and management of acute pancreatitis in dogs, urethral obstruction in cats, and a practical approach to immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA). Additionally, the seminar will address the spectrum of renal disease, covering acute kidney injury as well as the diagnosis and long-term management of chronic kidney disease in cats and dogs. It will also offer updates and practical guidance on chronic gastrointestinal presentations - including the diagnostic approach to chronic vomiting in cats and chronic diarrhea in dogs - and on the recognition and management of copper storage hepatopathy in dogs.
courses.location: Radisson Collection Hotel, Magdalena Plaza Sevilla

courses.title: Advanced Veterinary Acupuncture for Small Animals - Series 1
courses.description: This 6-module advanced veterinary acupuncture series provides 37 hours of medical education for veterinarians, bridging foundational acupuncture training with advanced clinical application in small animal practice. Through lectures, case-based learning, interactive discussions, and mentorship, participants develop practical strategies for integrating acupuncture and complementary modalities into multimodal treatment plans for neurologic, musculoskeletal, behavioral, gastrointestinal, pain, and oncology cases. The curriculum combines Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM), medical acupuncture, evidence-based approaches, rehabilitation, nutrition, herbal medicine, essential oils, and other integrative therapies to improve clinical decision-making, treatment planning, and patient outcomes.

courses.title: Advanced Veterinary Acupuncture Series 2
courses.description: This 6-module advanced veterinary acupuncture series provides 37 hours of medical education for veterinarians, bridging foundational acupuncture training with advanced clinical application in small animal practice. Through lectures, case-based learning, interactive discussions, and mentorship, participants develop practical strategies for integrating acupuncture and complementary modalities into multimodal treatment plans for oncology, dermatology, cardiology, endocrinology, and respiratory disorders in small animal patients. The curriculum integrates Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM), medical acupuncture, evidence-based approaches, nutrition, herbal medicine, essential oils, rehabilitation, and other complementary therapies to strengthen clinical decision-making, treatment planning, and patient outcomes.

courses.provider: AMERICAN KENNEL CLUB CANINE HEALTH FOUNDATION
courses.title: Understanding Protein-Losing Enteropathy in Dogs: New Genetic Insights
courses.description: Canine protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by loss of protein due to disease of the small intestine, but the mechanisms that lead to protein loss are not well understood. This webinar will explore the use of whole exome sequencing to investigate potential genetic causes of PLE in dogs and how discoveries in human PLE are informing this approach. Attendees will learn how identifying genetic variants and disease mechanisms could support future development of genetic screening and new therapeutic approaches for affected dogs.

courses.provider: AMERICAN KENNEL CLUB CANINE HEALTH FOUNDATION
courses.title: Aging in Dogs: Understanding Canine Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome
courses.description: Canine Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome (CCDS) can be difficult to distinguish from normal age-related changes in dogs, and historically there have been no consensus guidelines for its diagnosis. This webinar will explore the development of a standardized framework for diagnosing and staging CCDS, including approaches to evaluating cognitive and behavioral changes in aging dogs. Attendees will learn how consistent diagnostic criteria can support clinical care and advance research into canine cognitive aging.

courses.title: Ophthalmology Basics -What it Takes to Tackle an Eye Case
courses.description: In this 4-hour, LIVE seminar, Shelby Reinstein, DVM, MS, DACVO will present an in depth review of the basics of high-level general practice ophthalmology, including up-to-date medication recommendations, a step-by-step eye exam, and a review of the diagnostics for ocular and orbital diseases.

courses.title: Rabbit Anesthesia
courses.description: This talk presents the unique aspects of rabbit anesthesia. It will provide an overview of the anatomic and physiologic considerations for this species and discuss pre-anesthesia assessment and preparation, anesthetic drugs, analgesia, general anesthesia and monitoring, and recovery of the rabbit patient.

courses.title: Diagnosing and Managing Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease (MMVD) without an Echocardiogram
courses.description: Clinical cardiac work ups may include diagnostics such as blood pressure measurement, electrocardiogram (ECG), 24 hour ambulatory ECG Holter monitor, echocardiogram, thoracic radiographs, cardiac biomarkers (e.g., troponin I, NT proBNP), cardiac gated CT scan, cardiac catheterization, and cardiac MRI. Cardiac diagnostics will vary based on the suspected type of heart disease. In the face of financial constraints or absence of a cardiologist, how can the primary care clinician navigate their patients cardiac disease? This presentation will review ACVIM staging, diagnosis without an echocardiogram, and management for dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease.

courses.title: NT-proBNP in Practice: From Cardiac Signal to Clinical Decision
courses.description: This session reviews the clinical use of NT-proBNP as a cardiac biomarker in dogs and cats. Attendees will learn the physiologic basis of NT-proBNP release and its role as a marker of myocardial stretch. Practical applications in general and specialty practice will be discussed, including differentiation of cardiac versus non-cardiac disease, triage of clinical signs, and support of referral decisions. Emphasis will be placed on appropriate test selection, interpretation within clinical context, and limitations of NT-proBNP testing.

courses.title: One Life to Love: MMVD Made Practical Diagnose Smarter, Treat Sooner
courses.description: This course provides a practical, case-based approach to Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease (MMVD) in dogs, with an emphasis on early diagnosis, disease staging, and evidence-based treatment decisions. Participants can expect a focused review of ACVIM MMVD staging (A-D), criteria for identifying Stage B2 disease, and guidance on when to initiate pimobendan therapy. The program explores murmur grading, thoracic radiography (VHS/VLAS), home respiratory rate monitoring, and strategies for monitoring progression when echocardiography is not available. Emerging AI-assisted diagnostic tools, including digital stethoscope technology, will be discussed as clinical decision-support resources to improve confidence, efficiency, and client communication in everyday veterinary practice.

courses.provider: OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY - CARLSON COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: The Gut Microbiome and Cancer: From Research Discoveries to Veterinary Clinical Trials
courses.description: This continuing education program provides an overview of the rapidly growing field linking the gut microbiome to cancer biology and treatment in humans, and new developments in this field in veterinary medicine. The first part of the program will cover the scientific foundations of how gut microbiota influence cancer development, progression, and treatment response, including recent research findings from canine oncology cohorts demonstrating that microbiome composition predicts survival outcomes in dogs receiving immunotherapy. The second part will present ongoing clinical trials at the Bridge Animal Referral Center (BARC) evaluating Fecal Microbiota Transplant (FMT) to reduce chemotherapy-related gastrointestinal toxicity in dogs treated with Palladia (toceranib phosphate). The program will also discuss the translational significance of the canine cancer model for advancing microbiota-targeted therapies in both veterinary and human medicine.
courses.location: Gary R. Carlson, MD, College of Veterinary Medicine

courses.title: Infectious Disease Hot Topics and Vaccination Strategies
courses.description: This presentation goes over core and non-core vaccinations for dogs and cats per AAHA and AAFP vaccine guidelines, individual risk factors and helps determine clinic vaccination protocols. The course focuses on leptospirosis, Lyme disease, Feline Calicivirus, Feline Leukemia Virus and vaccine safety principles.

courses.title: The Power of Four: Protection Against Common and Emerging Parasite Threats_1.0CE
courses.description:
This comprehensive program provides veterinary professionals with a deep dive into the world of canine parasitology, exploring common and emerging threats, and introduces a recently approved comprehensive parasiticide protection product for dogs. Attendees will gain practical knowledge and insights to enhance their ability to diagnose, treat, and prevent parasitic infections in dogs.
The program begins with a foundational review of common internal (hookworms, roundworms, tapeworms, heartworms) and external parasites (fleas and ticks) affecting dogs, covering disease states, lifecycles, and key diagnostic features. It then focuses on emerging threats, particularly Echinococcus tapeworms, providing recent research updates and public health implications. Attendees will also review other important cestodes such as Taenia spp. and Dipylidium spp., including lifecycle, transmission, and diagnostic considerations.
Next, the program explores four key parasiticide molecules crucial for comprehensive parasite control: lotilaner, moxidectin, pyrantel, and praziquantel. Attendees will learn about the mechanism of action, spectrum of activity, and safety profile of each molecule. Lastly, attendees will receive an introduction to a recently approved parasiticide product for dogs, including detailed information about safety, efficacy, and unique features.

courses.title: Navigating Sarcomas: Osteosarcoma, Hemangiosarcoma, and More
courses.description: Mesenchymal tumors, including soft tissue sarcomas, hemangiosarcoma, and osteosarcoma, pose unique diagnostic and treatment challenges in veterinary oncology. This lecture explores the cytologic and histologic characteristics of sarcomas, as well as their biologic behavior, metastatic patterns, and implications for staging. Attendees will learn how to assist with advanced diagnostics, recognize the nuances of the different treatment option, and manage patient care with a focus on comfort and mobility. The technicians role in surgical support, pain management, client education, and long-term monitoring will be emphasized throughout.

courses.title: Hind Sight is 20/20: A Practical Guide to Hind Limb Lameness and Arthritis in Dogs
courses.description: In this 1 hour seminar we will discuss differentials, diagnosis, and management of common causes of hind limb lameness in dogs.

courses.title: Management of Fulminant Liver Failure in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This lecture will cover the basic pathophysiology of liver failure based on current veterinary literature, including some of the scoring systems used to help prognosticate these cases for practitioners. We will place special emphasis on the most common liver toxins in cats and dogs and on the management of hepatic encephalopathy. Finally, we will discuss the common treatments for acute liver failure as well as some individual therapies for specific toxins.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Common Oral Pathology
courses.description: The final session of our dental webinar series will expand into common oral pathology, highlighting conditions that veterinarians are most likely to encounter in daily practice. Topics will include the identification and treatment of discolored teeth, enamel defects, fractured teeth, granulomas, tooth wear, persistent deciduous teeth, unerupted teeth and dentigerous cysts, oral tumors, feline tooth resorption, and maxillofacial trauma triage. The importance of a thorough oral exam will be emphasized throughout as the cornerstone of diagnosis and treatment.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series: Oral Exam
courses.description: The opening session of the series will provide a strong foundation in the fundamentals of the oral exam, beginning with the instruments and equipment needed, along with proper patient positioning for dental procedures. Attendees will review dental anatomy in detail, including tooth structure, the components of the periodontium, and surrounding paradental structures, before learning the tooth numbering system and root configurations. Malocclusions will be introduced, and a step-by-step demonstration will highlight how to conduct a thorough oral exam in just five to seven minutes.

courses.title: When There's a Bone Marrow Issue. PIMA, IMN and Other Immune-mediated Disorders
courses.description:
This session will explore the spectrum of immune-mediated bone marrow
disorders with a focus on precursor-directed immune-mediated anemia (PIMA) and immune-mediated neutropenia (IMN). Attendees will examine diagnostic considerations, marrow changes, and therapeutic strategies while comparing these disorders to immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA). The presentation will also highlight expected outcomes and long-term management considerations for affected patients.

courses.title: Intro to TPLO
courses.description: TPLO has become a favorite technique of general and specialty veterinarians to treat CrCL tears in all sizes of dogs. TPLO stabilizes the stifle by eliminating cranial tibial thrust. TPLO is an excellent technique for treating partial and complete tears of the CrCL. This interactive course includes lectures and laboratories to teach participants the theory and method of tibial plateau leveling osteotomy TPLO. Participants will perform TPLOs on plastic bones and cadavers using state of the art equipment and implants. Participants will use locking plate technology to simplify increase precision and reduce complications of the procedure. Participants should have a basic knowledge of anatomy and surgical approach to the stifle and principles of bone plate application. Postoperative radiographs will be taken to assess the participants' repair technique. Postoperative management will also be discussed.

courses.title: Technical Animal Rescue for Veterinarians
courses.description: Animal Technical Rescue (ATR) for Veterinarians prepares the participant for emergency response to ATR incidents involving entanglement, entrapment, or recumbency. It provides critical care concepts for emergencies in prehospital settings involving trauma and medically compromised patients. The participant will learn about improvised and commercially made rescue equipment, use concepts and techniques to help resolve an ATR. The course provides context for accessing resources and utilizing them on scene within the framework of the Incident Command System (ICS). With a hybrid learning format, Participants review reading materials and study sheets prior to class time. This material builds on existing veterinary practice. Classroom time will reinforce concepts, then participants will practice skills to roll, rotate, pivot, lift, or haul a recumbent animal forward, backwards, and sideways.
courses.location: Univ. of Arizona, College of Veterinary Medicine

courses.title: (LIVE COURSE) Updates in The Management of Anaesthetic Complications
courses.description: This 3-week online course for veterinary nurses and technicians focuses on the recognition and management of common anaesthetic complications. We will cover the big three: hypotension, hypothermia and abnormal respiration, along with a number of others, including vomiting/regurgitation, and prolonged anaesthetic recovery. Each week emphasises practical monitoring, early intervention, and clear communication with the veterinary team required to manage these complications in a stress-free manner - so you can support your patient in the best way possible.

courses.title: Liver Let Die: A Practical Approach to Elevated Liver Enzymes
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive, practical approach to interpreting elevated liver enzymes in dogs and cats. We will review hepatic anatomy and physiology before examining the specific liver enzymes and liver function tests-- ALT, AST, ALP (including the liver, bone, and corticosteroid isoenzymes), GGT, total bilirubin, and bile acids-- and what each reveals about hepatocellular injury versus cholestasis. Attendees will learn a step-by-step diagnostic algorithm for both the symptomatic and asymptomatic patient, including when to retest, when to pursue liver function testing, and how to use radiography, ultrasound, cytology, histopathology, and culture. The course also covers drug-induced enzyme elevation, vacuolar hepatopathy, and breed-specific hepatic diseases in dogs (Bedlington Terrier, Labrador Retriever, Doberman Pinscher, and Dalmatian) as well as feline breed-associated liver disease. Participants will leave with a confident, systematic framework for working up abnormal liver enzymes in daily practice.

courses.title: Food Allergies and Diet Trials Challenges and Solutions
courses.description: An hour-long CE lecture aimed at helping small animal veterinarians overcome the most common challenges of working up food allergies and performing elimination diet trials

courses.title: 2026 Talbot Veterinary Informatics Symposium
courses.description: This is the Association for Veterinary Informatics' 32nd Annual Symposium! Named for professor, dean, and informatics pioneer Dr. Richard Talbot, DVM, PhD., the Talbot Veterinary Informatics Symposium began in 1995. Our mission is to guide and transform the veterinary profession in understanding, using and extending the practice of informatics and artificial intelligence. Veterinary clinical informatics is a rapidly evolving science that blends information technology, communications, social and behavioral science, and veterinary medicine to improve the quality and safety of patient care. Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in veterinary medicine for diagnostic imaging interpretation, predictive risk modeling, clinical decision support tools and automation of medical record documentation. These help practitioners identify disease patterns earlier, personalize treatment plans and increase efficiency. This course covers how veterinary medical informatics and artificial intelligence are used in epidemiology, medical data management, veterinary healthcare information technology, and clinical decision support with an emphasis on MEDICINE and health care, NOT business and management.

courses.title: Functional Mushrooms in Animal Health
courses.description:
Functional mushrooms are increasingly incorporated into companion-animal supplements and integrative veterinary care, yet clinicians often encounter inconsistent terminology, variable product formats, and differing interpretations of the available evidence. This course provides a practical, evidence-informed overview of functional mushrooms and their use in animal health.
The session will cover a brief background of fungi, including the mushroom life cycle and examples of the historical use of mushrooms in traditional medicine. Participants will review commonly used functional mushroom species and the major classes of bioactive compounds associated with them.
This webinar will provide an overview of commercial mushroom products, including insights into how different types of mushroom-derived ingredients are manufactured and what quality considerations are important to consider when selecting a mushroom-based supplement.
The course will explore proposed and evidence-supported relationships among mushroom-derived compounds, the gut microbiome, immune signaling, and host physiology. Attendees will learn practical guidance on how to better evaluate product quality and safety, dosing considerations, applications, and how to best integrate functional mushrooms into patient care plans.

courses.title: Management of Feline Urethral Obstruction and New Evidence on Dietary Modification
courses.description: Feline urethral obstruction (UO) is one of the most common and life-threatening emergencies encountered in small animal practice. Rapid recognition and appropriate intervention are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. This lecture will review the pathophysiology of urethral obstruction, emergency stabilization of the blocked cat, electrolyte and acid-base derangements, evidence-based approaches to urinary catheterization and analgesia, post-obstructive care, and strategies to reduce recurrence. Current literature and practical clinical recommendations will be discussed to improve outcomes in cats presenting with urethral obstruction.

courses.title: Low-Stress Handling: Practical Techniques for Reducing Fear, Anxiety, and Stress in the Clinical Setting
courses.description: This one-hour course provides veterinary doctors and technicians with practical, evidence-informed techniques for reducing fear, anxiety, and stress (FAS) during veterinary visits. Attendees will learn to recognize early signs of FAS in dogs and cats, apply low-stress handling and restraint alternatives in day-to-day clinical workflows, and understand how team-wide adoption of these techniques improves patient welfare, staff safety, and client satisfaction.

courses.title: Electrochemotherapy in Small Animal Oncology
courses.description: This course is focused on electrochemotherapy as a therapeutic modality for neoplasms in the dog and cat. The technique by which electrochemotherapy is delivered and situations in which it is indicated will be discussed.

courses.title: What the Blood Gas is Trying to Tell You
courses.description: What the Blood Gas is Trying to Tell You reviews a practical, step-by-step approach to acid-base analysis using common clinical case examples. Participants will learn how to interpret key blood gas values, differentiate primary acid-base disturbances, and develop appropriate differential diagnoses. The course also highlights the clinical utility of point-of-care blood gas analysis and demonstrates how blood gas results can be used to rapidly guide diagnostic and treatment decisions.

courses.title: Optimizing CKD Care: Trust Your Gut
courses.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common in older dogs and cats. Diagnosing and staging this disease is an important part of management. Nutrition has long been a cornerstone of disease management, and strategies for nutritional intervention of CKD will be discussed. A new approach to dietary management of CKD through manipulation of the gut-kidney axis with prebiotic fibers will be introduced. The results of studies using this fiber technology in dogs and cats will be reviewed, as will the overall importance of nutrition in disease management.

courses.title: Alphabet Soup of BRD Therapy: AMR, ICE & PTI
courses.description: This presentation will describe the antimicrobial resistance in the context of bacteria important in Bovine Respiratory Disease (BRD) complex. Numerous antibiograms with MIC determinations from field isolates from Mannheimia haemolytica, Pasteurella multocida and Histophilus somni will be presented and described. The Integrative-Conjugative elements (ICE) will be introduced and its role in multi-drug resistance discussed. The value of post-treatment intervals (PTI) in developing and implementing sustainable antimicrobial stewardship management protocol will be introduced.

courses.title: Garden State Veterinary Services Continuing Education: Neurology
courses.description:
This program will provide one hour of medical lecture with a topic covering neurology.
"When to Worry, When to Treat, When to Refer: Practical Neurology for the General Practitioner" (1 hour) Christian Woelfel, DVM, DACVIM (Neurology) & Jordan Schachar, DVM, DACVIM (Neurology).
courses.location: Garden State Veterinary Services, Woodbridge, NJ

courses.title: Seeing Through the Haze: A Practical Approach to Canine Non-Ulcerative Keratitis (OPHT202)
courses.description: With non-ulcerative keratitis, it can often be difficult to determine the underlying diagnosis. Even though dry eye sounds easy to diagnose, what do you do when the Schirmer tear test is normal? The course will cover how to make that diagnosis and the most up-to-date treatment options available. In addition, pigmentary keratitis, pannus, episcleritis, and the confusing corneal opacities will be discussed. You will be given tips on how to visualize lesions and recognize what you are seeing.

courses.title: NC Wildlife Medicine Symposium 2026
courses.description: Wildlife medicine is a growing field of veterinary medicine that impacts our local communities as well as global human and ecological health systems. Our symposium aims to present topics that span the breadth of this impact, from the latest clinical wildlife medicine techniques to research and conservation, encompassing a wide array of species. Speakers are experts in the fields of avian, exotic, zoological, aquatic, preventative health, and wildlife medicine. Eighteen (18.0) hours of continuing education are provided for veterinarians and veterinary technicians. Wildlife rehabilitators, students, and others interested in the above-mentioned fields are all welcome and encouraged to attend.

courses.title: Advances in Total Hip Replacements
courses.description:
2. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: Provide updates on new techniques and procedures available for total hip replacements.
3. LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
a. Review of anatomy
b. Review of hip dysplasia and pathophysiology
c. Arthroscopic techniques
d. Discuss candidates for surgery
e. Review of post-op care and complications Review of post-op care and complications

courses.title: Four Core Communication Skills for Veterinarians
courses.description: Communication is of vital importance in practice. We utilize it with our team and our clients. While it is essential, it is not always easy, nor are we taught how to be proficient at it. This workshop teaches participants about the Four Core Communication skills: Non-verbal, Open-ended questions, Reflective Listening and Empathy. Examples on how each can be implemented within the veterinary environment will be shared so attendees will have choices that they can use with their own clients.

courses.title: Cranial Closing Wedge Ostectomy Wet Lab
courses.description: This course will review the biomechanics of cruciate ligament deficient stifles and the treatment of canine cranial cruciate ligament disease, highlighting cranial closing wedge ostectomy (CCWO). CCWO is an option in dogs that have a steep tibial plateau or joint angle, such as the West Highland Terrier (Westies) and involve removing a portion of bone during surgery. It can also be a preferred method of treatment in smaller dogs where techniques like TTA may be difficult. Review of patient selection, instrumentation, pre- and post- surgical treatment and key objectives of CCWO surgery are discussed in detail before hands-on application techniques are practiced. Attendees will begin on a bone model before measuring and surgeries are performed on cadavers. The cadavers are then radiographed and reviewed, giving attendees real-time feedback before a second cadaver surgery and radiograph review.

courses.provider: NORTHERN CALIFORNIA ASSOCIATION OF EQUINE PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: NCAEP Fall Imaging Conference
courses.description:
Join the Northern California Association of Equine Practitioners for an engaging Fall Continuing Education Event focused on advances in equine diagnostic imaging, surgical intervention, and rehabilitation. The event will be held at UCD Valley Hall and will conclude with a tour of the new CEH Rehabilitation Center, hosted by Dr. Morgan.
Expert presenters will share practical insights into the diagnosis and management of subchondral injuries, the expanding clinical applications of equine computed tomography (CT), and current approaches to cervical vertebral surgery. The program will also explore rehabilitation strategies designed to support recovery, restore function, and improve long-term outcomes following musculoskeletal and neurologic injuries.

courses.title: Advanced Canine Reproduction (REPR101)
courses.description: This course will enable veterinarians and veterinary technicians/technologists to assist breeders with more complex reproductive scenarios, becoming a valued "breeder" veterinary resource.

courses.title: Veterinary Ventures Turks & Caicos 2026
courses.description: This course covers two specialty topics commonly encountered by the general practitioner & ER veterinarian - internal medicine and oncology. Dr. Cridge will discuss common internal medicine conditions and treatments. Dr. Binstock will discuss common cancers of the dog and cat, chemotherapy, and advances in oncology. This will be an interactive medical presentation. This is a 3 day conference that will provide 15 hours of RACE approved CE credits.

courses.title: 2026 Applied Reproductive Strategies in Beef Cattle
courses.description:
The Applied Reproductive Strategies in Beef Cattle Conference is hosted by the Beef Reproduction
Task Force, an academic group, and industry counterparts, who together form the Beef Reproduction Leadership Team.
See BeefRepro.org/ARSBC. Considered the premier educational program on beef cattle reproduction, this year's conference
brings together 16 nationally recognized speakers on various aspects of practical reproductive management. Topics will
include current research on nutritional management, bull fertility, genetics and reproduction, estrus synchronization
protocols, and application of this information in production settings.
courses.location: Holiday Inn DesMoines – Aiport / Conference Center

courses.title: 2027 28th Annual AAEP Resort Symposium
courses.description: This lecture and seminar-based symosium, features live speakers and interactive A&A sessions as well as panel discussion. It is designed to strengthen the clinical and field skills of equine practitioners. Sessions will provide practical updates and advanced techniques in pain management, reproduction, neonatology, imaging, sports medicine, and podiatry. Participants will learn current strategies for managing pain in both field and hospital settings, with a focus on the latest therapeutic options. The program will also provide advanced instruction in cycle management and approaches to the problem mare, equipping veterinarians with up-to-date tools for reproductive practice. Skills in neonatal care will be expanded through case-based learning that emphasizes practical application in ambulatory medicine. In addition, attendees will refine their use of abdominal ultrasound, including guided techniques, to improve diagnostic imaging. The symposium also highlights the integration of sports medicine and podiatry therapies to enhance lameness diagnosis and management in the field. Panel discussions and interactive case reviews will encourage direct engagement with subject matter experts, fostering collaborative learning and practical problem-solving that participants can immediately apply to their own practice.

courses.title: VetCE Virtual: Beyond Bad Behavior - Understanding Canine and Feline Behaviour Disorders
courses.description: This VetCE Virtual set of 3 live distance presentations includes topics of interest presented by experts. The presentations are held on separate dates. Attendees enroll in all three and must attend all to earn the completion certificate. The first presentation is on September 14, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Easy as one, two, pee: Solving Feline Housesoiling. The 2nd is on September 21, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Resource Guarding of Food. The 3rd and final presentation is on September 28, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Addressing the Medical Components of Behavior Cases. The VetCE Virtual series of micro-conferences are a convenient alternative to in-person events and are designed to deliver multiple RACE and/or CVPM approved CE credits in a virtual format with three one-hour presentations. They provide educational sessions presented by expert speakers, and an easy way to learn and earn credits in the comfort of your home or office.

courses.title: Veterinary Cardiorespiratory Symposium
courses.description:
Cardiac and respiratory diseases in small animals represent some of the most complex challenges in veterinary medicine, particularly due to the frequent overlap in their clinical presentation.
This symposium will provide a practical and clinically focused overview of the recognition, diagnosis, management, and long-term monitoring of cardiac and respiratory disorders in dogs and cats. Particular emphasis will be placed on identifying subtle clinical signs, applying advanced diagnostic techniques, including radiography, echocardiography, electrocardiography, and blood gas analysis and implementing evidence-based treatment strategies for both acute and chronic cases.
The program will also address anesthetic considerations and the challenges associated with managing patients with concurrent cardiac and respiratory disease, underscoring the importance of individualized care and interdisciplinary collaboration.
In addition, the symposium will include a hands-on echocardiography session designed to strengthen clinical confidence and enhance practical skills in the management of these complex cases.

courses.title: GI Deep Dive: Diets, Dysbiosis, and Esophageal Disorders in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: In this 3-hour, LIVE seminar with Dr. Christina Marino, DVM, DACVIM, participants will explore comprehensive strategies for diagnosing and managing complex gastrointestinal and esophageal conditions in dogs and cats. The program covers the modern definitions of chronic enteropathies with an emphasis on diet-responsive enteropathies, tailored dietary selection beyond standard options, and strategic supplementation. It dives into the development and manipulation of the gut microbiome, detailing dysbiosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics in acute diarrhea. Finally, the seminar reviews the anatomy and function of the oropharynx and esophagus, providing clear diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for dysphagia, regurgitation, and megaesophagus.

courses.title: Creepy Crawlies: Are You Sleeping with the Enemy?
courses.description: A thorough understanding of parasite lifecycle, prevalence, their medical impact as well as control methods is important in determining the best medical recommendations for your patients. In this presentation these key aspects will be discussed for fleas and the common ticks infecting canine patients.

courses.title: Leading With Intention: Building the Career and Culture You Want
courses.description:
Your first position after graduation will shape you but it should never define you.
Veterinary hospitals vary widely in their cultures, expectations, workflows, and utilization of team members. Learning to recognize those differences and intentionally choosing environments that align with your values and professional goals is an essential skill that is rarely taught in school. This session prepares participants to navigate the realities of veterinary practice with confidence, professionalism, and discernment while understanding how every member of the veterinary team contributes to exceptional patient care.
Participants will explore how to become a positive influence regardless of title by leading themselves first. Topics include understanding interdisciplinary roles, building professional credibility, advocating respectfully, navigating workplace dynamics, recognizing healthy versus unhealthy workplace cultures, and contributing to solutions rather than drama.
Discussion will also include strategies for evaluating prospective employers, establishing healthy boundaries, and maintaining professionalism in environments that may not always reflect the kind of veterinary medicine they hope to practice.
Through practical examples and guided reflection, participants will leave with a framework for making intentional career decisions, strengthening the teams they join, and becoming the kind of colleague who elevates the people and culture around them. Rather than simply adapting to veterinary medicine as it exists today, attendees will be challenged to become part of the profession they hope to create for tomorrow.

courses.title: There's Something I Need to Get Off My Chest: A Guide to Better Thoracic Radiographs
courses.description: The goal of the presentation is to help technicians understand a little more about thoracic radiographs and positioning so that they are more able to assess the quality of the images obtained, independently make corrections when needed, and take additional views when necessary.

courses.title: Controlled Substance Records and Security: Requirements and Reminders
courses.description: Are you confident that your practice's controlled substance records are complete and accurate? Are you taking proper steps to prevent diversion of your supplies of controlled substances? If the DEA came to your office tomorrow, could you pass a thorough inspection? If you're saying to yourself "I'm not sure...", this webinar will deliver information to help you evaluate and improve your practice's administration and management of controlled substances, including benzodiazepines and opioid medication. You'll learn the basics of essential required records, important security considerations, and some of the most common mistakes. Taught by DEA Diversion Group Supervisor Jed Nitzberg, a Portland-based investigator with 12 years of experience, you'll have a chance to ask questions and pick up valuable tips that can help protect your practice.

courses.provider: DBA VETERINARY DENTISTRY EDUCATION AND CONSULTING SERVICES
courses.title: Fundamental Canine and Feline Dentistry and Surgical Extractions
courses.description: This 16-hour CE course (8 hours of lecture and 8 hours of laboratory) is for veterinarians only. It is instructed by two Board Certified Veterinary Dentists. The 8-hour didactic course curriculum will start with canine and feline nomenclature and examination for foundation followed by lectures that will include canine and feline malocclusions, periodontal disease and management, fractured teeth, intraoral radiography interpretation, canine and feline tooth resorption and treatment, oral inflammation and stomatitis, regional analgesia, miscellaneous common dental and oral pathology (e.g., dentigerous cysts, retained deciduous teeth, feline pyogenic granulomas), and step-by-step mucoperiosteal flaps and surgical extractions. The laboratory portion will be hands on wet lab (canine cadavers and teaching models) with regional nerve block administration, intraoral radiographic positioning, surgical extraction of teeth with mucoperiosteal flaps, and subgingival crown amputation with intentional root retention. The course will provide canine and feline dentistry education and skills for primary care veterinary practice.

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.
