courses.title: 2027 Foundational Skills
courses.description: This course provides lectures, seminars, workshops and hands on learning aimed at early-career veterinarians including clinical topics such as : reproduction basics, podiatry basics, euthanasia, field necropsy, how to manage a down horse as well as business topics such as emergency planning/disaster planning, fiannces, medical records and mindset/motivation. Wet labs are part of the educational process with this program and include labs in medicine, neurology, ophthalmology, endoscopy, dental oral exams, ocular exams, dental radiology, ocular nerve blocks, SPL Placement, nasolacrimal duct flush, tarsorrhaphy, temporary tacking (eye), ultrasound of the neck and abdomen, odontoplasty, enucleation, cranial nerve and moving neuro exam as well as business lectures on contract negotiations and managing difficult client conversations.

courses.title: Eyes on Surgery: Ophthalmic Pearls and Procedures
courses.description: This live, interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will feature case presentations of common ophthalmic conditions to strengthen clinical decision-making around diagnosis, medical management, and surgical intervention. This course will review when continued medical management is appropriate, when surgery offers the best outcome, plus how to educate clients on surgical expectations and post-operative care.

courses.title: Fetch National Harbor 2026, part 2
courses.description: Fetch, a dvm360 conference, at National Harbor (part 2) is a live interactive, in-person conference with a combination of both medical and non-medical programs created for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers to achieve their continuing education in veterinary medicine. Educational content tracks include: Feline Medicine, Hands-on Lab; Endoscopy, Infectious Disease, Internal Medicine, and Pain Management

courses.title: Peripheral Nerve Block Wetlab
courses.description: This full day Peripheral Nerve Block Wetlab is a hands-on workshop designed for veterinary professionals who want to master techniques that can provide regional analgesia to the oral cavity and head. Attendees will receive brief didactic training on local anesthetics, as well as peripheral and regional nerve block principles. This will be followed by small groups working with expert guidance to locate nerves and surrounding structures on cadavers, with the goal of mastering multiple analgesic techniques for patients undergoing dental, maxillofacial, auricular and ocular surgery, reducing reliance on opioids and other systemic analgesics. In addition to blocks of the head, time allowing, interested participants will also be able to practice sacrococcygeal epidurals and/or distal extremity blocks.

courses.title: 48th Lake Tahoe Equine Conference
courses.description: PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: This conference will provide 20 hours of in-depth presentations with up-to-date practical clinical information for the equine practitioner or veterinary technician. Come enjoy high quality CE in a unique format that also allows ample time for recreation in beautiful Lake Tahoe. The attendees can expect to receive high quality, practical and up-to-date lectures pertaining to equine medicine and surgery, with emphasis on material they can take back and use in their daily practice. Light breakfast and heavy appetizers with beverages will be provided prior to each morning and evening session. Between sessions, the attendees will have free time to ski or snowboard, or just relax in the beautiful Lake Tahoe region.
courses.location: Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe at Incline Village, Nevada

courses.title: Approach to Radioactive Iodine (I-131)
courses.description: To learn to recognize, diagnose, and treat Hyperthyroidism in cats including paying attention to kidney values, heart and body weight. Recommending the correct form of treatment depending on patient.Going over all treatment modalities

courses.title: Uncovering Veterinary Cattitudes to Provide Better Care
courses.description: Veterinary professionals care for both dogs and cats but do we feel the same way about them? This engaging presentation explores surprising and sometimes uncomfortable differences in veterinary preferences, confidence, experience, and education related to canine versus feline patients. Drawing on survey data from veterinary faculty, staff, and students, the session highlights how cats consistently lag behind dogs and why that matters for feline welfare, client relationships, and professional satisfaction. Attendees will leave with insight into how training, experience, and even personal factors shape species attitudes, along with practical ideas for closing the feline confidence gap and improving care.

courses.title: What Makes a Mast Cell Tumor Aggressive? Evolution of Risk Assessment from Microscope to Molecule
courses.description: Canine mast cell tumors (MCTs) exhibit diverse biological behavior, ranging from lesions cured with surgical excision alone to highly aggressive neoplasms associated with metastasis and cancer-related mortality. Historically, assessment of clinically aggressive behavior relied on histologic appearance and clinical staging. Advances in pathology, molecular diagnostics, and understanding of tumor biology have reshaped our understanding of disease behavior. This session will explore the evolution of risk assessment in canine MCTs, from traditional morphologic grading systems to recent approaches that incorporate proliferation indices, KIT expression patterns, c-kit mutational analysis, and lymph node evaluation. Attendees will also examine emerging concepts involving the tumor microenvironment, tumor heterogeneity, genomic profiling and liquid biopsy-based testing for detection of tumor-associated biomarkers. Through review of key studies and recent literature, participants will gain a practical understanding for integrating diagnostic information to improved prediction of tumor aggressiveness, guide therapeutic decisions, and communicate prognostic assessment in dogs with mast cell neoplasia.

courses.title: Shaping the Diagnosis: The Power of Blood Morphology
courses.description: Automated hematology analyzers provide powerful quantitative data, but important diagnostic insights can be missed when blood morphology is not assessed. This presentation explores the clinical value of blood morphology assessment as a complement to automated CBC results. Through two canine case studies, participants will examine how morphology findings altered diagnostic pathways, improved interpretation of laboratory data, and influenced patient management. Practical guidance will be provided on when morphology review is most important and how morphology findings can be integrated into everyday clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Feline Lower Urinary Track Disease-FLUTD
courses.description:
In this 2 hour long, in-person lecture based meeting, an in-depth review of
feline lower urinary tract disease along with practical case review will occur. Emphasis on the
pathophysiology of the main causes of FLUTD and recommended diagnostics will be discussed.
Both medical and interventional therapies will be discussed, with particular emphasis on feline
idiopathic cystitis

courses.title: The Anesthetists Guide to ECG Basics
courses.description: This presentation is designed to teach the attendee the basic anatomy and physiology of the heart, including the cardiac conduction system and the electrical activity responsible for cardiac contraction. The lecture will then introduce the fundamentals of electrocardiography, including the components of a normal ECG waveform and a systematic approach to evaluating rate, rhythm, and origin. Common ECG abnormalities encountered during anesthesia will be discussed, including atrioventricular blocks, premature ventricular contractions, ventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation, and ventricular fibrillation. Attendees will learn to recognize these abnormal rhythms and understand their significance in the anesthetized patient.

courses.title: DEA Escape Room: Crack the Compliance Code
courses.description:
Step into the role of a DEA compliance officer on your very first day at a bustling veterinary clinic just in time for a surprise audit. In this immersive, escape room style workshop, participants will race against the clock to uncover controlled substance compliance risks, solve medication-use puzzles, and piece together the ultimate Golden Key to airtight drug oversight.
Working collaboratively, teams will progress through seven interconnected challenges that mirror real world controlled-substance management in veterinary practice. From identifying diversion risks and reconciling dispensing discrepancies to determining significant losses, performing inventory calculations, distinguishing waste vs. disposal, and diagnosing missing log entries, each puzzle builds both skill and confidence.
Designed for veterinary professionals and students seeking a highly interactive, hands on learning experience, this session blends problem solving with practical application of DEA requirements and best practices in controlled-substance stewardship. By the end, participants will not only escape with new knowledge they will walk away with a deeper understanding of compliant workflows that protect patients, staff, and the practice.

courses.title: Washington Wildlife Rehabilitation Association Conference 2026
courses.description: This program prepares veterinarians and veterinary technicians for .... in wildlife species.

courses.provider: KIN VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND SPECIALTY CENTER
courses.title: Acute Kidney Injury: A Paradigm Shift
courses.description: A one hour presentation on the dynamic process of acute kidney injury discussing the mechanisms at play, diagnosis, therapeutics and prognosis for patients with impaired kidney function. Key features include fluid therapy in the AKI patient and covering for treatable conditions. Will briefly touch on hemodialysis and specifically discuss AKI in cats, highlighting an under diagnosed condition. Lastly, will show case examples to highlight importance for recognizing patients that are failing medical management to facilitate timely referrals.

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.title: Targeted Relief: Allergic Dermatitis Treatment Options Demystified for Daily Practice_1.0CE
courses.description: The clinical management of canine allergic dermatitis remains a complex challenge for veterinary practitioners and a significant concern for pet owners. This session provides a comprehensive review of the current clinical landscape, including epidemiological trends and the latest expert consensus guidelines for differentiating between allergic and atopic disease. Participants will evaluate various pharmacological classes, focusing on their specific mechanisms of action and indications based on clinical presentation. Furthermore, the program introduces novel therapeutic interventions for the treatment of dogs with allergic and canine atopic dermatitis.

courses.title: Fighting CIRDC (Canine Infectious Respiratory Disease Complex) on Multiple Fronts_1.0CE
courses.description: Attendees will learn about the causative viral and bacterial agents responsible for CIRDC, associated lifestyle and patient risk factors. Updated industry guidelines are presented pertaining to vaccination strategies for CIRDC.

courses.title: Expanding the Modern Toolkit: A Comprehensive Portfolio Approach to Canine Atopy
courses.description: Canine atopic dermatitis is a chronic disease that requires thoughtful and flexible long-term therapeutic strategies. As our understanding of the disease advances, targeted biologic therapies are creating new opportunities to improve outcomes for dogs and their owners. In this session, we will introduce a new monoclonal antibody for the management of pruritus and canine atopic dermatitis. Attendees will gain an understanding of how this new therapy provides veterinarians with an additional choice to help control pruritus and support long-term disease management. Additionally, we will discuss our comprehensive therapeutic portfolio that supports care across the full spectrum of atopic disease. By combining our new monoclonal antibody with a robust therapeutic portfolio and a strong commitment to education, we aim to advance the standard of care for canine atopic dermatitis.

courses.title: Cutting Risk Short: Speed of Tick Kill as a Tool for Canine Tick-Borne Disease Control
courses.description: Ticks and tick-borne diseases continue to pose a significant and evolving threat to canine health across the United States. This presentation will review the most common medically important tick species affecting dogs and examine how speed of tick kill influences the likelihood of pathogen transmission. Particular emphasis will be placed on the blacklegged tick (Ixodes scapularis) and the lone star tick (Amblyomma americanum), including the mechanisms and timing of transmission of their associated pathogens and how rapid tick kill can meaningfully reduce disease risk. The session will also explore how effective tick control can influence the interpretation of commonly used diagnostic tests, helping clinicians better contextualize diagnostic findings in dogs with known tick exposure. In addition, recent data comparing the speed of tick kill among monthly-dosed isoxazoline products--across both existing and newly acquired infestations throughout the dosing interval--will be reviewed. Practical, evidence-based strategies for incorporating speed of tick kill into comprehensive tick-borne disease prevention and client communication will be discussed.

courses.title: TPLO Skills Lab
courses.description:
This workshop is designed specifically for veterinarians who have completed an introductory course in Tibial Plateau Leveling Osteotomy (TPLO) and are seeking to enhance their surgical proficiency. The focus of this hands-on session is to provide a platform for participants to refine their TPLO techniques through multiple cadaveric procedures.
Participants will spend much of their time performing TPLO procedures across the 2-day workshop. The workshop features live demonstrations by experienced instructors, followed by supervised practice. Post-Op radiographs will be taken and discussed.

courses.title: Comprehensive Elbow and Shoulder Forum
courses.description:
This high-impact Forum will equip you with the most in-demand forelimb topics in veterinary surgery:
- The "Shelbow" Solution - Master a streamlined algorithm for evaluating complex shoulder-elbow cases with confidence. Gain practical skills in forelimb assessment, imaging, and decision-making. Learn when to choose¿biceps tenodesis¿versus¿tenotomy, and perform each technique with precision using clear, evidence-based guidelines.
- Elbow Fractures - Sharpen your skills with hands-on techniques for managing complex elbow fractures using anatomic plating and cannulated screws.
- Shoulder Stabilization - Learn the cutting-edge Canine Subscapularis Repair using the SpeedFix Technique and the Shoulder TightRope Stabilization for optimal outcomes.
- Forelimb angular deformity - Deepen your understanding of¿forelimb malalignment assessment¿and surgical correction of angular deformities. Learn advanced techniques, including¿osteotomies,¿plating strategies, and intraoperative pearls to enhance precision and outcomes.
The forum also offers exclusive insights and expert tips on both standard and NanoNeedle arthroscopy of the elbow and shoulder, and hands-on percutaneous approaches to the elbow with fluoroscopy-guided transcondylar pinning, showcasing the latest advancements in minimally invasive treatment techniques.

courses.title: The Leaky Gut: Navigating Canine PLE
courses.description:
Diagnosis, management, and prognosis of canine protein losing enteropathies
Program Agenda:
- Diagnostic approach
- Management options (Diet, Medications, Short and long term monitoring)
- Prognosis
Learning Objectives:
1. Identify common clinical signs, physical exam findings, and labwork abnormalities associated with PLE
2. Differentials associated with canine PLE and diagnostic approach
3. Management depending on disease type
4. Long term prognosis of different causes of PLE

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Periodontal Therapy for the Busy GP
courses.description: This discussion will include a practical focus on periodontal therapy designed for the busy general practitioner. Attendees will review the anatomy of the periodontium, along with the pathogenesis and stages of periodontal disease, to build a clear understanding of how this condition develops and progresses. The discussion will include how to identify periodontal disease on radiographs and outline treatment options appropriate for each stage. Common misconceptions will be addressed, with guidance on how to provide effective, realistic care using the tools and resources typically available in general practice.

courses.title: Toxins Management Overview
courses.description: This course is a 50-minute presentation that covers an overview of toxin management in small animals. We will discuss the general principles of toxicology. Then we will discuss triage and stabilization of toxin exposure including diagnostics, monitoring and supportive care. We will discuss different decontamination techniques including emesis, gastric lavage, activated charcoal and cholestyramine. Finally, we will discuss specific treatment techniques such as ion trapping, lipid therapy, cathartics, reversals and antidotes.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Feline Dental Radiology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the details of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL), and how these technologies differ in both development and application. Both the interpretive and non-interpretive benefits of using AI as a tool to read intraoral dental radiographs will be discussed in detail. Focus will be on how to effectively use AI technology as a tool in dental radiograph interpretation, using case-based discussions that focus on felines. Examples are included to highlight the benefits and limitations of the technology. Emphasis will be placed on incorporating the dental radiographs, results of dental charting, the overall health status of the patient, and the clinician's clinical judgement to identify pathology and formulate a diagnostic and treatment plan, with an emphasis on the unique anatomy and pathologies in cats.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2026 Advanced Strategies in Renal and Urologic Care
courses.description: This advanced 2-day live virtual course will explore the most current and clinically relevant advances in veterinary nephrology and urology. Sessions will integrate recent research with practical applications in chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and lower urinary tract disorders. Topics include FGF-23 and phosphate management, renal biomarkers, microbiome, regenerative medicine, and interventional urology. Interactive panel discussions will allow participants to engage directly with internationally recognized experts and translate cutting-edge insights into practice.

courses.title: Environmental Impacts on Neurodevelopmental and Neurodegenerative Conditions
courses.description: Environmental exposures can negatively impact the developing nervous system and contribute to long-term or cumulative effects that increase the risk of neurodegenerative conditions with age. This course will explore how environmental factors, from air pollution to pesticides, play a role in the pathogenesis of both neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative conditions, as well as ongoing research into prevention and mitigation strategies. The first part of the course will discuss how perinatal exposure to environmental chemicals can disrupt normal neurodevelopment, emerging research tools in this area, and potential protective environmental factors, such as diet. The second half of the course will focus on the role of environmental exposures in the pathology of neurodegenerative conditions, including dementia and Parkinson's disease.

courses.title: Fear Free Microchipping: Reducing Stress While Protecting Pets
courses.description: Utilizing Fear Free methods for microchipping, the importance of microchipping pets

courses.title: Pathologic Basis of Disease (MULT207)
courses.description:
The first of seven courses in the Organ System Pathophysiology and ABVP Series, this course is designed to cover the pathophysiological basis of disease in small animals based on pathophysiological and discipline-specific concepts. Clinical examples will be used to illustrate these concepts.
It is a tour through some aspects of "DAMNITV" in preparation for future modules (which cover diagnosis and a more traditional specialty/body system-based review). Clinical examples will be used to illustrate these concepts; however, the focus is on pathophysiology and also on review of certain discipline-specific material, such as pharmacology, that would not otherwise be covered systematically in the later body-system review-based modules.
The Organ System Pathophysiology and ABVP Examination Review series of courses may be used as a comprehensive review for the ABVP examination for small animals. This series of courses repeats every other year. Individual instructors may change some of their material year-to-year, but much of the core content is repeated.
It should be noted that these courses are not designed specifically as preparation for test-taking. The instructors do not have access to information on the question types. Furthermore, the questions used on the examination may be a few years behind the current knowledge and practice, whereas the course will strive to be more current. We recommend using the course to keep progressing through the topics so all topics will have been studied prior to the exam and provide participants with feedback on their strongest and weakest topics to guide their individual exam specific preparations.

courses.provider: INTERNATIONAL SOCIETY FOR COMPANION ANIMAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE
courses.title: 9th Biennial ISCAID Symposium
courses.description: The ISCAID symposium being held in Dublin, Ireland, September 14 - 17, 2026 brings together the preeminent scholars in companion animal infectious disease to provide research and scientific updates on infectious diseases of dogs and cats. There will be specific focus on feline infectious peritonitis and antimicrobial resistance, but with a wide range of topics pertaining to infectious diseases across the planet.

courses.title: Building Healthy Veterinary Workplaces: The 4 Pillars of Wellbeing and Retention
courses.description: Veterinary teams face unprecedented pressures, and workplace culture is a critical factor in retention, burnout prevention, and patient care. In this session, Dr. Holowaychuk will break down the four pillars of a healthy veterinary workplace; trust, belonging, communication, and sufficient time for quality work; based on recent research. Participants will gain practical strategies to foster psychological safety, strengthen team cohesion, and create an environment where staff thrive and patient care excels.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2026 Unified by Nutrients: A Cross-Specialty Perspective
courses.description: This course gives all clinicians, from a wide range of specialties including nutritionists, internists, criticalists, cardiologists, immunologists, and behaviorists the unique opportunity to deep dive into specific nutrients to enable a more thorough understanding of the pathophysiology of each across a range of diseases. Course content will be delivered by experts in the field and will include cross-specialty perspectives on the role of tryptophan, magnesium, vitamin D and thiamine in a range of diseases. Engage with leaders in their field and expand your expertise, as we place individual nutrients in the spotlight and bridge them across a range of specialties!

courses.provider: CVETS - COLUMBIA VETERINARY EMERGENCY TRAUMA AND SPECIALTY
courses.title: Seize the Day: Practical Management of Canine & Feline Seizures
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical and clinically applicable approach to diagnosing and managing seizures in dogs and cats. Attendees will review seizure recognition, diagnostic workup, emergent stabilization, and maintenance treatment options. There will be an emphasis on evidence-based recommendations that can be applied in general practice.

courses.provider: SOUTH CAROLINA VETERINARY SPECIALISTS & EMERGENCY CARE
courses.title: Fluoroscopy in Everyday Practice: When Dynamic Imaging Changes Patient Care.
courses.description: Fluoroscopy is an underutilized imaging modality in veterinary medicine that provides real-time evaluation of dynamic physiologic processes not readily appreciated with conventional radiography or ultrasonography. This course will focus on the practical applications of fluoroscopy, including videofluoroscopic swallow studies, dynamic airway evaluation, and contrast studies of the lower urinary tract. Participants will learn when fluoroscopy should be considered, how these studies are performed, and how fluoroscopic diagnoses influence medical and surgical decision-making. Emphasis will be placed on recognizing appropriate referral candidates and integrating fluoroscopic findings into everyday clinical practice to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes.

courses.title: Managing Inter-Cat Conflict in Multi-Cat Households (BHVR111)
courses.description: Inter-cat conflict is a common welfare problem that also affects physical health. It is present in most multi-cat homes and is associated with stress-related conditions such as feline idiopathic cystitis, over-grooming, and reduced immune function. Much of it is quiet, building for months as avoidance, resource blocking, and hypervigilance before overt fighting appears, and advising caregivers to let cats work it out usually makes matters worse. This three-week course teaches veterinary professionals to read normal feline behavior, rule out medical causes, diagnose conflict, and reintroduce cats gradually, one sense at a time, with the caregiver communication that makes any plan succeed.

courses.title: Confident Conversations: Recommending Supplements as Part of Routine Care LIVE
courses.description:
Veterinary graduates enter practice with a strong foundation in physiology, pharmacology, and evidence-based clinical reasoning, yet many feel less confident discussing veterinary supplements with clients. Unlike pharmaceuticals, supplements are designed to support normal physiologic function rather than diagnose, prevent, or treat disease, requiring a different approach to evaluation and recommendation.
This session provides a practical framework for integrating veterinary supplements into routine patient care. Participants will learn how to evaluate supplement quality, identify patients who may benefit from physiologic support, recognize when additional diagnostics or medical intervention should take priority, and communicate recommendations with confidence. Through clinical examples and audience discussion, attendees will develop practical strategies for navigating supplement conversations in the exam room while maintaining an evidence-based approach.

courses.title: When, Why, and How to Recommend Veterinary Supplements with Confidence
courses.description:
Veterinary supplements are increasingly incorporated into patient care, yet many clinicians remain uncertain about how to evaluate product quality, determine when supplementation is appropriate, and communicate recommendations with confidence. Rather than viewing supplements as an empirical option or "last resort", veterinarians can apply the same objective clinical reasoning that they use throughout patient care by considering the underlying physiology, biologic rationale, product quality, and available evidence.
This webinar provides a practical framework for assessing veterinary supplements, including how to evaluate manufacturers, ingredient quality, certifications, and supporting research. Through examples from gastrointestinal and dermatologic health, participants will learn how to identify situations where supplementation may support normal physiologic function and complement a comprehensive patient care plan. Attendees will leave with a structured approach for selecting and recommending veterinary supplements that extends beyond anecdotal experience and aligns with clinical decision making.

courses.title: Electrochemotherapy in Companion Animals
courses.description: This comprehensive lecture introduces the principles and clinical applications of electrochemotherapy (ECT) in veterinary medicine. Participants will explore the step-by-step procedural workflow of chemotherapy administration alongside the specific technical execution of ECT. The presentation delves into the biophysical mechanism of action, demonstrating how electrical pulses enhance cellular drug uptake. Finally, attendees will learn optimal case selection criteria, expected outcomes based on specific tumor types, and real-world clinical outcomes through detailed case examples.
courses.location: White Labs Brewing Co - Asheville Kitchen & Tap

courses.title: 2026 Healing Oasis Homecoming Conference
courses.description:
Theme: Resilience in Motion: Comparative Rehabilitation & Manual Therapies for All Beings
Attendees will be provided with many topics addressing comparative rehab and how to use manual therapies to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Dentistry, Radiology and Oral Surgery
courses.description:
2-Day Lecture and Wet Lab Course for Veterinarians
Enhance your veterinary dentistry skills with our 2-Day Lecture and Wet Lab Course designed exclusively for veterinarians seeking to improve their proficiency in oral health assessment, radiographic interpretation, and common dental procedures. While this course covers many topics that are applicable to felines, there is a primary focus on canine dentistry.

courses.title: How Owner-Reported Financial Limitations Negatively Impact Emergency Veterinary Teams
courses.description: Join Dr. Emily McCobb, Dr. Elizabeth Rozanski, and Seana Dowling-Guyer for a free Open Door Veterinary Collective Live Discussion on what happens to veterinary emergency care teams when clients face financial limitations. Drawing on their recent JAVMA publication, Owner-reported financial limitations negatively impact emergency veterinary teams, they will share insights from their research and explore practical, compassionate solutions that support clients, pets, providers, and the practice as a whole.

courses.title: Chronic diarrhea in dogs: why is microbiota knowledge so important
courses.description: The gastrointestinal microbiota is now recognized as a distinct body system, with major roles in digestion, immunity, and metabolic signaling to other organs. This presentation reviews the composition and function of the canine microbiota, the concept and clinical consequences of dysbiosis, and current diagnostic tools such as the Dysbiosis Index. Particular attention is given to the relationship between antimicrobials and the microbiota, including evidence that even short courses of antibiotics can cause dysbiosis lasting weeks to months. With the help of clinical cases, the presentation covers microbiota changes seen in chronic gastrointestinal disease, and outlines evidence-based treatment strategies - nutritional management, prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation - along with updated, more judicious guidelines for antibiotic use in chronic diarrhea. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for managing gastrointestinal cases while protecting the microbiota and reducing unnecessary antimicrobial use.

courses.provider: NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: NC State CVM Companion Animal Behavior Symposium
courses.description: This symposium will cover a variety of veterinary behavioral medical topics for canines and felines, for primary care veterinarians, veterinary technicians, other veterinary professionals, and pet guardians. The program will address a variety of behavioral problems that may be seen in a veterinary setting, some of which may be best served by quickly addressing them or beginning a safety/management protocol while pursuing further intervention with a board-certified veterinary behaviorist
courses.location: NC State College of Veterinary Medicine

courses.title: Hypothermia - What's the hype? (TECH429)
courses.description: Almost all patients undergoing anesthesia or surgery, and most critical patients in shock, will experience some degree of hypothermia - but this doesn't mean it's "normal", or that we shouldn't aggressively try to prevent and control it. There are many negative physiologic implications for these chilly patients, and as technicians and assistants, you can do a lot to keep these patients warm. During this session, we'll uncover the cold, hard facts of hypothermia, as well as preventive measures that can be implemented in the operating room or intensive care unit.

courses.title: Basic Canine Reproduction (REPR100-0127)
courses.description: This course will familiarize veterinarians and technicians with the field of basic canine reproduction, enabling productive interaction with both hobby and professional breeders.

courses.title: From Referral to Recovery: Advancements in Radiation Therapy and Oncology Care
courses.description: This program will focus on Oncology topics for referring veterinarians. The first lecture will review the goals of veterinary oncology as well as resources and topics to help support referring veterinarian clients and patients through a cancer diagnosis. Will review new diagnostic and therapeutic options in the field of veterinary oncology that are available for use as a referring clinician. The second session will discuss the use of stereotactic radiation therapy in veterinary medicine. Also, will discuss case summaries featuring patients with successful radiation treatments.

courses.title: Seeing the Whole Picture: Veterinary Imaging Essentials
courses.description: Whether you're interpreting your first radiographs or looking to refine your diagnostic imaging skills, this comprehensive course provides practical case-based education you can immediately apply in clinical practice. Participants will explore the fundamentals of image acquisition and interpretation, thoracic and abdominal radiology, musculoskeletal and neurologic imaging, point of care ultrasound and expanding role of AI in veterinary medicine. Attendees will develop systematic approach to diagnostic imaging, improve confidence in image interpretation and learn when advanced imaging modalities are warranted. Designed for both GP and emergency clinicians and veterinary technicians, this course emphasizes practical decision-making to improve patient care.

courses.title: Rethinking the Insulin Reflex: SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy for Feline Diabetes Mellitus
courses.description: This course reviews the 2026 AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Cats and critically evaluates four objections commonly raised against SGLT2 inhibitor (bexagliflozin/Bexacat, velagliflozin oral solution/Senvelgo) therapy for newly diagnosed feline diabetes mellitus: perceived monitoring complexity, owner administration burden relative to insulin injections, cost, and the risk of euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis compared with insulin-associated hypoglycemia. Attendees will leave with a practical, evidence-based framework for selecting SGLT2 inhibitor versus insulin therapy in newly diagnosed diabetic cats.

courses.title: Connecting with Empathy to Clients Under Stress
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will review how to have difficult conversations with pet families in crisis to communicate information. This course provides guidance regarding the neurological implications of stress and strategies for the best way to communicate.

courses.title: Navigating Neurology from Localization to Treatment
courses.description: Neuro cases can be intimidating, but a systematic approach makes all the difference. This practical lecture series includes real cases designed for general practitioners and emergency veterinarians and managing common neurological conditions. Topics include neurological examination, seizures, vestibular syndrome, head trauma, IVDD, inflammatory CNS disease (MUO), and diseases of motor unit. Attendees will leave with practical diagnostic and treatment strategies they can implement immediately in everyday clinical practice.

courses.title: Sweet Dreams: Anesthesia, Analgesia & Recovery
courses.description:
Practical Veterinary Anesthesia: From Monitoring to Intervention
This continuing education program provides a practical, case-based approach to the anesthetic management of veterinary patients, with an emphasis on recognizing patient-specific risks, interpreting monitoring data, and responding appropriately to peri-anesthetic complications. The program will address challenging patient populations, including brachycephalic patients, dogs and cats with cardiac disease, and retired racing Greyhounds.
Participants will review the clinical interpretation of arterial blood pressure and electrocardiographic monitoring, including recognition of arrhythmias and determining when intervention is warranted. Additional discussion will focus on anesthetic-associated hyperkalemia in Greyhounds, appropriate clinical use of buprenorphine in dogs and cats, and strategies for selecting supportive and emergency interventions.
Case-based anesthetic scenarios will allow participants to work through complications in real time, emphasizing recognition of anesthetic events, selection of appropriate interventions, assessment of patient response, and modification of treatment when necessary.
Topics include:
Considerations for Managing Brachycephalic Patients
Considerations for Managing Dogs and Cats with Cardiac Disease
Arterial Blood Pressure: What Are We Actually Monitoring?
Arrhythmia Recognition: When to Watch and When to Intervene
Anesthetic-Associated Hyperkalemia in Retired Racing Greyhounds
Buprenorphine: The Orphan Child of the Opioid Family
Anesthetic Interventions Part 1
Anesthetic Interventions Part 2

courses.title: Coaching Skills Development Program
courses.description:
This five-month, five-sprint program develops coaching-based leadership skills in laboratory animal facility leaders using the GROW model (Goal, Reality, Options, Will) as its central framework. Each monthly sprint combines self-paced reading, video instruction, and structured reflection activities with a live 90-minute virtual group coaching session where participants practice the skills in real time with facilitator and peer feedback. Participants progress from foundational concepts through powerful questioning, active listening, and creating genuine accountability, finishing with an integration sprint and a personal sustainability plan.
Key topics include:
-Understanding why a coaching leadership style improves engagement over command-and-control management
-Applying the GROW model (Goal, Reality, Options, Will) to structure coaching conversations
-Constructing powerful, open-ended questions that raise awareness and responsibility
-Practicing active listening skills, including reflecting, paraphrasing, and using silence
-Creating genuine commitment and accountability through coaching-based feedback
-Building a personal, sustainable coaching practice and contributing to a coaching culture
Participants will explore practical applications of these concepts through live practice, structured reflection, and real coaching conversations with their own teams throughout the program.

courses.title: Endocrine Dynamics: Dyslipidemias and Thyroid Spectrum Disorders in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: In this 3-hour, LIVE seminar with Dr. Christina Marino, DVM, DACVIM, participants will explore diagnostic and management strategies for complex lipid and thyroid disorders in small animals. The program reviews lipid physiology, the clinical consequences of hyperlipidemia, and practical dietary/medical management, including selecting low-fat options in patients with concurrent comorbidities. It then evaluates canine thyroid disease, covering classic and atypical manifestations of hypothyroidism, levothyroxine trials, and diagnostic strategies to confidently distinguish true hypothyroidism from non-thyroidal illness syndrome. Finally, the seminar addresses feline pediatric endocrinology, focusing on fading kitten syndrome and the diagnosis and treatment of congenital hypothyroidism in neonates.

courses.title: Hobby Farm Medicine Basics (LAMS103)
courses.description: Hobby farming is growing in popularity, and these farmers may see their herds more as pets than production animals. When these animals become injured or ill, their owners are turning to their local family veterinarian for assistance, even though many small animal practitioners have little to no experience with farm animal medicine or with treating animals that are being used in food or fleece production. If you're one of those veterinarians or technicians, this course is intended to help you learn how to approach these farm calls, and to familiarize you with diagnosing and treating conditions of animals commonly encountered on hobby farms.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: The cases that stall: Using pet parent insights to provide care for emergency and chronic disease patients
courses.description: In celebration of National Veterinary Technician Week, join us for a practical, case-based exploration of one of the biggest challenges facing veterinary teams today: helping pet owners move from recommendation to action. Through a series of emergency and chronic disease cases, participants will examine how different pet parent decision-making styles influence treatment acceptance, adherence, and follow-through. Attendees will learn how factors such as cost concerns, convenience needs, emotional stress, and caregiving complexity can shape client decisions, even when medical recommendations are clear. By applying behavioral insights to real-world clinical scenarios, veterinary professionals will gain actionable communication strategies that help personalize recommendations, strengthen client alignment, and support better outcomes for pets across a range of care situations.

courses.title: Everything But the Kitchen Sink, Utilizing All Parts of the Anesthetic Protocol
courses.description: This presentation will discuss how utilizing the anesthetic protocol in its entirety can help mitigate potential negative side effects associated with using individual portions of the protocol alone. The presentation will cover pre-appointment medications, premedications, induction and co-induction, maintenance, MAC reducers including injectable anesthetics and local or regional blocks, and recovery. Emphasis will be placed on how each phase of anesthesia contributes to patient comfort, analgesia, smoother transitions between anesthetic phases, and reduction of anesthetic drug requirements. Patient-specific considerations and the benefits and limitations of commonly used anesthetic techniques will also be discussed.

courses.title: Confident Conversations: Communication Strategies for Increasing Trust and Wellness Compliance
courses.description: Helping clients understand the value of preventive care isn't always easy. Questions about vaccines, parasite prevention, and other wellness recommendations can lead to difficult conversations that leave veterinary professionals feeling discouraged. Join Dr. Donnelly as she shares practical approaches for navigating these everyday communication challenges. Using real-world wellness appointment scenarios, attendees will learn how to help clients feel heard, respond to concerns with empathy, and communicate recommendations in ways that foster trust and improve compliance.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Degenerative Mitral Valve Disease in Your Practice
courses.description: This session will discuss the approach to management of a small breed, older dog presenting with a heart murmur. In addition, there will be a review of how thoracic radiographs can be used to help stage a patient within the current ACVIM staging for degenerative mitral valve disease

courses.title: Shaping the Diagnosis Series: Differential Decoded
courses.description: Automated hematology analyzers provide powerful quantitative data, but important diagnostic insights can be missed when blood morphology is not assessed. This presentation explores the clinical value of blood morphology assessment as a complement to automated CBC results. Through one canine case study, participants will examine how morphology findings altered diagnostic pathways, improved interpretation of laboratory data, and influenced patient management. Practical guidance will be provided on when morphology review is most important and how morphology findings can be integrated into everyday clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management
courses.description: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management
courses.description: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Fetch Encore - NAVLE - Preparation, Placement & Professional Growth For the Vet Student and New Grad
courses.description:
Passing the NAVLE is one thing but being ready for real practice is another! This Fetch Encore virtual symposium focuses on the professional skills veterinary students and veterinary technician students need but rarely get taught:
Start making stronger calls with case-based learning, including:
- Managing the transition into practice
- Testing strategies
- Clinical reasoning
Expect honest conversations about confidence, imposter syndrome, and how to think like a doctor under pressure.

courses.title: Avoiding Mishaps: Selecting and Preparing Anesthetic Equipment
courses.description: This 1-hour presentation focuses on selecting the patient breathing circuit and setting up the anesthetic machine in preparation for a procedure. Learn how to perform appropriate anesthetic machine check out procedures to ensure equipment is assembled correctly and functional before applying to a patient.

courses.title: Whats that Sound? Approach to Puppies and Kittens with a Heart Murmur
courses.description: Heart murmurs are commonly detected during routine exams in young dogs and cats yet determining whether a murmur is innocent or pathologic can be challenging. This session will present a practical approach to evaluating murmurs in puppies and kittens, with emphasis on differentiating normal from abnormal findings using auscultation, physical exam, and breed-specific predispositions. Learn how to apply diagnostic tools such as thoracic radiographs, NT-proBNP, point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), and echocardiography to guide next steps. Special consideration will be given to congenital heart disease in both species, including when advanced imaging or referral is warranted.

courses.title: A Gut Feeling: Understanding Liver Abscesses in Beef x Dairy Cattle
courses.description: Liver abscesses are an important challenge in beef x dairy cattle, with reported prevalence exceeding 50% in some populations and occurring at substantially higher rates than in native beef cattle. But why are beef x dairy animals seemingly more susceptible and what can be done to reduce the risk? This webinar will explore the connection between gut health and liver abscess development, including how damage and disruptions to the gastrointestinal epithelium can allow Fusobacterium necrophorum and other bacteria to enter the portal circulation and reach the liver. The presenter will examine current industry trends and the growing importance of liver abscesses in beef x dairy production, including their potential impact on animal performance, carcass value, and profitability.

courses.title: Start Smart - Understanding & Preparing for a Veterinarian of Record Relationship (LIVE)
courses.description:
This program introduces the veterinarian of record (VOR) relationship in the context of animal shelters and animal welfare organizations. Participants will explore the purpose and value of establishing a veterinary partnership, the roles and responsibilities of both veterinarians and shelter leadership, and factors that contribute to an effective working relationship.
For veterinarians, the program will address the veterinarian-client-patient relationship (VCPR) within a shelter setting, differences between shelter medicine and traditional private practice, and considerations for determining interest and capacity to serve an animal welfare organization. Participants will also examine characteristics to consider when evaluating a potential shelter partner.
For shelter and animal welfare leaders, the program will provide guidance for identifying their organization's veterinary needs, distinguishing between a veterinarian-of-record arrangement and a more comprehensive veterinary partnership, and assessing organizational readiness to work effectively with a veterinarian.
Through discussion of expectations, capacity, communication, and partnership structure, participants will develop a framework for evaluating potential veterinarian-shelter partnerships and identifying appropriate next steps toward establishing or formalizing a veterinarian of record relationship.

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Wild About Eyes 2026
courses.description: This continuing education event brings together a variety of clinically relevant topics designed to help veterinary professionals strengthen their diagnostic and treatment skills. Sessions will cover feline infectious peritonitis (FIP), ophthalmic manifestations of systemic disease, ocular and orbital neoplasia, and non-ulcerative keratitis in dogs. Through practical, case-based discussions, attendees will gain current, applicable knowledge they can use to recognize complex disease, select appropriate diagnostics, develop treatment plans, and determine when referral or advanced care is indicated.

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.provider: ACCESS SPECIALTY ANIMAL HOSPITAL PALM BEACH COUNTY
courses.title: Veterinary Applications of Hemopurification
courses.description: This talk will provide basic information on purification of the blood using extracorporeal therapies including hemodialysis, therapeutic plasma exchange and hemoperfusion. The lecture will include an overview of each of the modalities and a case example will be provided for each.
courses.location: ACCESS Specialty Animal Hospital Palm Beach County

courses.title: When Bandages Go Wrong: Managing slips, sores, and owner conversations
courses.description:
This lecture dives into the most common complications that can occur with veterinary bandages, from slipping and unraveling to pressure sores and moisture damage. Attendees will learn how to identify early warning signs, correct mistakes, and effectively communicate with pet owners when issues arise. Practical tips and real-world case examples will help veterinary technicians feel more confident in preventing and managing bandage failures, ensuring better outcomes for both patients and clients.
Learning Objectives:
* Recognize and troubleshoot common bandage complications such as slipping, pressure sores, and moisture-related damage through early detection and intervention.
* Apply practical correction strategies to improve bandage security, comfort, and effectiveness, using real-world case examples and technician-focused techniques.
* Develop effective communication skills for guiding pet owners in monitoring bandages at home, addressing concerns, and ensuring compliance for better patient outcomes.

courses.title: SDEP Anatomy, Pain Points & Tips
courses.description: This presentation provides an overview of general anatomy and how it pertains to the sonographic presentation while scanning. Anatomical terms, ultrasound terminology, anatomical diagrams, and step by step scanning instructions are discussed in detail. Probe positioning, tips, and scanning techniques, trouble shooting, and efficient imaging are conveyed to the attendees. Cine loops and stills of proper scanning are also utilized. Interactive questions and answers are encouraged during this 2-hour presentation.

courses.title: Tackling Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency
courses.description: In this course, we will review the causes, clinical signs, diagnosis, and management of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI). The session highlights current evidence, clinical recommendations, and real-world case applications.

courses.title: Triage and Common Presentations in Exotic Companion Animals
courses.description: Exotic patients are fragile and often mask illness until advanced. This lecture reviews efficient, low-stress triage techniques, key history elements, and species-specific stabilization steps. Common emergency and appointment presentations in ferrets, rabbits, small mammals, birds, and reptiles are outlined with practical, actionable protocols to improve outcomes and client education.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Radiographic Interpretation
courses.description: This two-hour discussion (of our eight-part series) is dedicated to developing confidence and precision in reading and interpreting dental radiography, an essential skill for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning in veterinary dentistry. The session begins with a practical review of how to properly orient radiographs and identify which tooth is being examined, ensuring attendees feel grounded in the basics of interpretation. From there, participants will move into a detailed discussion of normal radiographic anatomy, building a clear picture of what healthy structures should look like. With that foundation in place, the focus shifts to identifying radiographic pathology, including how to recognize subtle changes and understand their clinical significance. Common conditions such as periodontal disease will be explored in depth, with attention given not only to diagnosis but also to treatment options. By the conclusion of this two-hour session, clinicians will be equipped with the knowledge to interpret dental radiographs with confidence, distinguish between normal and abnormal findings, and apply these skills directly to patient care.

courses.title: Stop Reacting, Start Controlling: A Simple Step-by-Step Plan for Inventory Success
courses.description:
Inventory is the second largest - and often most mismanaged - expense in a veterinary practice. Whether it's overstocking, understocking, or spending excessive time on manual counts, these missteps can drain your time, money, and energy. This webinar will address the real challenges that veterinary professionals face when managing inventory and provide practical strategies to take control.
We'll dive into the concept of inventory on hand (IOH) and how carrying excess stock ties up valuable capital. The webinar will explore the importance of formulary optimization to boost margins and reduce waste, and we'll walk through the benefits of cycle counting as a streamlined solution. Participants will gain hands-on advice for conducting full hospital counts, cleaning up old inventory, and organizing a system for ongoing success. The session includes a project plan, broken into small, manageable tasks, to help participants start improving their inventory practices right away.
No more relying on guesswork, post-it notes, or reacting to inventory shortages at the last minute. This webinar will provide actionable steps to regain control of inventory, reduce costs, and improve your practice's financial health.

courses.title: Veterinary Medicine: Radiology For Bone Lesions and Fractures in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Diagnostic work up of musculoskeletal disorders frequently includes radiographic examination and/or other diagnostic imaging procedures. The imaging modalities are used to further characterize clinically localized problems and to differentiate disease processes.
Aggressive and nonaggressive bone lesions are very common. Diagnostic imaging plays an important role in diagnosing and differentiating these pathologic processes. Radiology is considered the first technique to implement to try to establish a diagnosis.
Diagnostic imaging is a vital component in the diagnosis and management of fractures. At initial presentation, fractures can be identified and classified to permit planning of optimal treatment. Fractures can be monitored to assess healing and identify developing complications. Fracture identification and radiographic description of fractures along with evaluating fracture healing and complications of fracture repair, are of paramount importance for a successful treatment.

courses.title: (LIVE COURSE) Updates in Management of Neurological Emergencies
courses.description: This 3-week online course reviews current evidence and practical approaches to three common neurological emergencies in veterinary patients. We will cover traumatic brain injury, status epilepticus, and spinal trauma and acute disc disease. Each week focuses on triage, diagnostic decision-making, medical and surgical options, and monitoring. The content is designed for veterinarians who want the latest updates, with clinically applicable protocols you can use in practice.

courses.provider: ADVANCED VETERINARY CARE THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE
courses.title: The ABC SECTION'S Of Dystocia and Delivery Management Improving Your Outcomes
courses.description: This 1 hour CE lecture is designed for veterinary doctors, technicians, and tech assistants. It will cover an overview of neonatal resuscitation / care. Successful management of dystocia and neonatal resuscitation requires rapid assessment, effective teamwork, and timely intervention to optimize outcomes for both the dam and neonates. This presentation will review the recognition and management of dystocia, decision-making surrounding medical versus surgical intervention, and evidence-based approaches to neonatal stabilization and resuscitation. Attendees will gain practical knowledge of delivery room preparation, neonatal assessment, resuscitation techniques, and post-delivery care that can be immediately applied in clinical practice. Through case-based discussion and real-world scenarios, participants will learn strategies to improve survival rates and enhance patient care during obstetrical emergencies.

courses.title: The Real-Life Approach to Osteoarthritis Management: A Case-Based Discussion
courses.description: This program is a case-based discussion of osteoarthritis and building a general guideline for approaching the management of patients. OA is a complex and complicated process with no cookbook approach that works the same every time. It is a vicious cycle starting with joint pain and inflammation; it is the number one cause of chronic pain in dogs in the US. This talk will provide the presenters thoughts/opinions on managing patients with the goal being to have attendees make their own decision on how to manage their patients. We will discuss appropriate history taking, use of technicians, staging tools and at-risk patients. In addition, there will be a review of gait evaluation, examination, palpation and radiographs. Finally management options and multimodal approach.

courses.title: Perioperative Surgical Patient Care: Honoring the Bond
courses.description: A veterinary patient's perioperative experience is based on so much more than the surgeon's skill. Veterinary technicians play a vital role in the care of perioperative patients and educating pet owners. Strategies for supporting patient comfort and emotional wellbeing while assuring successful surgical outcomes will be discussed, such as the importance of Fear Free handling techniques, perioperative analgesia, and nutrition tactics for the veterinary team. Join this lecture for practical ideas that elevate the perioperative experience by nurturing the human-animal bond and exceeding client expectations.

courses.title: AAEP XP Series: NeuroXP (LEX)
courses.description: This intensive two-day program provides equine practitioners with practical, clinically focused training in the diagnosis and management of neurologic disease in horses. Through a combination of preparatory materials, targeted lectures, interactive case discussions, and extensive hands-on laboratory sessions, participants develop a structured approach to neurologic examination, neurolocalization, diagnostic planning, and treatment decision-making. Learning will include foundational concepts, diagnostic interpretation, and hands-on skills using live horses, cadavers, and imaging modalities with advanced case-based discussions, procedural training, and real-world clinical scenarios, including client communication and risk management. Small-group laboratories and expert faculty guidance ensure individualized instruction and immediate clinical applicability, enabling participants to confidently assess, diagnose, and manage complex equine neurologic cases in practice.

courses.title: Animal Health Canada Forum 2026
courses.description:
Animal Health Canada Forum brings together senior leaders from government, animal agriculture, and from across the animal health and welfare system to share experience, exchange knowledge, and learn from one another.
The Forum 2026 theme is, 'Turning Insight into Action for Canada's Animal Health and Welfare System.'
Forum will focus on rising animal welfare expectations, evolving biosecurity risks, and the growing impact of misinformation and disinformation.
Participants will leave with practical insights to support decision making and action across Canada's animal health and welfare system.

courses.title: 2026 VHA Expo
courses.description:
Program Description: Our 2026 conference features 5 compelling speakers, including opening keynote Sarah Wooten, DVM. The breakout sessions will be guided by industry leaders who will cover topics of Neurology, Hematology, Practice Management, and Spectrum of Care. We will conclude the day with closing keynote Paul Burke.
The objective of the 2026 VHA Expo is to elevate medicine practiced in the clinics attending through networking, education, professional development, new products and services, and industry trends and insights. The veterinary field is constantly evolving, with new research, techniques, and technologies emerging. Attending the 2026 VHA Expo can help veterinary professionals stay updated on the latest developments.
courses.location: Double Tree Hilton Bloomington Minneapolis South

courses.title: Percardial Effusion: Diagnosis and Management
courses.description: Patients frequently present to the emergency department in tamponade with significant hemodynamic compromise. Early recognition and appropriate management are critical to improving patient outcomes. During this session, we will discuss the immediate management of patients in tamponade, as well as long-term planning and therapy options to achieve the best results for our patient populations. We will also discuss pericardial effusion in the feline, which carries a different long-term complication and survival outcome when compared to the canine patient

courses.title: Developing and Utilizing a Parvo Champion in Your Practice LIVE
courses.description:
Come join the conversation with Open Door Veterinary Collective consultant Dr. Kathleen Babbitt, DVM, as we explore Developing and Utilizing a Parvo Champion in Your Practice.
Managing canine parvovirus presents unique hurdles for veterinary clinics, particularly regarding staffing, communications, and client financial constraints. Implementing a dedicated Parvo Champion mitigates team burnout while ensuring high-quality, compassionate patient and client care.
This session demonstrates how to integrate individualized patient care with practical, cost-effective treatment paths and go-home communication resources. Attendees will gain actionable tools for every stage of the patient journey - from intake to discharge - enabling teams to elevate clinical outcomes, alleviate workplace fatigue, and maintain financial sustainability.

courses.title: Continuing education evening with Vision Vets For Pets and East Tennessee Veterinary Dentistry
courses.description: This course will provide 1 hour of ophthalmology continuing education and 1 hour of dentistry continuing education. The ophthalmology portion will provide information on the diagnosis and treatment of glaucoma, and the dentistry portion will cover basic and advanced dentistry techniques for use in small animals.

courses.title: Easy to Swallow: Utilizing Contrast Radiography to Evaluate the Gastrointestinal Tract
courses.description: Contrast studies remain a valuable diagnostic tool for evaluating gastrointestinal disease. This lecture will discuss practical techniques for performing oral and rectal contrast studies, as well as interpretation of findings associated with disorders of the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and colon. Attendees will gain a better understanding of when contrast radiography is indicated and how these studies can contribute to clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Understanding and Navigating the Companion Animal Practice Marketplace : A Review of Current Dynamics
courses.description: This program is a 60-minute prepared lecture that introduces the attendee to the major dynamics in the companion animal marketplace, and how these recent shifts are driving changes in the practice of veterinary medicine. Included in this lecture are an overview of the recent growth and/or decline of the major segments of companion animal practice, including wellness & preventive medicine, parasite prevention, surgical and procedural volume, as well as chronic disease management. Intended for all positions within the veterinary hospital including owners, associate clinicians, technical support staff and administrative support staff/management, this program utilizes a nationwide data set of both product sales/consumption data and practice information management system (PIMS) data to present nationwide, regional and even subgroup detail.

courses.provider: ACCESS SPECIALTY ANIMAL HOSPITAL PALM BEACH COUNTY
courses.title: Minimally Invasive Orthopedic Surgery
courses.description: This lecture will review the advantages of minimally invasive orthopedic surgery and review the indications and minimally invasive orthopedic techniques.

courses.title: VSPN/AIMVT Elevate - Online Conference - Advance. Specialize. Inspire (AIMVT 010-2026))
courses.description:
This online conference will help the attendee in meeting their professional goals. As the title says, Advance, specialize, and inspire: the attendee will learn how to leverage their Veterinary Technician Specialist (VTS) credential, handle challenging communication issues, create a supportive learning environment in the clinic, and use critical thinking skills effectively.
Learning Objectives
-Compare multiple career pathways available to Veterinary Technician Specialists beyond traditional clinical practice.
-Recognize transferable leadership, communication, and educational skills that can be developed through obtaining a VTS credential.
-Apply strategies for leveraging advanced credentials to pursue opportunities in leadership, education, industry, consulting, and professional organizations.
-Create an individualized action plan to support continued professional growth and career advancement after earning a VTS credential.
-Review coaching techniques to ensure that information is taken to heart
-Review best practices for offering suggestions and feedback
-Identify tone and tenor that will color a conversation negatively
-Discuss next steps if medical standards are not met even after addressing them
-Understanding the basics of psychological safety and team communication and the role of Veterinary Technician Specialists in creating and supporting psychological safety on the hospital floor
-Prioritize communication between teams amongst all other responsibilities on the hospital floor and model this to other employees
-Integrate critical thinking exercises and train the trainer learning activities on the hospital floor
-Define critical thinking and distinguish it from passive skepticism or contrarianism within a professional clinical context.
-Identify at least three cognitive biases that commonly influence clinical decision-making in veterinary nursing practice and describe one concrete mitigation strategy for each.
-Apply a structured framework to evaluate a peer-

courses.description: Fetch, a dvm360 conference, at National Harbor, MD is a live interactive, in-person conference with a combination of both medical and non-medical programs created for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers to achieve their continuing education in veterinary medicine. Educational content tracks include: Artificial Intelligence, Behavior, Cardiology, Communication, Critical Care, Dentistry, Dermatology, Endocrinology, Ethics, Feline Medicine, Geriatrics, Infectious Disease, Internal Medicine, Laser Therapy, Marketing, Nutrition, Oncology, Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Pain Management, Parasitology, Practice Management, Practice Ownership, Preventive Medicine, Rehabilitation, Surgery, Technician Anesthesiology, Technician Critical Care, Technician Feline Medicine, Technician Medicine, Technician Neurology, Technician Pain Management, Wound Management.

courses.title: Dermatology Symposium
courses.description: The continuing education program will include two parts. Part I will be a single didactic lecture on modern pet diets. Part II will be a 2-topic lecture series with interactive elements.
