courses.provider: THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE SPECIALISTS NORTH SCOTTSDALE
courses.title: 2026 Thrive North Scottsdale Specialists Desert Summit: Advanced Multi-Disciplinary Case Management & Clinical Diagnostics
courses.description:
This comprehensive, single-track, day-long continuing education program provides primary care veterinarians and emergency clinicians with practical, evidence-based approaches to multi-disciplinary case management across key specialty areas.
Following a logical anatomical and physiological progression throughout the day, participants will cover:
Neurology: Fundamentals of performing a thorough neurologic examination and establishing an accurate neuroanatomic localization.
Cardiology: Clinical utility of cardiac biomarkers, including NT-proBNP, in dogs and cats to differentiate cardiac vs. non-cardiac disease and guide targeted management.
Anesthesiology: Tailored anesthetic protocols, premedication/induction choices, and hemodynamically stable fluid management strategies for patients with co-existing cardiac and renal disease.
Emergency & Critical Care: Pathophysiology of hemorrhagic shock and practical execution of emergency autotransfusion during acute blood loss.
Soft Tissue Surgery & Internal Medicine: Diagnostic workup, imaging, and management of surgical acute abdomens, peritonitis, and the perioperative anatomy, physiology, and complications associated with adrenal gland surgery ("Adrenal Squeeze").
Oncology: Practical diagnostic workups, staging plans, biopsy considerations, and clinical decision-making for common canine and feline neoplasms encountered in general practice.
Through case-based discussions and review of current literature, attendees will gain actionable strategies to optimize patient outcomes, preserve future treatment options, avoid common diagnostic pitfalls, and navigate timely specialty referrals.

courses.title: 2026 Saratoga Equine Practitioners Conference
courses.description: The NAEP is back in Saratoga for the Saratoga Equine Practitioners Conference from September 23-26th, 2026. This conference will include presentations in the following areas: Lameness, Podiatry, Internal Medicine. There will also be a full day of Wet Labs in the following areas: Lameness, Podiatry, Internal Medicine, and Ultrasound.

courses.title: Beyond the Diarrhea: Harnessing the Canine Gut Microbiome for Better Clinical Outcomes
courses.description: In this lecture, we will explore the crucial role of the intestinal microbiome in maintaining digestive health and resilience in dogs, with a focus on evidence-based strategies to preserve, support, and restore microbial balance in clinical practice. Using clinical cases of dogs with acute diarrhea, we will discuss the importance of a systematic diagnostic and therapeutic approach tailored to the severity of the clinical signs, highlighting interventions that minimize disruption of the microbiome whenever possible. Participants will gain practical guidance on when to consider fecal microbiota transplantation, how to select appropriate fecal donors, and how to safely and effectively perform fecal microbiota transplantation procedures.

courses.title: Human Grade Pet Food: Understanding the Highest Standard for Integrity, Quality, and Food Safety
courses.description:
Pet owners are increasingly seeking "Human Grade" diets for
their pets, but what does this claim actually mean? Is it simply a marketing term, or does it represent a
meaningful difference in ingredient quality, manufacturing, and food safety?
This presentation explores the regulatory definition of Human Grade Pet Food and the rigorous standards
required to legally make this claim. Attendees will learn how Human Grade products differ from conventional
pet foods in ingredient sourcing, manufacturing practices, facility requirements, documentation, and regulatory
oversight. The seminar will also examine why quality systems-including supplier qualification, sanitation,
traceability, preventive controls, and testing- play a critical role in ensuring product integrity.
Rather than focusing solely on nutrition, this session provides veterinarians with a behind-the-scenes look at
how pet food is produced and why manufacturing standards matter when evaluating food quality. Participants
will leave with a practical framework for interpreting Human Grade claims and confidently discussing ingredient
quality and food safety with clients.

courses.title: The Modern Veterinary Pharmacy: Integrating In-Hospital and Online Care
courses.description:
Consumer expectations have fundamentally changed the way veterinary clients purchase medications, prescription diets, and preventive products. Convenience, home delivery, automatic refills, and digital ordering have become standard expectations rather than competitive advantages. As a result, veterinary hospitals are invited to revisit how online pharmacy services fit within an overall strategy for patient care, client service, and hospital profitability.
This presentation explores the evolving role of online pharmacies as an extension of veterinary healthcare rather than simply another retail channel. Participants will examine how consumer purchasing behavior has shifted, the operational advantages and challenges of online pharmacy integration, and strategies for maintaining strong client relationships regardless of where products are dispensed. Discussion will explore the factors practices should consider when evaluating an online pharmacy partner, from inventory management and operational efficiency to client compliance, convenience, and practice profitability. Lastly, the presenter will touch upon ways to garner staff buy-in to an online pharmacy and how to integrate and promote the pharmacy within the hospital's daily workflows.

courses.title: Open Wound Management - What's New and What Works?
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical update on open wound management in veterinary patients, with an emphasis on current evidence and techniques that can improve wound healing. Topics will include wound assessment, debridement, wound bed preparation, lavage, topical therapies and dressings, negative pressure wound therapy, and decision-making for delayed or definitive wound closure. Participants will review what is new in veterinary wound care, which traditional approaches remain effective, and how to select appropriate management strategies for challenging wounds encountered in clinical practice.

courses.title: VetCE Virtual: Beyond Bad Behavior - Understanding Canine and Feline Behaviour Disorders
courses.description: This VetCE Virtual set of 3 live distance presentations includes topics of interest presented by experts. The presentations are held on separate dates. Attendees enroll in all three and must attend all to earn the completion certificate. The first presentation is on September 14, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Easy as one, two, pee: Solving Feline Housesoiling. The 2nd is on September 21, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Resource Guarding of Food. The 3rd and final presentation is on September 28, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Addressing the Medical Components of Behavior Cases. The VetCE Virtual series of micro-conferences are a convenient alternative to in-person events and are designed to deliver multiple RACE and/or CVPM approved CE credits in a virtual format with three one-hour presentations. They provide educational sessions presented by expert speakers, and an easy way to learn and earn credits in the comfort of your home or office.

courses.title: Communication Skills to Make Clients LOVE You
courses.description: Excellent communication skills are crucial to develop trusting client relationships and improve both client compliance and patient outcomes. These skills should be developed by all team members. It has been shown that veterinarians with excellent bedside manner and communication skills are more likely to have a satisfied client and less likely to receive board complaints or malpractice claims. During this lecture, we will review basic communication tools and then discuss their application in various situations in the clinic, including making diagnostic and treatment recommendations, talking to upset clients, managing complications, and discussing finances.

courses.title: Code Brown: Updates in Fecal Diagnostics & Emerging Parasites in Cats & Dogs Near You
courses.description: This case-based session will provide updates on recent advances in fecal diagnostics and summarize key diagnostic and management components of "moving GI experiences" (ie, feline and canine diarrhea). An overview of common day-to-day causes of infectious diarrhea, with a focus on canine and feline GI parasites, including those of One Health and emerging importance (eg, Echinococcus multilocularis, drug-resistant hookworms, Giardia spp) and relevant antimicrobial stewardship aspects, will be provided. Pet owner communication, recent research pearls, and contextualized clinical strategies will be incorporated to provide actionable insights for attendees.

courses.title: Improving Outcomes for Clients with Financial Limitations Using a Spectrum of Care Approach
courses.description: Cases limited by client finances are a daily occurrence for many small animal practitioners. As pets are considered part of the family, conversations between pet owners and the veterinary team can become emotionally charged, especially when finances are limited and decisions about care become life or death. These cases and the discussions that go with them can create moral distress and contribute to burnout for many veterinarians. But it doesn't have to be this way. This lecture will explore the concepts of spectrum of care and incremental care in the context of client financial limitations and provide tools that can be used in financial conversations to maximize patient outcomes in clinical practice.

courses.title: STP Virtual Modular Education Course: Digestive System Pathology
courses.description: The objective of the STP Modular Education Course, Digestive System Pathology, is to provide a practical framework for evaluating pathology of the gastrointestinal tract and associated digestive organs in nonclinical toxicology studies. The course emphasizes histology, species differences, spontaneous and treatment-related findings, and interpretation of lesions. Participants will strengthen their ability to distinguish background from treatment-related changes and integrate histopathology with clinical pathology, biomarkers, and mechanistic context. Emerging topics, including translational relevance, cutting- edge molecular pathology tools, and artificial intelligence in toxicologic pathology, are also included. The course will be a mixture of didactic lectures and case studies. Topics covered include: Overview of digestive system anatomy, physiology, and INHAND terminology; Contemporary approaches for evaluating digestive system structure and function; Digestive system considerations across therapeutic modalities, regulatory, translational, and case-based perspectives on interpreting digestive system findings in safety assessment. Course Chair: Kristofer Michalson, DVM, PhD, DACVP, (Bristol Myers Squibb); Course Co-Chair: Dinesh Bangari, BVSc, MVSc, MS, PhD, DACVP, (Sanofi); Course Scientific Advisors: Alys Bradley, BVSc (Charles River Laboratories); Ingrid Cornax, BS, DPhil, DVM (Altos Lab); Odete Mendes, DVM, PhD, DACVP, DABT (Merck & Co. Inc); Jagannatha (Jay) Mysore, MVSc, PhD, DACVP (Asklepios); and Jerrold Ward, DVM, PhD, DACVP, FIATP (Global VetPathology)

courses.title: Health Certificates Are Not Enough: What Veterinary Teams Need to Know About Pet Travel Readiness
courses.description: Pet travel is increasingly showing up in veterinary practice, yet many veterinary teams are being asked to manage these cases without standardized training, consistent workflows, or confidence in key areas of travel preparation. Using preliminary insights from the When Pets Fly Veterinary Pet Travel Education Interest Survey, this webinar will explore where pet travel preparation commonly breaks down, including how clinics handle travel appointments, the types of requests veterinary teams receive, and the areas where teams report the least confidence when advising clients. Participants will learn why a health certificate does not automatically mean a pet is ready to travel and why veterinary teams need to be involved before the final paperwork appointment to achieve earlier, more informed, welfare-centered travel preparation. Veterinary Air-Travel Medicine and the When Pets Fly Pet Travel Readiness Assessment, will be introduced as an emerging approach that moves pet travel conversations beyond health certificate completion and toward safe, consistent, and welfare-centered pet travel case management.

courses.title: Feline Ophthalmology: Comprehensive Clinical Update
courses.description: This 2-hour continuing education program provides veterinarians and veterinary technicians with a feline-specific review of common anterior and posterior segment eye disease. The first segment addresses feline conjunctivitis, corneal ulceration, corneal sequestrum, eosinophilic keratitis, bullous keratopathy, eyelid masses, and entropion. The second segment reviews feline uveitis, glaucoma, hypertensive retinopathy, iris melanoma, and practical enucleation decision-making and surgical pearls for general practitioners.

courses.title: Performing and Communicating Around Euthanasia With Compassion
courses.description:
Few moments in veterinary medicine require greater presence than guiding a family through the end of a beloved pet's life. While clinical skills are essential, the experience is equally shaped by communication, compassion, professionalism, and the ability to create an environment where families feel supported during one of their most difficult moments.
This session explores practical strategies for preparing both the physical space and your professional presence before, during, and after euthanasia appointments. Participants will learn techniques for creating a calm environment, clear energy, developing authentic communication scripts, and utilizing body language that conveys empathy and confidence.
Equally important, this webinar addresses what happens after the appointment ends. Repeated exposure to grief can quietly accumulate over time, making intentional recovery practices essential to a sustainable veterinary career. Participants will explore practical approaches for honoring each experience through protective practices, brief personal resets, structured team debriefs, and meaningful end-of-day rituals that acknowledge the emotional weight of the work while supporting long-term professional well-being.
By integrating compassionate behavior with intentional recovery practices, participants will leave with a framework for caring not only for patients and their families, but also for themselves and their colleagues.

courses.title: How We are Shooting Ourselves in the Foot: Veterinary Professionalism
courses.description:
While we often parallel ourselves with human medical counterparts, many in our ranks need some self-reflection and objective feedback before calling themselves professionals.
Everyone, from medical directors to kennel workers, should be representing the veterinary medical profession adequately to ensure appropriate public perception while commanding respect. What is veterinary professionalism and how do we obtain it?

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Heritage Vet Partners Cattle First Summit
courses.description: This program is being offered to provide a range of continuing education topics to practitioners in the Heritage Vet Partners Group. Topics will include research updates on transboundary animal diseases, bovine respiratory updates, transcriptomics, clinic best practices in relation to necropsies, and personnel management issues specifically related to bridging generational gaps in practice teams.

courses.title: PIMS is NOT a Four-Letter Word -Pick It More Strategically with Help LIVE
courses.description:
Your practice information management system touches every part of your hospital, from scheduling to invoicing to medical records. Join Veterinary Ownership Advocates for a webinar with PIMS expert Adam Wysocki on how to choose the right system for your practice.
Whether you're launching a new practice or evaluating an acquisition, this session will cover:
For startups: how to identify what you actually need and match it to the right PIMS
For existing hospitals or acquisitions: how to assess whether your current PIMS is meeting your needs, and if not, how to choose and convert to a better option

courses.title: Mission Possible: Beating FIP
courses.description: The objectives include recognizing that FIP is no longer 100% fatal, identifying the wide range of clinical presentations, and developing individualized diagnostic and treatment plans. Early recognition and intervention are emphasized as critical factors influencing treatment success. The main focus will be clinical presentations, diagnostic testing, and case review.

courses.title: 2026 AAHA CON Conference
courses.description: The American Animal Hospital Association has been setting the standard for small animal veterinary care for over 90 years. Every year, AAHA CON brings together veterinary professionals from across the country to learn, connect, and celebrate the future of veterinary medicine. In 2026, we're heading to Portland, Oregon for three unforgettable days of inspiration, education, and community. Immerse yourself in transformative learning experiences in an intimate setting designed for your personal growth. This year's conference celebrates the strength, stability, and growth that comes from being firmly grounded in veterinary medicine while reaching upward to explore new possibilities.

courses.title: From Instruments to Incision: Veterinary Ophthalmic Surgery
courses.description: This live, interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review common ophthalmic surgical procedures performed in general practice. This course will provide an overview of surgical anatomy, instrumentation, indications, and techniques. Common pitfalls for eyelid surgery will be highlighted, as well as key procedural steps to improve outcomes in ophthalmic procedures.

courses.title: Acupuncture And Western Herbs for Senior Pets.
courses.description: This two-session program provides a practical overview of integrative approaches to supporting the health and well-being of senior pets. One one-hour session focuses on the use of acupuncture to enhance comfort, mobility, and quality of life in aging dogs and cats. The second one-hour session explores the role of Western herbal medicine in supporting common age-related conditions and promoting healthy aging. Together, these sessions offer veterinary professionals an introduction to complementary therapies that can be integrated with conventional care to optimize outcomes for senior patients.

courses.title: Dental Radiography
courses.description:
Dental radiography is the most important diagnostic tool in veterinary dentistry, yet it is often underutilized or performed with technique that compromises image quality and safety. This lecture reviews core radiation safety principles the ALARA principle, personal protective equipment, and proper positioning of personnel relative to the primary beam along with regulatory considerations relevant to veterinary practice.
Attendees will compare available radiography systems, including conventional film, phosphor plate, and digital sensors, weighing image quality, workflow, durability, and cost to help determine the best fit for their practice. The lecture concludes with practical guidance on obtaining diagnostic quality radiographs, covering parallel and bisecting angle positioning, sensor placement for maxillary and mandibular arcades, and common technique errors and how to correct them.
By the end of this session, attendees will be equipped to implement safer radiographic protocols, make informed equipment decisions, and consistently produce diagnostic dental radiographs in practice.

courses.title: Medical Colic in the Adult Horse
courses.description:
This talk will cover the anatomy of the equine gastrointestinal tract and explore the subject of colic. There are many reasons for a horse to exhibit abdominal pain and most horse owners are well versed to spot the signs of colic. Many bouts of colic can be managed at the farm with an ambulatory veterinarian and will never need to be hauled into a referral hospital. Those cases that cannot be managed at the farm due to access to care, owner preference or severity can be managed medically or surgically depending on the reason for the abdominal pain.
Medically managed colic can range from a gastric impaction, an Ileus, or disruption in motility, to a displacement of the large colon into the nephrosplenic space. Treatment options include fluids, given in various ways, gastric decompression, specific medications such as phenylephrine, and pain management.

courses.title: Off to See the Wizard: A Journey to Reliable Itch Control
courses.description: Managing chronic canine itch can feel like being caught in a tornado--frustrated clients, flaring patients, and treatment plans that never quite stick. In this fun, practical, Wizard-of-Oz-themed webinar, Dr. Ali Diesel guides veterinarians along a clear 'yellow brick road' to more reliable long-term itch control. Participants will learn how IL-31 drives pruritus, why committing to a structured three-dose approach matters, how to manage common confounders, and how simple workflow strategies like forward booking support long term success. Through real-world cases and interactive discussion, attendees will leave with a confident, Monday-morning-ready framework for managing chronic itch in practice.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Complete Urinary System in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Urinary problems in dogs and cats, whether they are acute, chronic, or genetic, can diminish the health and happiness of patients and their owners. We understand that urinary surgery can be stressful. If urine trouble feels like you are in trouble inside your operating room, let this course get you back in the flow of things. That is why we designed this course, to help you develop & refine new surgical skills to ease your anxieties with future cases. You will perform nephrectomy, cystotomy, and canine & feline urethrostomies.
After this course, you will feel confident in performing surgery in the urinary system, including surgical planning, execution, and troubleshooting unexpected challenges.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Complete Urinary System in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Urinary problems in dogs and cats, whether they are acute, chronic, or genetic, can diminish the health and happiness of patients and their owners. We understand that urinary surgery can be stressful. If urine trouble feels like you are in trouble inside your operating room, let this course get you back in the flow of things. That is why we designed this course, to help you develop & refine new surgical skills to ease your anxieties with future cases. You will perform nephrectomy, cystotomy, and canine & feline urethrostomies.
After this course, you will feel confident in performing surgery in the urinary system, including surgical planning, execution, and troubleshooting unexpected challenges.

courses.title: CARES VetMed Fall 2026 Virtual Conference
courses.description: This live, virtual conference is provided by 12 individual Veterinary Technician Specialists in either Anesthesia & Analgesia or Emergency and Critical Care. Topics to be presented include: Heart Rate of the Anesthetized Patient: The Chronotropic Effects of Autonimic Tone and Anesthetic Agents, ECG in the ER: Rapid Rhythm Recognition for Critical Patients, Fresh Frozen Facts: Blood Transfusions in Veterinary Medicine, Triaging Trauma, Pheochromocytoma - What Do I Do?, Riding the Waves of Capnography, "The Inordinately Protected Airway" Brachycephalic Anesthesia, Sedation in the ER, When Sugar Hits the Fan: Recognizing HHS, Emergency and Critical Care of Exotic Companion Animals, Prioritize, Assess, Intervene: Understanding What it Means to Triage, and Cardiology for the Anesthetist.

courses.title: Senior Cats and Hidden Disease: The Impact of Early Detection
courses.description: Senior cats are often affected by hidden diseases that go undetected until advanced stages. This session will explore the findings of the Mortier study to highlight gaps in feline preventive care and examine key conditions that may be improved through early detection. Emphasis will be placed on the latest diagnostic data, and the role of regular wellness assessments in improving outcomes. Attendees will also gain strategies for practice- and client-level change management to better support feline health through proactive care.

courses.title: Frustrating Felines: The Inappetent Cat
courses.description: How do we get a sick cat to eat? Surely, this is one of the greatest challenges in feline practice. This session will explore the mechanisms that regulate appetite in healthy cats and emphasize the importance of identifying and addressing underlying causes of inappetence through appropriate diagnostic evaluation. A multimodal approach to managing inappetent cats will be discussed, including dietary and environmental modifications as well as pharmacologic options to support food intake.

courses.title: Feline Triaditis in Practice: Understanding the Tricky Triad
courses.description: This presentation explores feline triaditis, a complex syndrome involving concurrent disease of the gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, and hepatobiliary system. Current understanding of the etiopathogenesis will be reviewed, along with practical approaches to diagnosis and clinical evaluation. Attendees will also learn to develop effective treatment strategies while considering how therapies for one component of the triad may impact others.

courses.title: Heart Healthy Anesthesia for the Small Animal Cardiac Patient
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review the challenges of anesthetizing a small animal with cardiovascular conditions. This course will focus on alterations and adaptations to anesthetic techniques, plus feature practical strategies and protocols for a safe anesthetic episode. An overview will also be provided on the current literature regarding heart healthy anesthesia for cardiac patients.

courses.title: Feline Lower Urinary Track Disease-FLUTD
courses.description:
In this 2 hour long, in-person lecture based meeting, an in-depth review of
feline lower urinary tract disease along with practical case review will occur. Emphasis on the
pathophysiology of the main causes of FLUTD and recommended diagnostics will be discussed.
Both medical and interventional therapies will be discussed, with particular emphasis on feline
idiopathic cystitis

courses.title: Oral Tumors in Canines & Felines: Adjuvant Therapies and Surgical Resection
courses.description:
This course covers common neoplastic tumors that are encountered in veterinary medicine for dental and
oral cases. The oncology team will discuss detail information on behavior of the tumors, prognosis for
patients, as well as options of adjuvant therapy. The dental & oral surgery team will then discuss
different surgical resection options for these tumors and examples with case reports.

courses.title: (Live Webinar) The Secret of Pee: Myths and Realities of Urinary Health in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Urinalysis is a valuable but often misunderstood diagnostic tool in small animal practice. This session will explore the clinical significance of two commonly encountered urinary findings, crystalluria and bacteriuria, and help clinicians distinguish clinically relevant abnormalities from incidental findings. The webinar will discuss the different types and causes of crystalluria, when treatment is warranted, and practical approaches to management. It will also address the interpretation of bacteriuria in dogs and cats, including how to differentiate true urinary tract infection from contamination or subclinical bacteriuria, and when antimicrobial treatment is appropriate. Through a practical, case-based approach, participants will gain a clearer understanding of how to interpret these findings and make evidence-based treatment decisions in everyday clinical practice.

courses.title: Thoracic Pathology and Ultrasound. When is it cardiogenic vs. other? (LIVE/LECTURE)
courses.description: This 2 hour Live/On-site lecture program will present the necessary actions and clinical parameters needed to dial down whether clinical signs are derived from cardiac disease/thoracic disease, or other. In depth discussions of: normal respiratory parameters, normal echo parameters and radiographic findings, cardiac parameters of left sided heart failure, pleural effusion, cardiogenic parameters vs non-cardiogenic, thoracic lesion mapping for US-guided sampling, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema causes, thoracic causes of abdominal passive congestion, pulmonary & other thromboembolic presentations, thoracic cysts, lung consolidations, lung lobe torsions, US-guided thoracic sampling, thoracic hernia, thoracic arcinomatosis/lymphomatosis, valve disease classifications, cardio-thoracic case presentations.

courses.title: To Spay or Not to Spay, That is the Question
courses.description: Plan to discuss previously accepted recommendations for castrating dogs based on age and breed/size and how recommendations have changed based on new research over the last two decades. Within the presentation there are also correlations between animals and humans with similar disease processes. At the end of the presentation guidelines will be provided to help veterinarians educate their clients about this topic as well as the different surgical options available today.

courses.title: Winning with Senior Pets and Nutrition
courses.description:
Seminar diving into what data and clinical evidence tells us about aging pets, their diseases, and how we can elevate the standard of care for senior pets through nutrition and home delivery
Program Agenda:
Review of Senior pet demographic data and what is changing
Introduction of a Framework for better senior care appointments
Review of the prevalence and treatment data for 3 common diseases of aging- Renal disease, Arthritis, Cognitive decline
Show how more proactive recommendation of nutrition and more proactive use of vet sponsored home delivery can elevate care for senior pets
Learning Objectives:
The changing demographics for senior pets and the prevalence of disease
How to plan and execute more effective senior pet visits
How large the patient care opportunity is with arthritis, renal disease, and cognitive decline
See the impact that home delivery can have on patient compliance and business outcomes

courses.title: The Curvilinear Approach for Consistent Recognition of Sonographic Pathology (LIVE/Lecture)
courses.description: This program focuses on following the natural external and internal curvilinear patterns in all organ systems, when interrogating ultrasound or any imaging modality, allows a cognitive flow pattern that: recognizes deviation from normal, evaluates degree of deviation, identifies neoplastic criteria or NEEDLE CRITERIA, ensures methodical approach to organ interrogation minimizing risk of lesion omission, provides clinical-pathological insight to Normal vs. Age-related vs. Inflammatory vs. Neoplastic states.

courses.title: Ophthalmology Surgery - Common GP Techniques
courses.description: In this 3-hour, LIVE seminar, Shelby Reinstein, DVM, MS, DACVO will present numerous ophthalmic conditions which are typically managed surgically, including eyelid masses, prolapsed gland of the third eyelid, and glaucoma.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: 77th AALAS National Meeting
courses.description: Each fall since 1950, the American Association for Laboratory Animal Science has held its annual National Meeting. During the five days of the meeting, members and non-members come together to enjoy the workshops, lectures, poster sessions, and exhibits. The program is designed to have topics relevant to the entire membership. Exhibitors have an opportunity to interact with AALAS members from the academic community, research institutions, government organizations, and commercial companies. The AALAS National Meeting is the largest gathering in the world of professionals concerned with the production, care, and use of laboratory animals. The meeting will be held at the George R Brown Convention Center in Houston, Texas from October 25 - October 29, 2026.

courses.title: 2026 AETA - CETA/ACTE Joint Annual Pre-Conference Sessions
courses.description: The AETA & CETA/ACTE 2026 Joint Convention aims to present a unified voice for those involved in the embryo transfer industry in the promotion of mutual interests and objectives, provide continuing education and information regarding current issues in the embryo transfer industry for members. The American Embryo Transfer Association embraces its responsibility as the resource for embryo transfer in the United States. This authority is developed and supported through our commitment to excellence in several broad areas: education and standards of quality.

courses.title: Practical Pruritus: Making the Right Drug Choice for Dogs in Everyday Practice
courses.description: In this presentation, we will cover changing client perceptions and treatment options for managing allergic dogs. Current concepts surrounding diagnosis and treatment considerations will be covered. We will focus on currently available therapeutic options and where they fit with managing allergic dermatitis in dogs and how clinical presentation and client desires may affect treatment decisions.

courses.title: 2nd Annual Veterinary Burnout Preparedness Summit of the Year
courses.description:
The 2nd Annual Veterinary Burnout Preparedness Summit of the Year is a two-day continuing education program for veterinarians, veterinary technicians and technologists, practice managers, and veterinary support staff. The program addresses burnout preparedness, compassion fatigue, compassion satisfaction, moral distress, workplace communication, leadership, psychological safety, grief in end-of-life care, anxiety, and team wellbeing. Across eleven one-hour sessions delivered by veterinarians and allied subject matter experts, participants examine both individual and organizational contributors to burnout and learn practical, evidence-informed strategies for personal recovery and team-level culture change. Sessions cover foundational wellbeing terminology and burnout preparedness frameworks, compassion satisfaction as a protective factor, expectation-setting and its effect on retention and client compliance, career design and sustainability, physical durability and ergonomics in clinical work, anxiety recognition and management, sustainable organizational wellbeing systems, burnout as an occupational risk addressed through upstream organizational and regulatory strategy, learned helplessness and employee silence, and cumulative grief in end-of-life care. The program is delivered live and interactive online, with presenter interaction available throughout each session.
Attendees may select from the available sessions. CE credit is awarded on the basis of documented per-session attendance, and hours earned are reported per licensee.

courses.title: Infectious Disease Hot Topics and Vaccination Strategies
courses.description: This presentation goes over core and non-core vaccinations for dogs and cats per AAHA and AAFP vaccine guidelines, individual risk factors and helps determine clinic vaccination protocols. The course focuses on leptospirosis, Lyme disease, Feline Calicivirus, Feline Leukemia Virus and vaccine safety principles.

courses.title: SDAALAS Symposium 2026
courses.description:
During this full day symposium AALAS members and non-members come together to experience lectures and networking. The program is designed to have topics relevant to the entire membership
.Sick to Solved: Identifying and Addressing Morbidity & Mortality in Rodent Colonies, When Things Go Sideways: Lessons Learned for Vivarium Leaders, From Manager to Coach: An Introduction to Coaching Skills, Life Lessons from the Animals in Our Care, Think in Color: Using Six Thinking Hats to Drive Decisions, : Leadership Development Coaching: Building Influence, Engagement, and Impact,

courses.title: Regional Dental Anesthetic Blocks Lab
courses.description: This lab will introduce participants to the tips and techniques for applying regional dental anesthetic blocks for pain management during oral surgery cases. It will include hands on practice, as well as discussions on patient considerations and how to manage recovery.

courses.title: Fur Real Math: Calculations and Dilutions
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will provide practical guidance on common veterinary calculations and dilution techniques. This course will review how to accurately calculate dosages based on dose and weight conversions, prepare dilutions for medications, plus calculate appropriate additive volumes.

courses.title: BRisky Business: Brachycephalic Anesthesia
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review congenital issues common to brachycephalic breeds and focus on utilizing brachycephalic risk (BRisk) scoring to assess anesthetic dangers. In addition, this course will include methods to improve safety under anesthesia by implementing brachycephalic protocols plus review best practices to manage brachycephalic patients to optimize peri-operative safety.

courses.title: My Pet has Diabetes
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review the clinical signs leading to the diagnosis and management of diabetes mellitus in dogs and cats. This course will review the underlying etiologies, appropriate glucose monitoring techniques, and evidence-based treatment options.

courses.title: Sterile Processing
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary technicians will provide an overview of sterile processing practices focusing on the principles of sterility and infection prevention. This course will examine key sterilization methods, including the differences in types of sterilizers for clinical applications, plus review the use of chemical and biological indicators to ensure effective sterilization and patient safety.

courses.title: Understanding and Interacting with the Pain Pathway
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will introduce the pain pathway and its role in patient care. This course will review pain pathway components, how protocols interact with each stage, and the importance of multimodal analgesia in comprehensive pain management for veterinary patients.

courses.title: Veterinary Technician Certificate Course in Principle Techniques of Small Animal Anesthesia, Perioperative Analgesia & Critic
courses.description: This ESAVS Certificate Program for veterinary nurses and technicians covers advanced education in veterinary anesthesia, analgesia, and perioperative care as necessary to satisfy the growing expectations of both the veterinary community and animal owners. The course program is directed towards licensed animal health technicians/nurses with focused interest in small animal anesthesia, analgesia, and perioperative care and potentially the desire to pursue in the future a career as veterinary technician specialist (VTS) in anesthesia & analgesia. The 3-module course combines traditional methods of lecturing and laboratory/workshop teaching with the new technology of in-person online and on-demand e-learning. Furthermore, it offers the opportunity to obtain certification in basic and advanced techniques of cardiopulmonary resuscitation from the International Veterinary Emergency & Critical Care Society (Recover Initiative).

courses.title: Smooth Delivery: Anesthetic Management of Emergency Cesarian Sections
courses.description: Emergency cesarean sections present unique anesthetic challenges that require rapid assessment, efficient stabilization, and careful balancing of maternal and neonatal outcomes. This lecture is designed for veterinary technicians and will provide practical, evidence-based approaches to the anesthetic management of canine and feline emergency C-sections. Participants will also learn essential techniques for neonatal assessment, resuscitation, and immediate post-delivery care to improve neonatal survival. Emphasis will be placed on rapid decision-making, effective team communication, and practical skills that veterinary technicians can confidently apply in both emergency and general practice settings.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Concepts for the Rehabilitation Team
courses.description: This course gives veterinary technicians and assistants a fundamental understanding of functional canine anatomy, therapeutic modalities, therapeutic exercise, and massage. It also introduces the basics of neurological rehabilitation. Participants get hands-on experience with dogs on-site. Outcome measurement, documentation, patient education, and legal and ethical issues related to canine rehabilitation are also covered.

courses.title: Your Pet Got Into What?? Asking the Right Questions when Assessing an Animal Poisoning
courses.description: Wow, animals get into some crazy things! Did you know that not every animal should be treated simply based on the toxin? This lecture will discuss the basics of properly assessing a poisoned patient in order to understand both the risks presented by the toxin and the risks associated with specific species, breeds, and pre-existing conditions.

courses.title: Onsite Dental & Anesthesia Workshop for the Veterinary Technician
courses.description: Hands-on, limited-number attendees (16) offering the essentials of indispensable tricks to dental prophylactic care and dental radiographic skill sets. Anesthetic insights for drugs, physiologic responses and other factors affecting the patient safety. Overall approaches to taking away the fear and making dental procedures faster and easier.

courses.title: My Pet has Diabetes
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review the clinical signs leading to the diagnosis and management of diabetes mellitus in dogs and cats. This course will review the underlying etiologies, appropriate glucose monitoring techniques, and evidence-based treatment options.

courses.title: Fall VTNE Preparation Class (TECH120)
courses.description: This course is designed to provide a review of the veterinary technicians essential skills tasks and knowledge base as provided by the guidelines set forth by the AVMA CVTEA for approved veterinary technology programs. Active engagement in the entire course should help organize study time and allow for better competency and test-taking skills. The course library will contain a variety of handouts, study guides, charts, interactives, slide shows, and flashcards. Note: This class does not guarantee passage of the exam; we will approach as many topics as possible in an effort to help the student identify levels of competency as an aid to focus study efforts. In-depth and advanced topics will NOT be covered.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF EQUINE VETERINARY TECHNICIANS AND ASSISTANTS
courses.title: AAEVT Fall Anesthesia Society Event 2026
courses.description:
This equine anesthesia program is designed to expand the knowledge and practical skills of veterinary technicians at varying levels of experience who are involved in, or interested in, the anesthesia and perioperative care of equine patients. Through a combination of lectures and hands-on wet labs, participants will explore advanced concepts in cardiovascular and respiratory monitoring, arterial blood gas analysis, mechanical ventilation, pain physiology and multimodal analgesia, anesthetic emergency management, airway management, and vascular access.
Hosted at Rood & Riddle Equine Hospital in Lexington, Kentucky, the program provides participants the opportunity to learn and practice advanced anesthesia techniques within a leading equine referral hospital and clinical setting.
Lecture sessions will emphasize interpretation and clinical application of physiologic and monitoring data, recognition and management of anesthetic complications, and development of appropriate interventions to support patient safety throughout anesthesia and recovery. Hands-on wet labs will reinforce these concepts through practical experience with arterial catheterization, invasive blood pressure monitoring, arterial blood gas sampling, mechanical ventilation equipment and troubleshooting, advanced airway techniques, and alternative vascular access methods.
The combination of advanced didactic instruction and practical application will provide participants with knowledge and skills that can be incorporated into equine anesthesia protocols and patient management within their clinical practice.

courses.title: Build It or Buy It? The Realities of Veterinary Practice Ownership
courses.description:
For veterinarians dreaming of practice ownership, there are two primary paths: build a clinic from the ground up or purchase an existing practice. But which option is the better fit for your goals, finances, timeline, and vision for the future?
In this panel-style webinar, experienced veterinary industry professionals will explore the realities of both approaches--from start-up costs, financing, and time to profitability to existing goodwill, established client bases, operational risks, and long-term value. Attendees will gain practical insight to help determine which path makes the most sense for their own ownership journey.

courses.title: Paws & Unwind Wellness Retreats
courses.description: In this conference we aim to provide an opportunity for wellness and rejuvenation as well as continuing education for veterinary technicians. We will feature a variety of CE sessions focused on internal medicine, grief, burn out, compassion fatigue, and overall wellness.

courses.title: Beyond the Bleed: Understanding Small Animal Blood Products
courses.description: The participant can expect to learn common blood types of dogs/cats, common blood products used in veterinary medicine, the importance of crossmatching, how to correctly monitor patients for transfusion reactions, and the breakdown of each blood product any why they are used.
courses.location: Bay State Veterinary Emergency and Specialty Services

courses.title: Stall to Table, When It's Time to Cut
courses.description: This program will discuss 5 core areas of the surgical colic. These areas are most common types of surgical colics, why surgery is an option, indicators that warrant surgery while touching on Anesthesia and discussing the prognosis whether good or bad.

courses.title: Bite-Sized Wisdom: Dentistry for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: This workshop is for technicians and assistants only and will empower them by increasing their knowledge in many aspects of veterinary dentistry and implement a higher level of dental care in a general practice setting. Covered topics will include a compete professional dental cleaning using ultrasonic scalers and hand instruments, performing and correcting diagnostic radiographs, instrument care and sharpening, regional anesthesia, ergonomic in veterinary medicine, treatment plans and home care tips. All the discussed items will be implemented during the hands-on wet lab portion. This course is limited to 10 technicians or assistants with one instructor and one assistant.

courses.title: From Assessment to Action: Improving Pain Management in Veterinary Patients.
courses.description: Effective pain management is a critical component of high-quality veterinary patient care, and veterinary technicians play an essential role in recognizing, assessing, and advocating for appropriate analgesia. This lecture is designed to enhance technicians' understanding of pain physiology, improve confidence in pain assessment, and provide practical tools for supporting multimodal pain management in clinical practice.

courses.provider: CVETS - COLUMBIA VETERINARY EMERGENCY TRAUMA AND SPECIALTY
courses.title: Turning on the Lytes: Electrolyte Basics for Nurses
courses.description: This course will cover the basics of electrolytes, their normal values, and nursing considerations for patients with electrolyte derangements. The focus will be on the common electrolytes tested using point-of-care blood gas machines (EPOC, GEM 5000, Nova etc.) that nurses will often times be reviewing before the attending doctor. The goal is to help nurses be more confident interpreting basic electrolyte values to improve patient advocacy, as well as being able to anticipate potential treatment changes.

courses.title: Dental Radiograph Positioning Training
courses.description: Learn how to take efficient full mouth diagnostic dental radiographs with positioning techniques. Participants will get hands-on practice with feline/canine skulls or cadaver heads. There will be three workstations set up with Midmark x-ray generators and both Progeny and ScanX films available. A Zoom video lecture will be sent prior to the hands on training.

courses.title: BRisky Business: Brachycephalic Anesthesia
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review congenital issues common to brachycephalic breeds and focus on utilizing brachycephalic risk (BRisk) scoring to assess anesthetic dangers. In addition, this course will include methods to improve safety under anesthesia by implementing brachycephalic protocols plus review best practices to manage brachycephalic patients to optimize peri-operative safety.
